{#0.1.19} W ≥ (1 + log L)^pmax{(L/t)^κ, L/t₃}; the product, not the maximum, is needed at the sites near a face at distance t₃ ≫ t from a contact (#A.16–#A.17, (K5)–(K6)). On a block of side L, and on a coordinate plane of any dimension μ ≥ 1 through a block centre (the nearest lattice plane for even L), the average of W is ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^p: by Hölder with exponents q ∈ (1, 1/κ) and q/(q − 1), (L/t)^{qκ} has a bounded average since qκ < 1 and the faces of Λ meet such a plane transversally or at distance ≥ L/2 − ½, and (L/t₃)^{(1−κ)q/(q−1)} has a bounded average for q close to 1/κ, the exponent then being close to 1, while the contacts meet such a plane in codimension ≥ 2 or lie at distance ≥ L/2 − ½ from it, a contact of codimension k lying in k face hyperplanes {x_i = a_i}. Two cells of Λ^c that meet only in codimension ≥ 2 share no site, and no bond has one endpoint in each. So at a point z of the contact they are distinct local components unless a chain of cells of Λ^c sharing faces, with closures containing z, joins them, as the third cell of an L-shaped configuration does; t₃ counts only the contacts between distinct local components.

Then E(Q_r) ≤ C(d)(r/s₃)^αĒ for ρ₀ ≤ r ≤ s₃, with {#D.s₃} s₃ := min(L/8, t₃(x₀)/C(d)) and α = α(d) ∈ (0, 1), by four steps; the sources of steps (1) and (4) have exponents ≥ 2 > α and are absorbed by the iteration (#A.7). Since t₃ ≤ L, this is E(Q_r) ≤ C(d)(r/L)^α(L/t₃(x₀))^αĒ, and above s₃, E(Q_r) ≤ Ē for r ≤ L. Below s₃ every contact of codimension ≥ 2 between cells of Λ^c near Q_r(x₀) is locally joined, and the sites of Λ^c in Q_r(x₀) form one local component (#A.1), so no jump between components enters.

{#0.1.27} {#L6.KW} *The gradient part (KW).* Let {#D.λ} λ := λ_{x̄} on Q_{6L}(x̄), so u = v_{x̄} + w_{x̄} + ∂₁λ there. Every cube used below for the bound at x̄ lies in Q_{6L}(x̄) (#A.13). On the bonds of each component K_i of the mass graph, ∂₁λ = u − v_{x̄} − w_{x̄} carries the weight (L/t)^{1−α/2}(L/t₃)^{α/2}, times ρ₀ for t(b) < 4√dρ₀, which p absorbs (K2, #A.17). So the oscillation of λ on K′ ∩ Q_r(z), K′ the local component of z in Q_{2r}(z), the part of one K_i there by the join argument of (K3), is ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^p(r/L)^{α/2}(L/t₃(z))^{α/2}Lθ for ρ₀ ≤ r ≤ t₃(z)/C(d), and, on each of its cells meeting Q_r(z), ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^{p+1}Lθ for r ≤ L/16, through paths that enter the component, along which t grows (K3). The local maximum principle and Poincaré give osc_{𝒞_{L/256}(x₀)}λ ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^{p+1}Lθ for x₀ ∈ Q_{5L}(x̄), the components' offsets being compared at deep sites at distance ≥ L/32 − 1 from the strata (K4).

The interior gradient bound at the scale t then gives abs(∂₁λ(x)) ≤ C(d)W(x)θ (K6). Hence ‖u‖_W ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^pC_H^{reg}θ_B for the response u to data B, C_H^{reg} the bulk constant, ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^{p′} with constants of d only and no dependence on M or β₀ (in the N_b problem by the bounds on C̃ above and local regularity, in VAR's problem by #A.11 (K0)(f) with θ_B for θ; derived, not reviewed), and θ_B the supremum of the fine data and of the coarse block data (in the units of θ); in the N_b problem, with data g′ and response u = C̃g′, {#D.θ_B} θ_B := L² sup abs(g′), the units of the field, in which C̃ = O((1 + log L)²L²) (#0.1.17); the hole-filling's data sources are then of the bulk size.

{#0.1.28} A bound by ‖B‖_W alone is not claimed: W is ≈ L^κ at the unit bonds next to a face, and fine data of that size along a face have a harmonic extension that does not decay like (L/t)^κ. In the chain the data are of the admissible kind. The coarse data are block averages, ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^p‖c‖_W, since the block averages of W are ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^p (above). The chain of #0.1.40–#0.1.42 needs a bound on the fine data read in the weighted region of c, where abs(Im c) ≤ W‖Im c‖_W and W ≤ (1 + log L)^pL/ρ₀, t and t₃ being ≥ ρ₀. In case (i) below no such reading occurs, given #0.1.41 (derived, not reviewed): an old term's member equals c up to the response to the old term's own variables. In case (ii) the old term, of scale i < i_prev, reads c at the scale q ≤ i of its blocks. Its analyticity domain is defined by the radii of its own scale i (CRE p.259, (ii) below (2.27): U_i^c(X, α_{0,i}, α_{1,i}); for the terms of 𝐑^{(i)} by p.260 below (2.30), "Terms of this representation have the properties (i)–(iii) formulated above"), so by #0.1.42 the datum carries (1+β₀)²(i_prev − i)^{1/2}L^{−(i_prev−i)} times the bound at i_prev, relative to the thresholds of the scale i.
{#0.1.28-1} At the scales q at least that of the lattice on which c's W is measured, the datum is a value or an average of c on that lattice, ≤ W‖Im c‖_W at its bonds; so for i_prev − i ≥ 2 the factor ≤ 2(1+β₀)²L^{−2} pays W ≤ (1 + log L)^pL/ρ₀, leaving (1 + log L)^p/(Lρ₀) within the factor per level C(d)(1 + log L)^{p′}/L of #0.1.42 (derived, not reviewed). The readings in c's weighted region at blocks finer than c's occur only inside T_□: off T_□ run B's constraints are run A's composed with M (#4.445.1), and #4.445.2 adds the sources of the strip. Inside T_□, c is run B's composite c^B (#4.445.1) or a member with c^B's layers at complex data in the polydisc of #0.1.41, and its norm is ‖·‖_{W_ms} of #0.1.30 and #A.11.42, the supremum over the fine bonds b of abs(Im c)/W_ms with the field in the units of L^{j(b)}, j(b) the least j with χ_j(b) ≠ 0 (#A.11.49), with W_j measured from run B's layer Λ^B_j in its own units. Run B's layers are the shells Ω^B_j ∖ Ω^B_{j+1} between nested boxes (#4.445.1). Around a codimension-k edge of the inner box the 2^k − 1 cells of the shell are joined through face-sharing chains, and near an edge of the outer box the shell is one orthant, so no two distinct local components of a layer meet, t₃ = L in every W_j, and W_ms ≤ (1 + log L)^p(L/ρ₀)^κ on □₀, t being ≥ ρ₀.
{#0.1.28-2} Run B's scale indices count from its finest spacing ε/L, and scales of the two runs are compared as block sizes. So every value of Im c there at a bond of any W_j's lattice is ≤ (1 + log L)^p(L/ρ₀)^κ‖Im c‖_{W_ms} in the units of L^{j(b)}, and so in those of a reading scale ≤ j(b), which every reading there has: χ_j ≠ 0 at a bond of run B's layer Λ^B_n only for j ∈ {n − 1, n} (#A.11.49), so j(b) ≥ n − 1, and a reading at blocks finer than c's there has a scale ≤ n − 1, and every average of such values is ≤ C(d) times that, to first order in the complex part (#0.1.39). At i = i_prev − 1 the gain (9/8)(1+β₀)²L^{−1} then leaves the factor per level C(d)(1 + log L)^{p′}L^{−μ}ρ₀^{−κ} of #0.1.42, κ = 1 − μ, and for i_prev − i ≥ 2 the gain 2(1+β₀)²L^{−2} leaves less (derived, not reviewed). The weight L/t₃ is not removable by a gauge: the gauges of N_b vanish on Λ^c, and in Bałaban's problem those of N_𝔅 and N(Q′) vanish on Λ₀, so the jump is invariant under them, and in Bałaban's problem it is fixed by the coarse constraints at the size of the coarse datum, which on the contact bond is L times the datum in the units used here.

{#0.1.29} {#L6.balaban} *Bałaban's problem.* For VAR's problem (heading) the residual group is N_𝔅, and the components are those of the graph of the data bonds of Λ₀. t₃ is, as in the N_b problem, the distance to the contacts of codimension ≥ 2 between distinct local components (#A.10); the averages of W over blocks and over the coordinate planes through block centres remain ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^p, by the Hölder bound above, since the exponent of L/t₃ there is close to 1 < 2, and so the weighted kernel sums are ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^p times the unweighted ones. A_N (heading) has ∂*A_N orthogonal to N(Q′), whose orthogonal complement is ran Q′*, the block-constant fields transported by R(U(Γ_{y,x})) (PBG (3.19)). So ∂*A_N is constant on each block of Λ, the layer sites included. So in (KW) λ solves Δλ = −σ at every site of Λ in Q_{6L}(x̄), the boundary is Λ₀, where λ = c_i up to the increments B − v_{x̄} − w_{x̄} on the data bonds, and the maximum principle needs no condition at the layer sites. The hole-filling is run for the residual a = A_N − E of #A.11 (K0)(b), not for A_N, whose energy near a face of Λ₀ is of order L^{d−1}θ_B² per block. a vanishes on the data bonds, so the mass term of E(Q_r) (#0.1.20) is absent and the fields w of #0.1.21 are a − ∂φ with φ constant on the components of the data graph, where a − ∂φ = 0.

{#0.1.30} Its linear term ℓ_E, tested with η²w, is bounded by the dual-norm sources S of (K0)(b): it vanishes where χ_dχ_f = 1, d*F_f being 0 on the free bonds of supp χ_f ((K0)(b)), and on Q_r(x) it is ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)³S(Q_r(x))(E(Q_{C(d)r}(x)) + r^{−2}‖w‖²_{Q_{C(d)r}(x)})^{1/2}, T̂_f reading dT within C(d)m_f ≤ C(d)r. With S(Q_r)² ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)r^{d−2}θ_B² (K0)(b) and Ē of the bulk size L^{d−2}θ², this is a source of exponent d − 2 > α. The region at distance L/32 to L/16 from Λ₀, where ∇χ_d ≠ 0, adds a source of exponent d. The coarse constraints are hard: Caccioppoli's test fields are corrected by the bumps β_c of #0.1.33.1, at a source cost with exponent d + 2 (#A.8). The rest of (KW) is unchanged, with the weighted L² decay of VAR's problem derived in #A.11 (K0), so ‖A_N‖_W obeys the same bound.
{#0.1.30-1} At the interfaces Λ_j/Λ_{j+1} with j ≥ 1 the same holds in the units of L^j for the representative {#D.A_♮} A_♮ := A_N + ∂ω_♮ of #A.11 (K0)(g)(6), with ω_♮ ∈ N(Q′), abs(Im ηω_♮) ≤ C(L, M)ε₁ pointwise, and A_♮ = A_N at the points of R₀ outside the blocks of Λ₁ that meet R₁ (#A.11.50); for the complex part of the data (#0.1.11) the chain uses A_♮ in place of A_N and ω − ω_♮ in place of ω, at group level through the representative u_R^{g_♮^{−1}} of #A.9.6 with ‖Ad(g_♮)‖ ≤ 1 + C(L, M)ε₁, and its norm is ‖·‖_{W_ms} with {#D.W_ms} W_ms := max_jW_j of (K0)(g)(5), which has the properties of W used here. The random walk (2.141), Proposition 2.6, and PBG Corollary 3.6 are used only for B₀, with Bałaban's constants O(1)(d, L). B₀ is also the constant of VAR's bounds abs(HB) ≤ B₀(L^jη)^{−1}abs(B) and abs(∇HB) ≤ B₀(L^jη)^{−2}abs(B) on Ω_j (p.285 l.27), and it enters VAR only through the radii, the smallness conditions, B₃, B₅, and the correction of (187), as listed at #0.1.14, all fixed before ε₁ or multiplied by it. For the scalar local propagators G′_□ of Δ′_a, the blocks of 𝔅 partition the region, and the per-block Poincaré bound, ‖λ‖²_B ≤ C(d)(S²‖∂λ‖²_B + S^dabs(Q′λ)²), gives the gap c(d)min(1, a)S^{−2} in each block's units with no interface term, since the coefficients of PBG (3.24) (p.394), a₁ = a₀ = a and a_{j+1} = aa_j/(aL^{−2} + a_j), obey a/2 ≤ a_j ≤ a for L ≥ 2 by induction.
{#0.1.30-2} At a background U, λ is read in the frame of a coordinate tree of each block, in which U = 1 on the tree. By VAR (2) (p.278), abs(U(∂p) − 1) < ε₀L^{−2j} on the plaquettes of Ω_j, so the loop of a bond of a block of side S = L^j with its tree paths, which bounds ≤ C(d)S plaquettes, has holonomy defect ≤ C(d)ε₀S^{−1}, and the covariant difference differs from ∂λ by ≤ C(d)ε₀S^{−1}abs(λ) on each bond. The contours of Bałaban's average against the tree paths bound ≤ C(d)S² plaquettes, with defect ≤ C(d)ε₀, so the covariant mean differs from Q′λ by ≤ C(d)ε₀S^{−d/2}‖λ‖_B. For ε₀ ≤ c(d) both are absorbed, and the covariant per-block Poincaré bound and the gap hold with other constants of d only (derived, not reviewed).

{#0.1.31} *The two-layer gap.* PRT2 bounds the form (2.122) from below in the axial gauge within blocks ((2.121)) by (2.123) (p.244), with the constant dL^d, for the bonds inside the blocks, and through the bonds of the hyperplane Δ′ = {x_μ = y_μ + L − 1} of each block for the bonds between blocks ((2.125)–(2.127), PRT2 p.245, figure), which gives (1/12d²)L^{−d−1} in (2.128) (p.245). The bound used instead is a gap on the gauge orbit, in the setting of each of its uses: #0.1.16 (Λ^c and Λ of PRT2 Lemma 2.4, the form (2.122)), #A.11 (K0)(d) (the problem 𝒫₁ of (c), Λ₀ and Ω₁), and (K0)(g)(1)–(2) (the two-layer problem for V on the scale-j lattice, Ω_{j+1}^c and Ω_{j+1}). In units of the fine scale, there is a fine region F, with D = 0 on the bonds with both endpoints in F (the data bonds), and a coarse region C := F^c, a finite union of blocks of side L of one grid of which F is also a union, with QD(c) = 0 on every bond c of the grid with an endpoint in C. Here Q is the average over x ∈ B(c₋) of the sums of D along the lines from x to x + Le_μ, at the flat base (CMP98 (124)–(125), p.36), so Q∂λ(c) = Q′λ(B(c₊)) − Q′λ(B(c₋)) with Q′ the block mean, and QD(c) = 0 holds also on the bonds of the grid between two blocks of F, whose lines run on data bonds. PRT2's Q₁ is L^{−1}Q ((2.125), p.245; (2.103), p.241), and CMP98 (125) carries the same L^{−(d+1)}, so CMP98's Q₀ is PRT2's Q₁.
{#0.1.31-1} The coarse norm carries L^d, so L^{−2}‖(Q₁B)↾_{Λ′}‖² = L^{d−4}Σ_cabs(QB(c))². The unit bonds from F into C, the crossing bonds, are free in every use: in #0.1.16 they are bonds of Λ, the set of bonds with at least one endpoint in Λ, on which B is free (PRT2 Lemma 2.4, p.245), and in (d) and (g) VAR does not constrain them (REG p.81). No constraint of a finer scale on bonds into a coarser region enters. By (2.3), for j ≥ 1 the scale-j bonds of Λ_j are those with an endpoint in Ω_j^{(j)} and none in Ω_{j+1}^{(j)}, and the problems of (c) and (g)(1) fix the data of the coarser layers by constraints of the one coarse scale.

{#0.1.32} The claim (derived, not reviewed). With ℓ := L on the bonds with an endpoint in C and ℓ := 1 on the others, there is λ in the group {#D.N_F} N_F := {λ : λ = 0 on F, Q′λ = 0 at every block of C} such that ‖ℓ^{−1}(D − ∂λ)‖ ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)‖dD‖. By Q∂λ = Q′λ(B(c₊)) − Q′λ(B(c₋)), N_F keeps the zeros and the constraints of D. The construction (#0.1.34–#0.1.37.1) is run for a D vanishing also on a set 𝒳 of crossing bonds, one into each site of C joined to F. Every class of D modulo ∂N_F contains such a D, D − ∂λ₀ with λ₀ ∈ N_F (#A.11.9, with N(Q′) := N_F), and the λ for D is λ₀ plus that for D − ∂λ₀, since dD is unchanged. For #0.1.16, F := Λ^c, C := Λ, and N_F = N_b. B ∈ 𝒮 is the least element of B + ∂N_b in ℓ², and ∂N_b vanishes on the bonds with both endpoints in Λ^c, so with the lift below and the claim for D := B − Ã, ‖B↾_{Λ^c}‖² + L^{−2}‖B↾_Λ‖² ≤ ‖B↾_{Λ^c}‖² + L^{−2}‖(B − ∂λ)↾_Λ‖² ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)²F(B), with B↾_Λ the restriction to the bonds with an endpoint in Λ, the crossing bonds included, on which ℓ = L, since (B − ∂λ)↾_Λ = Ã↾_Λ + (D − ∂λ)↾_Λ.

{#0.1.33} The lift for (2.122). For a field B let {#D.Ã} Ã := B on the bonds with both endpoints in Λ^c plus Σ_cr(c)β_c over the bonds c of the grid with an endpoint in Λ, with {#D.r(c)} r(c) := QB(c) − Q(1_{Λ^c}B)(c), 1_{Λ^c} the indicator of the bonds with both endpoints in Λ^c, and β_c the bump of #0.1.33.1 at the scale 1 in the block of c in Λ (B(c₋) if both are). Then Qβ_c = δ_c on these bonds, abs(β_c) ≤ C(d)/L, abs(dβ_c) ≤ C(d)/L², and β_c is supported at distance ≥ L/8 from the faces of its block, off the bonds of Λ^c and the crossing bonds. So QÃ = QB on these bonds and Ã = B on the bonds of Λ^c, and {#D.D} D := B − Ã vanishes on the bonds of Λ^c, with QD = 0, and D = B on the crossing bonds. Each bond lies on at most L of the lines of Q, so by Cauchy–Schwarz abs(Qg(c))² ≤ L^{2−d}‖g‖²_{Ω_c}, Ω_c := B(c₋) ∪ B(c₊), and L^{d−4}abs(r(c))² ≤ 2L^{d−4}abs(QB(c))² + 2L^{−2}‖B↾_{Λ^c}‖²_{Ω_c}. A block carries the bumps of at most 2d bonds, with ‖β_c‖² ≤ C(d)L^{d−2} and ‖dβ_c‖² ≤ C(d)L^{d−4}, so ‖dÃ‖² + L^{−2}‖Ã↾_Λ‖² ≤ C(d)(‖B↾_{Λ^c}‖² + L^{d−4}Σ_cabs(QB(c))²) ≤ C(d)F(B). Then ‖dD‖² ≤ 2γ₀^{−1}F(B) + 2‖dÃ‖² ≤ C(d)F(B), γ₀ of (2.118) depending on d only (PRT1 p.29).

{#0.1.33.1} The bumps (derived, not reviewed). In units η = 1, let c be a bond of direction μ and scale j with a block in the layer Λ_j, {#D.S.2} S := L^j, and Q_j the average over x ∈ B(c₋) of the line integrals of length S, as in #A.8, so that Q_j maps a constant field a to Sa (PBG's Q_j is S^{−1} times this). Let B be the block of c in Λ_j (B(c₋) if both are). At the flat base the one-step contours of a bond stay in its two blocks, and so do those of the composites (CMP98 (124), p.36; PBG (3.15), p.393). So among the scale-j constraints, a field on the direction-μ bonds of B is read only by c and by the direction-μ bond c* of the scale j whose other block is B (the previous bond for B = B(c₋), the next for B = B(c₊)). For B = B(c₋), a scale-(j−1) bond e at the position k(e) ∈ {1, …, L} along μ in B lies on k(e) of the one-step lines of c and on L − k(e) of those of c*, each of weight L^{−d}; a fine bond z enters Q_{j−1} only through the scale-(j−1) bonds e whose two blocks contain it, with k(e) − k(z) ∈ {−1, 0}, k(z) the position of z's scale-(j−1) block. So the weights w_c and w_{c*} of z obey (k(z) − 1)w_{c*}(z) ≤ (L − k(z) + 1)w_c(z) and (L − k(z))w_c(z) ≤ k(z)w_{c*}(z), and by induction on j their sum is S^{1−d} on every direction-μ bond (for j = 1, k + (L − k) = L lines of weight L^{−d}); for B = B(c₊) the roles of k and L − k are exchanged.
{#0.1.33.1-1} Let ψ₁ and ψ₂ be sampled smooth functions on the sites of B, 0 ≤ ψ_i ≤ 1, abs(∇ψ_i) ≤ C(d)/S, at distance ≥ S/8 from the transverse faces, with ψ₁ supported at k ∈ [3L/4, 7L/8] and ψ₂ at k ∈ [L/8, L/4], each equal to 1 on ≥ c(d)S^d sites. For L ≥ 16, w_c ≥ 2w_{c*} on supp ψ₁ and w_{c*} ≥ 2w_c on supp ψ₂. With a_i := Q_j(ψ_ie_μ)(c) and b_i := Q_j(ψ_ie_μ)(c*), a₁ ≥ 2b₁ ≥ 0, b₂ ≥ 2a₂ ≥ 0, and a₁, b₂ ≥ c(d)S, so a₁b₂ − a₂b₁ ≥ (3/4)a₁b₂. Let {#D.β_c} β_c := (x₁ψ₁ + x₂ψ₂)e_μ with a₁x₁ + a₂x₂ = 1 and b₁x₁ + b₂x₂ = 0; then abs(x_i) ≤ C(d)/S. So Q_jβ_c = δ_c on the scale-j bonds, abs(β_c) ≤ C(d)/S, abs(∂β_c) ≤ C(d)/S², ‖∂β_c‖² ≤ C(d)S^{d−4}, and β_c is supported in B at distance ≥ S/8 from its faces: off the data bonds, off the scale-(j − 1) blocks of B that touch its faces, and off every other layer. In PBG's normalisation, Q_jβ_c = S^{−1}δ_c, so the bump with Q_j = δ_c is Sβ_c, of size C(d) and ‖∇(Sβ_c)‖² ≤ C(d)S^{d−2}. On Λ₀, whose blocks are single sites, β_c is the unit field on c.

{#0.1.34} Block potentials. For a block B of the grid let 𝐁_B be the ball of radius L/8 about its centre, and for x in the cube 5B of side 5L about B let {#D.φ_B} φ_B(x) := the average over a ∈ 𝐁_B of the sums of D along the lattice paths within distance 1 of the segment from a to x, averaged as for G^Y in #A.11.13. As there, (D − ∂φ_B)(b) on a bond b = (x, x + e_μ) of 3B is an average of sums of dD over strips of width ≤ C(d) along the segments. A plaquette p at distance t from x lies in them for a fraction ≤ C(d)max(t, 1)^{1−d} of the a, the segments having length ≤ C(d)L and 𝐁_B the radius L/8. So abs((D − ∂φ_B)(b)) ≤ C(d)Σ_{p⊂5B}abs(dD(p))max(abs(p − x), 1)^{1−d}, and since Σ_{p⊂5B}max(abs(p − x), 1)^{1−d} ≤ C(d)L, Schur's test gives ‖D − ∂φ_B‖_{3B} ≤ C(d)L‖dD‖_{5B}. Let {#D.φ̂_B} φ̂_B := φ_B − mean_Bφ_B.

{#0.1.35} The relative constants. For the bond c of the grid from B to B′ = B + Le_μ, Q∂φ_{B′}(c) = mean_{B′}φ_{B′} − mean_Bφ_{B′} and QD(c) = 0. So abs(mean_Bφ̂_{B′}) = abs(Q(D − ∂φ_{B′})(c)) ≤ L^{1−d/2}‖D − ∂φ_{B′}‖_{Ω_c} ≤ C(d)L^{2−d/2}‖dD‖_{5B′}. For B′ = B + Lv, v ∈ {−1, 0, 1}^d, a chain of at most d such steps through blocks in 3B′ gives the same bound with another C(d). On the box P := 3B ∩ 3B′, which contains B and B′, g := φ̂_B − φ̂_{B′} has ‖∂g‖_P ≤ C(d)L‖dD‖_{5B∪5B′}, and mean_Bg = −mean_Bφ̂_{B′}, so Poincaré on P gives ‖g‖_P ≤ C(d)L²‖dD‖_{7B}. Each pair of neighbouring blocks is compared through its own constraints, so nothing accumulates along chains of blocks.

{#0.1.36} The interior. Let ψ_B be a sampled smooth partition of unity over the blocks, ψ_B supported in 2B with abs(∇ψ_B) ≤ C(d)/L, and {#D.Ψ_int} Ψ_int := Σ_Bψ_Bφ̂_B, a finite sum, since φ_B = 0 for the blocks with D = 0 on 5B. On a bond b = (x, x + e_μ) with x in the block B₀, the product rule ∂(ψφ)(b) = ψ(x + e_μ)∂φ(b) + φ(x)∂ψ(b) and Σ_B∂ψ_B = 0 give (D − ∂Ψ_int)(b) = Σ_Bψ_B(x + e_μ)(D − ∂φ_B)(b) − Σ_B(φ̂_B − φ̂_{B₀})(x)∂ψ_B(b), the blocks B in the sums lying in 3B₀. So ‖D − ∂Ψ_int‖_{B₀} ≤ C(d)L‖dD‖_{9B₀}, and ‖D − ∂Ψ_int‖ ≤ C(d)L‖dD‖. Since mean_{B₀}Ψ_int = Σ_Bmean_{B₀}(ψ_B(φ̂_B − φ̂_{B₀})), abs(mean_{B₀}Ψ_int) ≤ C(d)L^{2−d/2}‖dD‖_{9B₀}. On a block Y of F, D = 0 on the bonds with both endpoints in Y, so ‖∂Ψ_int‖_Y ≤ C(d)L‖dD‖_{9Y}, and Poincaré on Y gives ‖Ψ_int‖_Y ≤ C(d)L²‖dD‖_{9Y}. No logarithm enters. Ψ_int does not vanish on F, and cutting it off at F would cost the trace of D − ∂Ψ_int on the faces of F, a factor L more, so near F the potential anchored at F is used.

{#0.1.37} Near F. On the sites of C within L/8 of F, the anchored potential Ψ of #A.11.13–#A.11.14, with Λ₀ := F, its blocks Y of side L, and the sites of C as the free sites, and with Ψ := 0 on F, gives D = ∂Ψ + R + e on the bonds of C within L/32 of F, where χ_d = 1, and D − ∂Ψ = e on the crossing bonds. Here ‖m^{−1}R‖² ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)‖dD‖² and ‖ℓ^{−1}e‖² ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)²‖dD‖² (#A.11.13–#A.11.16). These use only that D vanishes on the data bonds and on a set 𝒳 of crossing bonds, one into each site of C joined to F, and that QD = 0. Every class of D modulo ∂N_F contains such a D (#0.1.32, #A.11.9; N_F is N(Q′) in (d)). Let L ≥ 128, χ := 1 on F and on the sites of C within L/128 of F, χ := 0 beyond L/64, abs(∇χ) ≤ C(d)/L, and {#D.h} h := Ψ_int − Ψ on F and on the sites of C within L/32 of F. For a site x of C within L/64 of F, let Y be a block of F nearest to x, and 𝐁 the ball of radius L/32 about the point of Y nearest to x moved by L/8 towards the centre of Y, which lies in Y for d ≤ 4. dist(·, Y) is convex, so the segments from 𝐁 to x stay within L/64 of Y, and the lattice paths along them run on bonds of F and of C within L/32 of F. h(x) is the average over a ∈ 𝐁 of h(a) = Ψ_int(a) plus the sums of ∂h along these paths, where ∂h = e + R − (D − ∂Ψ_int) on the bonds of C, e − (D − ∂Ψ_int) on the crossing bonds, and −(D − ∂Ψ_int) on the data bonds. The averaged paths give a kernel ≤ C(d)max(abs(x − b), 1)^{1−d}, ‖e‖ + ‖R‖ ≤ C(d)L(1 + log L)‖dD‖ there, and abs(avg_𝐁Ψ_int) ≤ C(d)L^{−d/2}‖Ψ_int‖_Y. So, by #0.1.36 and bounded overlap, ‖h‖ ≤ C(d)L²(1 + log L)‖dD‖ over the sites of C within L/64 of F.

{#0.1.37.1} The conclusion. Let {#D.λ₁} λ₁ := Ψ_int − χh, which is Ψ where χ = 1, in particular 0 on F. On a bond b = (b₋, b₊), D − ∂λ₁ = (1 − χ(b₊))(D − ∂Ψ_int)(b) + χ(b₊)(D − ∂Ψ)(b) + h(b₋)∂χ(b), with D − ∂Ψ = e + R where χ(b₊) ≠ 0. Against ℓ = L on the bonds with an endpoint in C, the three terms give ‖ℓ^{−1}(D − ∂λ₁)‖ ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)‖dD‖, and on the data bonds D = ∂λ₁ = 0. Last, the block means. With ψ̃_B a sampled smooth bump of mean 1 in the sites of B at distance ≥ L/4 from its faces, abs(∇ψ̃_B) ≤ C(d)/L, put λ := λ₁ − Σ_Bmean_B(λ₁)ψ̃_B over the blocks B of C. By #0.1.36 and the bound on h, Σ_BL^{d−2}abs(mean_Bλ₁)² ≤ C(d)L²(1 + log L)²‖dD‖², and ‖∂ψ̃_B‖² ≤ C(d)L^{d−2}, so the bumps cost ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)‖dD‖ in ‖ℓ^{−1}·‖. They avoid F and the sites where χ ≠ 0. So λ = 0 on F, Q′λ = 0 at every block of C, and ‖ℓ^{−1}(D − ∂λ)‖ ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)‖dD‖. The logarithm comes only from e and R near F.

{#0.1.38} For the premise, Bałaban's (1.61) at s = 1, U^0_k = U(𝐁″_k(Y_1), M^·(U^0_k)) (LFR II p.373; #4.516), is an identity of this kind for one member. On Y_1^0 the determining sets 𝐁″_k(Y_1) and 𝐁″_k coincide. On the boundary layer Y_1 ∖ Y_1^0, at most 2M_1 wide, Bałaban keeps the gauge u_k^0, an analytic function of 𝐇″_k given by (106) of his [12] (p.373 l.26–30). That u is the normalising transformation u(y) = (block average of R₀U₁)^{−1} of [12] (CMP 98, p.31, l.13–18 of the transcription), and (106) writes u(x) as a product over the scales j < k of transports by U₀ and of the deviations of R̄^j_0Ū̄^j_1 from its block average along the contours Γ_{x_{j+1},x_j}.

{#0.1.39} These contours lie in the scale-k block of x, with total length ≤ 2dL^kη. U₀ is "a fixed configuration" (CMP98 p.29 l.2), in LFR II's use the background U₁ of (1.53), which is complex at the complex members; the transports then add a product of their complex part with the real deviations, of order C(L, M)ε₁θ, which is part of the background term. The data change only through u at the block points, (Ū^u)_b = u(b₋)Ū_bu^{−1}(b₊) (REG (1.14), p.78), and there u(y) = (\overline{R_{0,y}U_1}^{(k)})^{−1} (CMP98 (87), p.31), built by (82)–(85) (pp.30–31) as nested averages, with the weights L^{−d} of (78), over x_j ∈ B(x_{j+1}) of the transports along the scale-j contours Γ_{x_{j+1},x_j}, which carry the scale-j averages Ũ₁^j of U₁ (Ũ₁^0 = U₁ on Γ_{x₁,x}), where U₁ = exp iηA₁. So the complex part of u at y is, to first order, a sum over j < k of these averages of the integrals of the scale-j averages of Im A₁ along Γ_{x_{j+1},x_j}, and an average of a field f is at most ‖f‖_W times the same average of W. A single contour of the scale k − 1 can run inside a face of Λ, where W is ≈ (1 + log L)^pL^κ, so the bound is taken for the average (derived, not reviewed). A bond of the coordinate segment of Γ_{y,x} in the direction μ has the coordinates of x in the directions before μ and those of y after μ, and it is crossed by at most L^{d−μ+1} of the contours. So the average over x of ∫_{Γ_{y,x}}W is at most Σ_μ L times the average of W over the μ-dimensional coordinate plane through y, a point of 𝔅_k and so a block centre (VAR (181), p.307), which is ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^p (the Hölder bound at the definition of W), in units of the scale k − 1.

{#0.1.40} That is, A₁ and its problem are read on the lattice of the scale k − 1, whose unit bonds have length L^{k−1}η, and W, t, and t₃ are measured in those bonds. The contours of the scales j < k − 1 have total length ≤ 2dL^{k−1}η, at most 2d units of the scale k − 1, on which W ≤ (1 + log L)^pL. So the complex part of u at the block points is bounded by C(d)(1 + log L)^pL^kη‖Im A₁‖_W. In the units of a scale-k datum (L^kη times the field) this is C(d) times the complex part of A₁ on the block, and A₁ is the response to 𝐇″_k, bounded by C_H + δ_U ≤ 2C_H at a real base (#A.11.1.6). The transformation u acts on the data of the layer from one side only at the boundary of Y_1^0, so the complex part of the data there is at most (1 + 2C(d)C_H) times that of the variables, C(d) being doubled to cover C_H + δ_U ≤ 2C_H. This multiplies the factor per level below by 1 + 2C(d)C_H, which is a power of 1 + log L (derived, not reviewed). At a general member c the premise holds in the following form (derived, not reviewed). An old term 𝐑^{(i)} reads c through its scale-i averages M^{(i)}(c) on its domain, plus its own large-field and margin variables (CRE (3.26)). Its blocks have scales ≤ i: the step at which a region froze if that step is ≤ i, and i otherwise. c's blocks have scales ≥ the step at which a region froze in c's history, or k. (i) If the old term's history is a prefix of c's, then in every region the old blocks refine c's. The regions frozen at j ≤ i carry the same blocks, and elsewhere the old scale is i ≤ c's. The averages compose (PBG (3.15), (3.19)), so c is admissible.

{#0.1.41} At real data it is minimal by the argument of *U_{k,Z} as the background.* (#3.85), through the uniqueness of the minimal orbit (CRE p.256 l.43–53, (2.12)). The old problem's data outside its blocks are c's own values: the localised determining set has the outermost layer Ω₀ ∖ Ω₁ of order-0 averages, which are the bonds themselves (CRE p.256 l.57–63, (2.14) p.257), and M^·(c, b) = c(b) at the unit bonds (RG I (1.15), Ū⁰ = U). At complex data the identity extends by analytic continuation. Let D range over the polydisc of c's data, and {#D.F(D)} F(D) := 𝓗_old(M_old(𝓗_new(D))) − 𝓗_new(D), defined since the complex parts stay within the radius ε₂ by the bounds of this paragraph. F is analytic on the polydisc, which is convex, and F vanishes at its real points, an open subset of the real subspace. So F ≡ 0, and the member equals c up to the response to the old term's own variables (derived, not reviewed).

{#0.1.42} (ii) If c is a comparison configuration of another history (#4.245), c may carry blocks of a scale j < i where the old history has the scale i. There the old constraints are coarser than c's, and the member is the minimiser at c's scale-i averages: a response to data at the scale i. The averages' complex parts are at most L^iη·sup abs(Im c) in field units, so the member's complex field is at most C_H sup abs(Im c). The gain does not use c's blocks; the readings of c's fine data in its weighted region are bounded in #0.1.28. sup abs(Im c) is bounded relative to the thresholds of the scale i_prev of c's own data: the step k for the literal points, whose complex variables are of the scales ≥ k (the Cauchy note's #C5.27), and the reading scale of the previous member otherwise. The old term reads at a scale i < i_prev, since its generation precedes that of the term or step at which c is read. This is strict by (α): the recent terms, k₁ < j ≤ k, including 𝐑^{(k)}, are read only at the callers' points and never inside the quotients at members, so at every level the reading generation is ≤ k₁ < k. Relative to the thresholds of the scale i this is (1+β₀)²(i_prev − i)^{1/2}L^{−(i_prev−i)} ≤ (9/8)(1+β₀)²L^{−1} times the bound at i_prev, by the Cauchy note's #C5.27. ## 1. The Structure of a Young History (Derived) {#S1}

{#1.1} Let X be an alive component of a young matched pair, born at the scale j₀ > k − ⌊k/2⌋, so that Ω_i = T for i < j₀ (Cauchy note §6.2).

- {#1.2} *The integration variables.* By CRE (2.20)–(2.21) (p.258 l.14–31), the operation 𝐓^{(j)} integrates V_j on Ω^c_{j+1} ∩ X with the constraint δ(V̄_jV^{−1}_{j+1}). On the part of X that is large-field from the scale j₀ on, the variables V_{j₀}, …, V_{k−1} are fixed by the constraints as iterated block averages of V_{j₀−1}. So the integration there is over V_{j₀−1}, with the Haar measure and the constraints, and over the fluctuation variables A_j on Z_{j+1} ∩ Ω_{j+1} ∩ X.
- {#1.3} *The regularity of the data.* The point lies in Ω_{j₀−1} ∖ Ω_{j₀}, so the determining set carries the layer Λ_{j₀−1} there, with data V_{j₀−1}. VAR's hypothesis (7) (p.278 l.35–45) is one bound ε₁ on the data plaquettes of all layers, the mixed plaquettes at a layer's boundary included. It holds on the support of the term with {#D.ε₁} ε₁ := C max_j(ε_j + ϑ_j), from the seven groups of LFR I p.178, as follows.
  - {#1.4} The cubes of (1.3) at the scale j, □ ⊂ (Ω_j^{∼4} ∖ Ω_{j+1}^∼) ∩ Z (LFR I p.178 l.16–19), bound the plaquettes of U_{j,□}(V_j) by ε_j(L^{k−j}η)². With Ω_{j₀−1} = T they cover the large-field region of the scale j₀ outside the collar Ω_{j₀}^∼ ∖ Ω_{j₀} (Ω^∼ is the enlargement, CRE p.250 l.26). The data of U_{j,□} are V_j, so CMP 98 Proposition 2 (p.26, (54)), which needs only the local plaquette bound (52), gives |V_j(∂p′) − 1| < 2ε_j there. This is the remark of VAR p.278 l.46. The group (1.4) gives the same at the scale j + 1.
  - {#1.5} In the collars, (1.7) and (1.8) put V_j, and the lifted fluctuation field, within 2ϑ_j of the reference configuration V^{(j)}_{□′}. This is the scale-j average of a minimiser corrected by exp i𝐇^{(j)}_{□′} (LFR I p.185 l.29), so its plaquettes are bounded by the item above, and those of V_j by that bound plus Cϑ_j.
  - {#1.6} By CRE (2.4) and (2.6) and ϑ_j = g_j(A₁/A₀)p₀(g_j) (CRE p.265 l.39), ε₁ ≤ Cḡp₀(ḡ) ≤ a₁ for ḡ small, with ε₁ independent of k, K, and ε.
- {#1.7} *The configurations.* The fine configuration of the term is a minimiser with these data: U_k(V) for the action (CRE p.258 l.44–47), and U″_k = U_{𝐁″_k}(·) for the R-operation (LFR II (1.50), p.370 l.4). VAR Theorem 1 (p.279 l.8–28) treats determining sets 𝔅_k = ∪_jΛ_j, layer by layer. Its hypothesis (7) holds with the ε₁ of the previous item. So the regularity (9)–(10), |A| < B₃Mε₁(L^jη)^{−1} and its companions, holds on every cube of VAR's class at the spacing L^jη of its layer (p.279 l.17–27), and every layer of X lies at a scale ≥ j₀ − 1 ≥ k/2 − 1.

{#1.8} The coarse block averages of V_{j₀−1} are not regular at the coarse scales, and the fine configuration depends on them only through the layers. This is why the depth of the young pairs is first order in the ratio of the fine spacing to the layer's spacing, L^{−(j₀−1)}: the same order as for the all-small-field pair at the scale j₀ − 1.

## 2. The Run-Dependent Ingredients, Sorted (Derived) {#S2}

{#2.1} The ingredients of a young term at the scales i ≥ j₀ are listed in the Cauchy note's §6.2. The selectors are the seven groups of LFR I p.178 l.15–49 and the test (2.17).

{#2.2} (a) *The ingredients of (α).* The small-field action, the covariance, and the function (1.6) are derived in the Cauchy note's §6.2.

{#2.3} (b) *The coupling shells: (1.5) and (1.9).*
- {#2.4} (1.5), χ(|V_j(y,x) − 1| < ε_j), acts on the variable V_j(y,x) of the lattice T_{L^{−j}}, which both runs share. The threshold ε_j = g_jp₀(g_j) depends on the run only through the coupling.
- {#2.5} (1.9), χ(sup|A_j(b)| < g_j^{−1}ϑ_j), acts on the fluctuation variable. Its threshold also depends on the run only through the coupling.
- {#2.6} The mechanism is D6a's cutoff part (`Balaban\DIFFERENCES_PROOFS.md` §2.1, item 2, *Cutoff part, a shell estimate.*; CRE's cutoff r(g) in `WILSON_CAUCHY_LIP1A_2026_10_21.md` §2, *D6a, cutoff part.*). D6a telescopes the two products of indicators and evaluates RG2's bounds on the mixed products, using the room in RG2's constants. Bałaban's bounds are not stated for mixed thresholds, so the split here keeps each piece on one run's own support. With Π_X the product of run X's indicators and ρ_X the rest of its integrand,
  {#2.7} Π_Aρ_A − Π_Bρ_B = Π_AΠ_B(ρ_A − ρ_B) + Π_A(1 − Π_B)ρ_A − Π_B(1 − Π_A)ρ_B.
  {#2.8} The first piece lies on the common support and belongs to (α) and (d). In the second, 1 − Π_B ≤ Σ_b(1 − χ_{B,b}), and on the support of Π_A the factor 1 − χ_{B,b} is the indicator of the shell between the two thresholds at b. The third piece is the same with A and B exchanged.
- {#2.9} So each shell term is run A's own term (or run B's) with one shell indicator inserted. Bałaban's bound (1.79) of 𝐓′1 is proved by estimating the group-valued integrals, with their normalised weights (1.6), by 1, and the A_j-integrals by the positivity of their quadratic forms (LFR II p.383 l.30–34). The shell indicator is ≤ 1 and is kept inside the corresponding integral, so the shell term is at most Bałaban's bound times the mass of the shell under that normalised weight.
- {#2.10} That mass is ≤ C|t′ − t|t′^{d_G−1} times the maximal density on the shell, in the variable X = g_j^{−1}log V_j(y,x) for (1.5) and A_j(b) for (1.9). The thresholds are t = ε_j/g_j = p₀(g_j) and t = g_j^{−1}ϑ_j = (A₁/A₀)p₀(g_j), and |t′ − t| ≤ Ct|g_j − g′_j|/g_j ≤ Ctg_j²|x_j − x′_j| (LIP1A l.68; D6a step 3), with {#D.x_j} x_j := g_j^{−2} and the primes for the other run.
  - {#2.11} For (1.5), the density of the normalised weight (1.6) in X is ≤ C, uniformly in g_j small, since z ≥ cg_j^{d_G}. On the shell it is ≤ Ce^{−cp₀(g_j)²}, since 1 − Re tr V ≥ c|log V|² near 1.
  - {#2.12} For (1.9), the A_j-Gaussian has the precision Q = C*Δ^{(j)}C − C*Δ^{(j)}CC^{(j)}C*Δ^{(j)}C of CRE (2.21), and Q ≤ C*Δ^{(j)}C since C^{(j)} ≥ 0. The marginal variance of A_j(b) is ((Q^{−1})_{bb}) ≥ (Q_{bb})^{−1} ≥ ‖C*Δ^{(j)}C‖^{−1}, so the marginal density is ≤ (‖C*Δ^{(j)}C‖/2π)^{d_G/2}, a lattice constant. No Gaussian tail is used.
  - {#2.13} So the per-variable relative shell factor is ≤ Cp₀(g_j)^{d_G}g_j²|x_j − x′_j|. The variables are counted per point of the history as the variables of (1.6) are in (α) (Cauchy note §6.2).
- {#2.14} The complement χ^{(j−1)c}(R_j) of LFR II p.380 l.42–46 has the shell of (1.9), since the difference of 1 − χ is minus that of χ. Bałaban bounds its integral by the same positivity of the quadratic form (p.380 l.31), so the same bound holds.
- {#2.15} The radial cutoffs of the R-operation are bounded in the Cauchy note's §8.6, except the numerators' factor χ̄(Λ)(V′_k), whose shell is bounded in §4(d). The denominator's χ({|B′| < M₀g_k^{−1}ε_k}) of LFR II (1.2) is the soft test χ̄(Λ) of LFR I (1.101) (§3(d)), and its shell is bounded per bond by the Lipschitz bound of χ̄. The numerators' χ′ (|B| < g_k^{−1}δ′_k) of (1.70) is LFR I's sharp (1.82), and its shell is bounded by the density device above.
- {#2.16} The bound is relative to Bałaban's bound of the term, not to the term itself. So the majorant of the Cauchy note's (LF) is to be read as M_τ built from Bałaban's bound (1.79) of sup𝐓′1, which is the bound that §11(c) uses.

{#2.17} (c) *The plaquette shells: (1.3), (1.4), (1.7), (1.8), and (2.17).* These test U_{j,□}(V_j), U_{j+1,□′}(V_{j+1}), or the reference configurations V^{(j)}_{□′} built from them. All are minimisers computed on the run's fine lattice. At equal data the two runs' tested quantities differ by δ^f_jt with {#D.δ^f_j.2} δ^f_j := C(ε/a_j)^{1−2ε₀}, by the minimiser distance of the Cauchy note's §9.7 applied to the local problem of the cube (VAR Theorem 1 for 𝐁_j(□^{∼4}), as in the Cauchy note's §9.8). Their thresholds, ε_j = g_jp₀(g_j) and 2ϑ_j = 2g_j(A₁/A₀)p₀(g_j), differ through the coupling by ≤ Ctg_j²|δ_j|, as in (b). This is (LF-P), §3.

{#2.18} (d) *The large-field integrands.* These are (LF-A), §4.

## 3. The Plaquette Shells (Derived) {#S3}

{#3.1} (a) *The redundant tests (derived).*
- {#3.2} CRE (3.6)–(3.8) (p.265 l.46–47, p.266 l.26–33): for a cube □ ⊂ Ω^∼_{k+1} of the scale-k test (2.17), on the support of the next scale's small-field test (3.2) and of the Q-test (3.3), |U_{k,□}(∂p) − 1| < (2(1 + β₀)L^{−2} + 4/10)ε_kη² < ε_kη², "Thus χ_k(□) = 1 for □ ⊂ Ω^∼_{k+1}". (3.9) gives the same for the axial-gauge functions χ_{Ax}.
- {#3.3} CRE p.268 l.26–30 with (3.19) and p.269 l.2–4: for □′ ⊂ R^c_{k+1}, the complement taken in Ω^{∼−1}_{k+1}, the Q-test of (3.3) is equal to 1 on the support of the fluctuation cutoff (3.16).
- {#3.4} So in each run's term the tests of the scale j that are not equal to 1 on the support of the term's other characteristic functions lie as follows. The plaquette and axial tests lie on cubes not contained in Ω^∼_{j+1}, in the large-field region Ω^c_{j+1} of the next scale. The reference tests lie on cubes of the collar Ω^{∼2}_{j+1} ∖ Ω_{j+1} (LFR I (1.7)) and of S_{j+1} = (Ω_{j+1} ∖ Ω^{∼−1}_{j+1}) ∪ R_{j+1} (CRE (3.20)–(3.21), p.269 l.7–21), and, in LFR I, of (Ω_{j+1} ∖ Λ^∼_{j+1}) ∩ Z (LFR I (1.8)). All of these lie in the large-field region of the term or its collar. The tests of the stopping scale act on every cube of Ω_k. Where a test is equal to 1 in both runs there is no shell.
- {#3.5} The consequences are three.
  - {#3.6} The all-small-field term ℓ₀ carries the stopping-scale test χ_k(T) of (2.18) and the fluctuation cutoffs (3.16), whose shells are the Cauchy note's §8.2(b), and no other test.
  - {#3.7} In a young history Ω_{i+1} = T for i + 1 < j₀, so every test that is not equal to 1 on the support of the other characteristic functions is at a scale ≥ j₀ − 1 ≥ k/2 − 1 on a cube of the history, or on a stopping-scale cube of Ω_k. So δ^f_j ≤ CL^{−(1−2ε₀)(k/2−1)}, and the history cubes are counted by the history volume, with no volume factor.
  - {#3.8} The tests at the fine scales occur only in the old histories, whose terms the Cauchy note's §6.2 measures against each run's own Z_{ℓ₀}, with no comparison of tests.

{#3.9} (b) *The stopping-scale test of the all-small-field term (bounded in (d)).*
- {#3.10} *The shell.* ρ^X_{ℓ₀}(V) = χ^X_k(T)(V)exp A^X_k(V) on G^{bonds(T^{(k)})}, X = A, B, with χ^X_k(T) the product (2.17) over the stopping-scale cubes, at most N_s⁴ of them, built on run X's fine lattice. Write {#D.f^X_□} f^X_□ := sup_{p⊂□^∼}|U^X_{k,□}(V, ∂p) − 1|/(η^X)² and {#D.t^X} t^X := ε^X_k. On either run's support, |f^A_□ − f^B_□| ≤ δ^ft^A with {#D.δ^f} δ^f := C(ε/a)^{1−2ε₀} (§2(c)), and |t^A − t^B| ≤ Ct^Ag_a²|δ_k| (§2(b)). With {#D.δ^s} δ^s := 2δ^f + 4Cg_a²|δ_k|, which is δ^s_k of §3(d) and exceeds the width δ^f + Cg_a²|δ_k| that this split needs, the split of §2(b) puts the shell on one run's own support: run A's term with the indicator of {t(1 − δ^s) ≤ f^A_□ < t}, {#D.t.2} t := t^A, inserted for one cube □, and the same with A and B exchanged.
- {#3.11} *Lemma SH with a radial family does not work here.* In the complete axial gauge of the torus with the winding holonomies w_μ held fixed, x = 0 is flat only when the w_μ commute; at the plaquettes where the winding bonds of two directions meet it carries [w_μ, w_ν], of size up to 2N_s²ε_k = 2N_s²t on the support, so (M) fails there for every threshold on ḡ.
- {#3.12} *The bound.* The soft tests of (d) bound this shell.

{#3.13} (c) *The young pairs (bounded in (d)).*
- {#3.14} *The form needed.* A bound of each shell term's mass by C(ε/a_j)^{1−2ε₀} times Bałaban's bound of the term, plus a coupling part ≤ |δ_j|, has per cube of the history the form (LF) asks for: s^{LF}_j ≤ C(ε/a_j)^{1−2ε₀} ≤ C_hθ̃^j, since θ̃ ≥ L^{−(1−2ε₀)}, with the coupling part inside s′_K. The soft tests of (d) give it.
- {#3.15} *Lemma SH does not work here.* A radial shrinking of V_j on the cube can switch a failed large-field test of ζ(Ω^c_{j+1}) (CRE (2.21)) to passing, so its hypothesis (R) fails.

{#3.16} (d) *The soft tests (derived).*
- {#3.17} *The device.* F_K = N_K/(κ_KZ_K) (the Cauchy note's §1), with N_K and Z_K the lattice integrals, which do not depend on the decompositions of unity used to expand them. At every K and in both runs, each plaquette and reference test χ({f_□ < t}) is replaced by the soft test χ̄(f_□/t), {#D.χ̄(x)} χ̄(x) := min(1, max(0, (1 + κ_s − x)/κ_s)), and its complement by 1 − χ̄(f_□/t).
  - {#3.18} These are the tests of CRE (1.1), (1.4), (1.8), (2.17), (3.2), and (3.3); of LFR I (1.3)–(1.4), (1.7)–(1.8), (1.22)–(1.24), (1.27), (1.75), and (1.88); and their restatements in LFR II (1.70) and p.380 l.31–46.
  - {#3.19} *The cascade tests.* The tests χ_k^{(n)} of LFR I (1.22)–(1.24) are soft at nested thresholds. There n = j − h counts the integrations, n = 0, …, N with {#D.N} N := k − h, and U^{(N)}_{k,Z} = U″_{k,Z} (p.181 l.4, p.182 l.35). At a cube □, {#D.f^(n)_□} f^{(n)}_□ := sup_{p⊂□}|U^{(n)}_{k,Z}(∂p) − 1|/T_n(p), with T_n(p) the threshold of (1.24) at p, and χ_k^{(n)} is replaced by ∏_□χ̄_c(f^{(n)}_□/(1 + κ_c)^{N−n}), with χ̄_c the function χ̄ with {#D.κ_c} κ_c := κ_s/(N + 1) in place of κ_s. So the test n has the plateau f^{(n)}_□ ≤ (1 + κ_c)^{N−n} and the support f^{(n)}_□ < (1 + κ_c)^{N−n+1}, and every cascade threshold lies between T_n and (1 + κ_c)^{N+1}T_n ≤ e^{κ_s}T_n ≤ (1 + 2κ_s)T_n. The test n = N, at j = k, has the plateau T_N and the width κ_c, and it keeps this form wherever it occurs again.
  - {#3.20} A test keeps its soft form wherever it occurs again: as the stopping test of the next step, in a product of tests on disjoint cube sets (LFR II p.378 l.15–16, where CRE (3.20) makes X_i^{∼−6} and Ω_k^{∼4} disjoint, so no χ̄² = χ̄ is used), and after a change of variables, as in LFR I (1.59).
  - {#3.21} The radial, fluctuation, and gauge-fixing cutoffs stay sharp: CRE (1.5), (1.18), and (3.16); LFR I (1.5), (1.9), (1.55), and (1.82), with (1.5) the restatement of CRE (1.5); and χ′ of LFR II (1.70), which is LFR I's (1.82) (LFR II p.381 l.33).
  - {#3.22} The radial cutoff χ(Λ_i) of the R-operation, LFR I (1.101), is soft, as defined at (1.100)–(1.102) below, and it is the same soft function in LFR II (1.1), (1.2), and (1.70) (p.356 l.19–37, p.378 l.13–14). Its shells are bounded per bond by the Lipschitz bound of χ̄: the shell of χ̄(Λ)(V′_k) in §4(d), and the denominator's in the Cauchy note's §8.6.
  - {#3.23} Every decomposition stays exact, since Σ_P∏_{□∉P}χ̄_□∏_{□∈P}(1 − χ̄_□) = ∏_□(χ̄_□ + 1 − χ̄_□) = 1 for any functions with values in [0, 1]. So N_K and Z_K are unchanged, and F_K is defined at every K by this one construction, both as run A of one pair and as run B of the next.
  - {#3.24} {#D.κ_s.2} κ_s := β/30 = 1/240, with β = 1/8 (§4(d), *The choice β = 1/8, checked.*), within Bałaban's β ≤ 1/4 of LFR I p.191 l.34–35 and p.198 l.16 (the choice of β below (1.24) allows β ≤ ½, p.182 l.16–17). A passed test of width κ_s enters at the threshold (1 + κ_s)t, and a passed cascade test at a threshold ≤ (1 + 2κ_s)t. The checks below are written with 1 + κ_s and hold with 1 + 2κ_s in its place. The smallest relative margin of the passed-test comparisons is that of LFR I (1.31) (p.184 l.8–9), β/10 − β/(5L²) ≥ 7β/90 at L ≥ 3, and (1 + β/15)(1 − 7β/90) < 1. Every other margin below allows a factor 1 + 1/22, and 2κ_s ≤ 1/60. The removals of the cascade tests use no margin (*The statement (R-s)*, χ_k^{(n)}). The letter κ without the index is Bałaban's decay constant, as in exp(−κd_j(X)).
- {#3.25} *The shell bound (derived).* For a test at □ of the scale j, put {#D.x^X} x^X := f^X_□/t^X in run X.
  - {#3.26} The tested quantities differ by |f^A − f^B| ≤ δ^f_jt^A on either run's support, with {#D.δ^f_j.3} δ^f_j := C(ε/a_j)^{1−2ε₀} (§2(c), with the regularity of the support at the thresholds (1 + 2κ_s)t, which changes C by the factor 1 + 2κ_s). The thresholds differ by |t^A − t^B| ≤ Ct^Ag_j²|δ_j| ≤ ½t^A (§2(b)).
  - {#3.27} LFR I (1.27) tests |V_j(b)(V^{(j)}_Z(b))^{−1} − 1| on the bonds b of (Ω_{j+1}^c ∖ Z″_{j+1})^{(j)*} (p.182 l.53), with V^{(j)}_Z = M^j(U^{(j+1−h)}_{k,Z}) the scale-j average of a cascade minimiser (LFR I (1.26)), at the threshold 2δ′_j, and §2(c)'s δ^f_j is stated for the local minimisers of the cubes at the thresholds ε_j and 2ϑ_j. The cascade minimisers are VAR minimisers of their multiscale determining sets, with the same data in both runs, so the profile (P′) of §5(c) and CMP 98 (159)–(163) for the averages bound the two runs' difference of V^{(j)}_Z by 2c_vρ̄_j, ρ̄_j the bound ρ̄ of (P′) on the layer j.
  - {#3.28} *The shell of (1.27) (derived).* For G-valued W_A, W_B, the runs' V^{(j)}_Z(b), ||V_jW_A^{−1} − 1| − |V_jW_B^{−1} − 1|| ≤ |V_jW_A^{−1} − V_jW_B^{−1}| = |W_A^{−1}(W_B − W_A)W_B^{−1}| = |W_B − W_A|. So the tested quantities differ by ≤ 2c_vρ̄_j, and relative to the threshold 2δ′_j by ≤ c_vρ̄_j/δ′_j.
    - {#3.29} The factors. ρ̄_j = 2C_G(ε₀)c″_K(ε/a_j)^{1−ε₀}ε₁ (§4(b), *The configuration difference.*), δ′_j = g_jA₁p₁(g_j) with p₁ < p₀ (LFR I p.183 l.2), and ε₁ = C(M)R_kε_k of (c), with ε_k = g_kA₀p₀(g_k) (CRE (2.4)) and k ≥ j the scale of the configuration. By CRE (2.6), g_k ≤ (1 + β₀)(k − j + 1)^{1/2}g_j and g_j ≤ (1 + β₀)g_k, so log g_k^{−2} ≤ 2log g_j^{−2} for g small, and p₁(g_j) ≥ 1. With R_k ≤ L(log g_k^{−2})^r (CRE (2.5)), ε₁/δ′_j ≤ C(M)(A₀/A₁)(1 + β₀)2^{p₀+r}L(k − j + 1)^{1/2}(log g_j^{−2})^{p₀+r}.
    - {#3.30} The absorption. The shell bound is used on the histories of the young pairs, born at a scale n > k_s/8.   - {#3.44} (a) Every removal of a redundant test holds on the plateau f < t, given the other soft tests at the thresholds (1 + κ_s)t. A cascade test χ_k^{(n)} is removed on its plateau (1 + κ_c)^{N−n}T_n, given χ_k^{(n+1)} at its support threshold (1 + κ_c)^{N−n}T_{n+1}.
  - {#3.45} (b) Every bound that uses a passed test holds at the threshold (1 + κ_s)t, or (1 + 2κ_s)t for a cascade test, and every bound that uses a failed test at the threshold t.
  - {#3.46} (c) The changes of variables that carry a test into a test of the new variables (CRE (1.22), p.269 l.45–50; LFR I (1.59)) stay exact.
  - {#3.47} (d) VAR's (7) holds with ε₁ enlarged by the factor 1 + κ_s (§1). Nonnegativity, the convergence of the expansions, and the loop bound B_W are not affected, since the soft tests have values in [0, 1].

      - {#3.84} *The geometry.* On a component X_i of Z, Λ_k ⊂ Ω_k^{∼−2} (CRE (3.20)), so every plaquette p of Ω_k^c ∩ X_i is at distance ≥ 2MR_k from Z^c. The LM₂R_k-cube □ ∋ p lies in Ω_k^{∼4} or in (Ω_k^{∼4})^c ∩ X_i, so on the first class it passes the soft test, from χ_k(Ω_k^{∼4}) of LFR I (1.71) or from the decomposition of p.378 l.6: |U_{k,□}(∂p) − 1| < (1 + 2κ_s)ε_kη². The operation ∼ on □ adds a layer of M₂R_k-cubes, and M is much larger than M₂ > M₁ (CRE p.245 l.34–38), so □^{∼4} lies within (L + 4)M₂R_k of p and inside Z^{∼−2}, where 𝔹_k(Z) consists of k-blocks (CRE p.256 l.58–63).
      - {#3.85} *U_{k,Z} as the background.* On □^{∼4}, the constraints of 𝔹_k(□^{∼4}) fix the k-block averages of 𝔹_k(Z), and all bonds outside its support. So a competitor of the □^{∼4}-problem at the data M^·(U_{k,Z}), extended by U_{k,Z}, is admissible for the Z-problem, with the same change of the action. By the uniqueness of the minimal orbit (CRE p.256 l.43–53), U_{k,Z} is the minimiser of the □^{∼4}-problem at its own data, the property of U_{k+1,□′} that CRE (3.6) uses. As in (3.6), U_{k,□} = (exp(iη𝐇_{k,□}(B))U_{k,Z})^{u^{−1}}, with {#D.B} B := (1/i)log[M^·(Q_k^{s*}V_k)(M^·(U_{k,Z}))^{−1}].
      - {#3.86} *The argument B.* Off the boundary layer of □^{∼4} of width 2M₁, both averages are V_k: the constraint of U_{k,Z}, and M^k(Q_k^{s*}V_k) = V_k as in (3.6). So B = 0 there. On the layer, M^·(Q_k^{s*}V_k) = M^·(U_{k,□}), and U_{k,□} and U_{k,Z} have the same k-block averages and plaquettes below α₀η², with {#D.α₀} α₀ := O(1)B₃(1 + 2κ_s)ε_k, by |∂V_k − 1| < 2(1 + 2κ_s)ε_k (p.378 l.10–11 with the soft χ_k) and the bound of LFR I p.193 l.20. ## 4. The Large-Field Integrands (Derived; the Points of the Open Gaps Not Reviewed) {#S4}

{#4.1} By §1, U″_{h+2}(exp ig_kB, V″) and U″_k are VAR minimisers with layer data regular at their own scales, all at scales ≥ k/2 − 1.

{#4.2} (a) *The configurations and their data (derived).*
- {#4.3} U″_k = U_{𝐁″_k}(V″⌈_{Λ^c}, exp ig_kBM^·(U^{(AL)}_0)⌈_{Λ∩Ω″^{∼2}_{h+1}}, V″⌈_{(Ω″^{∼2}_{h+1})^c}) (LFR II (1.50), p.370 l.3–5) is the minimiser of the Wilson action with the multiscale determining set 𝐁″_k. Its data are the shared block variables V″ and B, except on Λ ∩ Ω″^{∼2}_{h+1}, where they contain the block averages of U^{(AL)}_0.
- {#4.4} U_0 is the minimiser of A(U) over U regular on Z with M_{𝐁_k}(U) = M_{𝐁_k(Z)}(Q^{s*}_kV_k) on Z ∖ Λ and no constraint on Λ (LFR II (1.3), p.357 l.10–14, with "the results of Sect. G [15]", VAR).
- {#4.5} So the two runs' U″_k differ in three ways: (A-i) the fine lattice of the problem of U″_k at equal data; (A-ii) the data on Λ ∩ Ω″^{∼2}_{h+1}, through U_0, whose own problem is solved on the run's fine lattice; and (A-iii) the coupling in exp ig_kB, which differs relatively by ≤ g_k²|δ_k| and belongs with the coupling terms of (α).

{#4.6} (b) *(A-i), the depth at equal data (derived).* The chain of the Cauchy note's §9 is run for the multiscale problem, with {#D.a_j} a_j := εL^j the spacing of the layer Λ_j in run A's units and j(x) the layer of the point x. Each step has a multiscale form.
- {#4.7} *Regularity.* VAR Theorem 1 treats determining sets 𝔅_k = ∪_jΛ_j. With (7) on the support (§1), (9.2) holds on the cubes of the layer j with a_j in place of a: |F| ≤ C₀ε₁/a_j², |∇F| ≤ C₀ε₁/a_j³, |A| ≤ C₀ε₁/a_j in the cube gauge. The cube-gauge regularity (3.35)–(3.36) of {#D.Ũ} Ũ := MU^B is §9.8's computation on each cube, and the weights (9.11) of the linearised averaging are local, so both hold layer by layer.

So |b(U^B)| ≤ Σ_xC_b(ε/a_{j(x)})ε₁², the sum over the points x of the layers in their own units, and the remainders of (9.5) satisfy |r₁| ≤ C_rεε₁/a_{j(x)}³, |r₀| ≤ C_rεε₁²/a_{j(x)}⁴ at x.

PBG (3.42)–(3.44) (p.397 l.37–p.398 l.25) bound the propagator with the factor L^jη of the layer of x and the decay e^{−δ₀d(y,y′)} in the weighted distance PRT2 (2.46) (p.231 l.9–13). At x in the layer j, a source in the layer j′ enters a_j|𝔊ℒ*D*r₁(x)| with the factor a_j²/a_{j′}³ = (a_j/a_{j′})²a_{j′}^{−1}, and the plain source r₀ enters a_j|𝔊ℒ*r₀(x)| with the factor a_j³/a_{j′}⁴ = (a_j/a_{j′})³a_{j′}^{−1}, by the entries G′∇_U^*λ (for D*r₁) and G′λ (for r₀) of PBG (3.42) (p.397 l.42–44) transferred to 𝔊 by Theorem 3.13 as in §9.5, with the constant 2B₀. For j′ ≥ j both factors are ≤ a_{j′}^{−1}.

  {#4.9-3} VAR's contraction runs in the layer-weighted sup norm of (115) and (117)–(121), so (9.6) gives the fixed point in that norm, not pointwise: a_{j(x)}|A₁*(x)| + a_{j(x)}²|∇A₁*(x)| ≤ {#D.ρ̄} ρ̄ := 2C_G(ε₀)c_K(ε/a_n)^{1−ε₀}ε₁ at every x. This is the form used below.
- {#4.10} *The joins (derived, not reviewed, including the middle-layer width and the block size M′).* The sets 𝐁₁ = 𝐁″_k ∪ 𝐁_h(Ω″^∼_{h+1}) and 𝐁₂ = 𝐁″_k ∪ 𝐁_h((Ω″^∼_{h+1})^c) of LFR II (1.52) are joins by CRE (2.14), and their layers need not be wider than RM.
  - {#4.11} The collar. On Ω ∖ Ω^{∼−2} a join is 𝐁_h(Ω), whose domains satisfy dist(Ω_n, Ω_{n−1}^c) ≥ L^nξM₁ on T_ξ, ξ = L^{−h} (CRE p.256 l.57–60). So its layer n − 1 is at least LM₁ wide in its own units. This is VAR's (1) for R < L, and it is less than RM.
  - {#4.12} The join. By (2.14) the join is 𝐁 on Ω^{∼−2} and 𝐁_h(Ω) on the strip {#D.S} S := Ω ∖ Ω^{∼−2}, with ∂Ω in the layer h of 𝐁 at a distance ≥ 2M₁ from that layer's boundaries inside Ω (CRE p.257 l.9–15). Distances below are in the units of the scale h. The collar's domains Ω_n satisfy Ω^{∼−2} ⊂ Ω_h (p.256 l.61–62) and dist(Ω_h, Ω_{h−1}^c) ≥ M₁ (l.57–60 at n = h), and Ω″_{h+1}^∼ adds one layer of the MR_{h+1}-cubes of the scale h + 1 (LFR I p.179 l.6–7), so dist(Ω″_{h+1}, (Ω″^∼_{h+1})^c) ≥ LMR_{h+1}. For j ≤ h, Ω″_j = Ω_j (LFR I (1.12)), and these layers of 𝐁″_k are wider than 2MR_j in the units of their scale j (CRE p.256 l.21–23). For h + 1 ≤ j ≤ k − N₀ the Ω″_j are R-operation domains, with Ω″_j ∖ Ω″_{j+1} = Ω_j^{∼5} ∖ Ω_{j+1}^{∼5} on Z, which CRE p.256 l.21–23 does not cover. Bałaban takes the functions U_{𝐁₁} and U_{𝐁₂} after (1.52) and expands U^0_k, the configuration of 𝐁″_k, around U_{1,2} by VAR's Sects. D–E at (1.54) (LFR II p.370), without stating the widths of these sets. The width of these middle layers is derived, not reviewed, in *The middle layers.* below, from CRE (3.5).
  - {#4.13} The layers of 𝐁₁. Here Ω = Ω″^∼_{h+1} ⊂ Ω″_h, so the join's domains Ω^J_j equal the collar's Ω_j for j ≤ h, and Ω″_{h+1} ⊂ Ω^{∼−2} for the layers above. The layers j ≤ h − 1 are the collar's, ≥ LM₁ wide in their own units. The layer h runs from ∂Ω_h, within 2M₁ of ∂Ω, to ∂Ω″_{h+1}, so its width is ≥ LMR_{h+1} − 2M₁ ≥ LM₁, since M > M₂ = L²M₁ (CRE p.245 l.35–38). The layers above h are those of 𝐁″_k: the top N₀ are M wide, and the middle ones, h + 1 ≤ j ≤ k − N₀, have the width of *The joins.*, derived, not reviewed.
  - {#4.14} The layers of 𝐁₂. Here Ω = (Ω″^∼_{h+1})^c, the join's top layer is h, and it can be thin, since (2.14) gives only dist(∂Ω, ∂Ω″_h) ≥ 2M₁ ≥ dist(Ω_h, Ω^c). A layer j ≤ h − 1 of the join is the collar's layer j on S and 𝐁″_k's layer j on Ω^{∼−2}, and the distance from Ω^J_{j+1} to (Ω^J_j)^c is at least L^{j+1−h}M₁, LM₁ in the units of the scale j, in each of the four cases. Collar to collar it is the collar's width. 𝐁″_k to 𝐁″_k it is 𝐁″_k's width. From Ω″_{j+1} ∩ Ω^{∼−2} to S ∖ Ω_j or to Ω^c it is ≥ dist(Ω_h, Ω_{h−1}^c) ≥ M₁, since Ω^{∼−2} ⊂ Ω_h and Ω_j^c ⊂ Ω_{h−1}^c. From Ω_{j+1} ∩ S to (Ω″_j)^c it is ≥ dist(Ω^c, (Ω″_j)^c) − 2M₁ ≥ 2MR_{h−1}L^{−1}, since a path from Ω^c = Ω″^∼_{h+1} ⊂ Ω″_h to (Ω″_j)^c crosses ∂Ω″_h, at ≥ 2M₁ from ∂Ω, and then 𝐁″_k's layers h − 1, …, j.
  - {#4.15} The top layer of 𝐁₂ is not crossed. In PRT2's decomposition of a contour, each crossing joins two surfaces Σ_{j_l} and Σ_{j_{l+1}} with |j_l − j_{l+1}| = 1 and lies in the layer min{j_l, j_{l+1}} ((2.47), p.231 l.20–36). A crossing in the layer h of 𝐁₂ would join Σ_h with Σ_{h+1}, and 𝐁₂ has no Σ_{h+1}. So (2.57) uses only the widths of the layers below the top, and the thin top layer of 𝐁₂ does not enter the count.
  - {#4.16} The count at a smaller width. Bałaban's count (2.58) uses (2.2) only through (2.57), the length > RM of each crossing between two surfaces Σ_j (PRT2 p.233 l.18–23), and Lemma 2.1's (2.60), the decay e^{−αδ₀RM·max(|j−j′|−1, 0)} (p.234 l.2–6), follows from (2.48) and (2.57). So (2.57)–(2.61) and every count of this section hold with RM replaced by any common lower bound W of the layer widths in their own units, each line unchanged.
  - {#4.17} At the joins W = LM₁. The top N₀ layers of 𝐁″_k, inside the joins, are one layer of M-cubes of their own scale wide (LFR I p.179 l.19–24), so M wide in their own units, and M > M₂ = L²M₁ > LM₁ (CRE p.245 l.35–38, with Bałaban's choice M₂ = L²M₁ and M "much larger than M₂"). So every layer that a crossing traverses is ≥ LM₁ wide in its own units, in 𝐁₁ and in 𝐁₂, and so are the middle layers h + 1 ≤ j ≤ k − N₀ of 𝐁″_k in 𝐁₁, by the next item.
  - {#4.18} The middle layers (derived, not reviewed). For h + 1 ≤ j ≤ k − N₀, Z″_j = (Ω_j^{∼5})^c ∩ Z (LFR I (1.11), p.179), so on Z the layer j of 𝐁″_k is Ω_j^{∼5} ∖ Ω_{j+1}^{∼5} for j ≤ k − N₀ − 1, by (1.12). At j = k − N₀ the next set is Z″_{k−N₀+1} = (Ω^{∼7}_{k−N₀+1})^c ∩ Z (LFR I (1.10), p.179 l.15), so that layer is Ω^{∼5}_{k−N₀} ∖ Ω^{∼7}_{k−N₀+1}. Ω_j^{∼n} adds n layers of the cubes of Ω_j, of the side MR_j in the units a_j of the scale j (LFR I p.179 l.7–8). These Ω_j are the domains of the renormalisation steps j, not domains determined by the R-operation (the two kinds of CRE p.256 l.21–22), as Bałaban states (checked). By the condition (ii) (LFR I p.177 l.27–28), no new large-field region was created in Z in the last N steps, and he draws the consequence for (1.2) at once: the one-step operations 𝕋^{(j)}(Z_{j+1}) "are given by the formula (2.21) [III], in which the functions ζ, χ have the simplest form, namely by the condition (ii) no large field characteristic functions are included in them" (LFR I p.178, below (1.2)). Their ζ(Ω_{j+1}^c ∩ Z_{j+1})χ(Ω_{j+1} ∩ Z_{j+1}) is the product (1.3)–(1.9) of the small-field tests of step j, so Ω_{j+1} on Z is the domain that step j's tests determine, and (1.11)–(1.12) take these Ω_j. A step adds at least ten layers of MR-cubes to the large-field region (LFR I p.177 l.18–19).
    {#4.18-1} Directly from CRE (3.5) (p.265), Ω_{j+1} lies three layers of MR_{j+1}a_{j+1}-cubes inside B^{j+1}(P^1_{j+1}). That set lies five further layers inside the complement of Z′_j ⊇ Λ_j^c ⊇ Ω_j^c (CRE p.264 l.52–56, p.265 l.16–22; Λ_j ⊂ Ω_j by CRE p.269 l.9, Λ_{k+1} = Ω_{k+1}^{∼−2} ∩ (R′^∼_{k+1})^c). So dist(Ω_{j+1}, Ω_j^c) ≥ 8MR_{j+1}a_{j+1}. The enlargement ∼5 moves the boundary of Ω_{j+1} outwards by at most 5MR_{j+1}a_{j+1}, and that of Ω_j outwards, which only widens the layer. So dist(Ω_{j+1}^{∼5}, (Ω_j^{∼5})^c) ≥ 3MR_{j+1}a_{j+1} = 3LMR_{j+1}a_j, and the layer j ≤ k − N₀ − 1 is at least 3LMR_{j+1} ≥ 3LM > LM₁ wide in its own units (R_{j+1} ≥ 1, M > M₂ = L²M₁). At j = k − N₀ the enlargement ∼7 moves the boundary by at most 7MR_{j+1}a_{j+1}, so that layer is at least LMR_{j+1} ≥ LM > LM₁ wide. The same bounds give VAR's (1) for this sequence, (L^jη)^{−1}dist(Ω″_j^c, Ω″_{j+1}) > RM₁ on Z, with R and M₁ the parameters of VAR's (1) (REG (1.4)), under LM > RM₁, which holds for M large (CRE p.245 l.35–38). At the joins these parameters are R′ and M′ (*The separation.*), and LM > LM₁ > R′M′. With Bałaban's ten layers the width is 5LMR_{j+1}. Case 4 of 𝐁₂ uses only the layers ≤ h − 1 of 𝐁″_k, where Ω″ = Ω. The conditions that the counts of this section put on RM become the condition (J-W): (2.59) at α = 1/128 and ⅛δ_*LM₁ ≥ 4 log L + 1, at the rate δ_* of *The rate.* below.
    {#4.18-2} Their left sides increase with the width and the right side of (2.59) decreases with α, so (J-W) implies the conditions at every α ≥ 1/128 and at every width ≥ LM₁, and it replaces the conditions on R and M wherever a layer that the profile crosses is narrower than RM: at the joins, and at the top N₀ layers of 𝐁″_k, which are M wide.
  - {#4.19} (J-W) holds for M₁ large.
    - {#4.20} The rate. Two rates enter the counts: PRT2's local rate δ₀^{(2.43)}, inside the proofs through Lemma 2.1, and the rate δ₀^{PBG} of PBG Theorem 3.1, whose constants M₁, δ₀, a₀, and B₀ are "dependent on d and L only" and serve "for M ≥ M₁", M the size of the big blocks (PBG p.397 l.37–38). Both depend on d and L only (*RDG's big blocks.* below). The counts are taken at δ_* := min(δ₀^{PBG}, δ₀^{(2.43)}). The left side of (2.59) increases with δ₀ and c₀ decreases with it, so the conditions at δ_* give those at either rate, and no comparison of the two rates is needed. The distance is PRT2 (2.46), in the block units of each layer (p.231 l.9–13).
    - {#4.21} Theorem 3.1 at the joins. PBG proves Theorems 3.1–3.3 by generalised random walk expansions that reduce them to the theorems for propagators without external field proved in PRT2, and states their constants independent of {Ω_j} "if the conditions (2.1), (2.2) are satisfied" (PBG p.399). In PRT2's counts, (2.2) enters through the length > RM of each crossing in (2.57) (p.233): Lemma 2.1 (p.234) and the factors e^{−cδ₀RM·max(|j−j′|−1, 0)} of p.235 and p.237. PRT2's own localisations also use the layer geometry, with cubes of the size 2ML^jη that meet at most B^{j+1}(Λ_{j+1}) besides B^j(Λ_j) (p.230 l.1–2, p.235 l.35, p.238, the last four lines, p.239 l.40–42); the reach below covers them, PRT2's largest cube being □̃³. The choice of Ω₀ at distance ≤ RM from Ω₁ is an example ("e.g.") at PRT2 p.228 l.20 and PBG p.394 l.32; at PBG p.396 l.17 it defines Λ₀ for the regularity class, which holds at R′M′ as well. PBG's own localisation is a further use of the layer geometry: its cubes □̃³ are "either contained in B^j(Λ_j), or intersect also the domain B^{j+1}(Λ_{j+1})" (p.408 l.19–34), with local sequences satisfying "(2.1)–(2.4) of [4]" (p.408 l.2) and "the conditions (2.1), (2.2)" (p.408 l.34). The printed dichotomy names only the inner domain; as an exhaustive dichotomy it assumes that □̃³ does not meet the finer domains, and PBG does not treat that outward case.
      {#4.21-1} The reach into B^{j−1}(Λ_{j−1}) occurs at any width; the reach into B^{j−2}(Λ_{j−2}) is the case specific to layers LM₁ wide. PBG's cubes are □̃ⁿ, "a cube of the size (2 + 2n)ML^jη" (p.408 l.23–24), and its localisation uses n ≤ 5 (□̃³ in the dichotomy, Ω_j(□) ⊂ □̃⁴, and Ω₀(□) ⊂ □̃⁵) and n = 8 in Sect. C (p.415 l.9–10). A cube of 𝒟_j has one big block in B^j(Λ_j) (p.408 l.21) and can reach one big block beyond ∂Ω_j, so its □̃⁵ reaches about 6ML^jη outwards, while the finer layer Λ_{j−1}, LM wide in its own units, is only M wide in the units L^jη; so □̃⁵ can meet Λ_{j−2}, for every L. This happens in Bałaban's own sequences as well: CRE's maximal sequences 𝐁 have layers L^nξM₁ deep, LM₁ in their own units (p.256 l.57–62), and CRE applies the theorems of the previous papers to them at the size M₁ (p.245 l.35–37). At the joins the sequences are these sequences 𝐁 of CRE, with M₁-cubes. CRE takes M₁ as "the size of large cubes for which all the theorems of the previous papers, especially those concerning the variational problem, are valid" (p.245 l.35–37). Here, at the joins, the theorems of PBG and VAR are applied instead with a smaller block size, so that the reach into B^{j−2}(Λ_{j−2}) does not occur (derived, not reviewed):
      - {#4.22} *The block size M′.* Let M′ be a power of L with M′ ≥ max(M₁^{PBG}, R₀M₀, R₁M₁^{VAR}), with M₁^{PBG} the threshold M₁(d, L) of PBG Theorems 3.1–3.3 (p.397 l.38, "for M ≥ M₁"), R₀M₀ that of PBG's local sequences, and R₁M₁^{VAR} VAR's product, which is also REG's, since VAR fixes R₁, M₁ so that the results of REG hold ([6] of VAR, p.277 l.17, p.281 l.14) and REG's smallest integers (REG p.098 l.8) are replaced by them (the Cauchy note's #C9.1), the last two taken as powers of L, so that M′ is a multiple of each: PBG takes M = KR₀M₀ (p.408 l.28), and VAR's cube parameters are multiples of R₁M₁ (VAR p.279 l.3, p.300 l.29–30). Take CRE's {#D.M₁} M₁ := KM′ with K a power of L and K ≥ 12d + 1, since PBG identifies the big-block lattice with T^{(j+m)} for M = L^m (p.408 l.20). This covers the reach below (K ≥ 10d + 1), the lift's R_ι (K ≥ 4d + 1), and the W-δ note's condition R ≥ 12dL on its walk problems (its §§7, 11, and 12), which at the joins reads R′ = LK − 1 ≥ 12dL and holds since L(12d + 1) − 1 ≥ 12dL. M′ also satisfies (1/16)δ₀M′ > 2d log c₀(⅛) + 1, PRT2's (2.59) at α = ¼ with RM = M′, which the count of the strip sources at the composites uses ((iv), *The size of the strip sources.*); it is a lower bound of d, δ₀, and c₀(⅛).

F sequences (144) and cubes □̃ (p.300 l.33–37), (163), (165), and M(ε₁). With M′ a multiple of VAR's R₁M₁ they are run at the cube parameter M′, which is what R₁ = 1 means here. So (J-W) at the width R′M′ holds once M₁ ≥ 2M_J(d, L) (*The choice of M₁.*). The printed conditions on R, M, R₁, and M₁ are lower bounds of four kinds: on the products RM and R₁M₁, among them VAR's "R₁M₁ sufficiently big, so that B₃e^{−½δ₀R₁M₁} ≤ ½" (p.304 l.2–4); separate ones, R ≥ R₁ (VAR p.277 l.17) and R, M "sufficiently large" (PBG p.408 l.26), of which the latter fixes R₀ and M₀ of PBG's local sequences, which are unchanged here, while R enters PRT2 only through the product RM, in (2.59) and (2.83), and through the layer geometry, so R′ needs no separate threshold; divisibility, M = KR₀M₀ (PBG p.408 l.28) and VAR's cube parameters multiples of R₁M₁ (VAR p.279 l.3, p.300 l.29–30; REG p.098 l.6–8); and ratios, REG's example "L^{−1}RM > 2dR₁M₁", which gives □̃ ⊂ Ω_{k−1} (REG p.098 l.17–18), and the reach below. VAR p.300 l.36–37 states □̃ ⊂ Ω_{j−1} for its Sect. F cubes without a printed ratio; for its cubes of the side 2R₁M₁ the derived condition is R > 4dLR₁ (the W-δ note's §12, *The lift's R_ι (checked).*), which R′ meets at R₁ = 1 for K ≥ 4d + 1, since LK − 1 ≥ 4dL + L − 1. C, PBG takes G′_{□̃₀²} with the boundary conditions outside □̃₀⁵, which it identifies in the original cubes with the outside of □̃⁸, or of □̃₁⁸ with □₁ ∈ 𝒟_{j+1} (p.415 l.9–10, with p.411 l.22–25 and p.413 l.6–10). Theorems 3.9 and 3.10 state that their terms depend on U restricted to the enlargements X̃⁵ of their localisation domains, among them X = □̃₀² = □̃⁴ itself. Under the convention (2 + 2n), the fivefold enlargement of □̃⁴, of the side 10M′L^jη, has the side 20M′L^jη, that of □̃⁹; so Bałaban's identification □̃₀⁵ = □̃⁸ is not exact, and □̃⁹ bounds both. Every other cube of PBG is □̃ⁿ with n ≤ 5, and PRT2's are at most □̃³ (PRT2 p.238, the last four lines). □̃⁹ reaches at most 10M′L^jη beyond ∂Ω_j. The layer Λ_{j−1} of 𝐁 is M₁L^jη = KM′L^jη wide in these units in the lattice distance, which is the ℓ¹ distance (PRT2 p.223 l.16), and an ℓ∞ reach of 10M′L^jη is an ℓ¹ reach of at most 10dM′L^jη; K ≥ 10d + 1 > 10d. The geometric two-layer conditions, PBG's class cubes in B^j(Λ_j) ∪ B^{j+1}(Λ_{j+1}) (the class of (3.35), p.396, used for □̃⁵ on p.409) and PRT2's torus □̃³ carrying two scales (p.238, the last two lines, and p.239), are covered by the same count; inwards they hold with a large margin, since Λ_{j+1} is L²KM′ wide in the units L^jη. For □₁ ∈ 𝒟_{j+1} the same holds in the units L^{j+1}η against the layer Λ_j, which is KM′ wide in these units. So every localisation domain of PBG meets at most the layers j − 1, j, and j + 1. The reach into j − 1 is the one that occurs at every width, in PBG's own sequences too, and the case specific to layers LM₁ wide does not arise.

Bałaban also uses the joins' functions himself: LFR II takes U_{𝐁₁} and U_{𝐁₂} after (1.52) (p.370).

A bond b belongs to the layer j when b ∈ Ω_j ∖ Ω_{j+1}, as in PBG (3.41), where Ω also denotes the set of bonds with at least one endpoint in Ω (PRT2 p.224 l.17–19); so a bond that straddles the boundary of Ω_{j+1} belongs to the layer j + 1. Put {#D.π(x)} π(x) := (ε/a_{j(x)})^{1−ε₀} ≤ 1. For a block y of the layer j, {#D.‖A‖_y} ‖A‖_y := sup_{b∈Δ(y)}(a_j|A(b)| + a_j²|∇A(b)|).

For complex A with |A|_∞ ≤ ε₃ ≤ ¼a₃ and every bond b of the block y, a_{j(y)}³|N(A)(b)| ≤ C_Nε₃Σ_{y″}e^{−⅛δ₀d(y,y″)}‖A‖_{y″}, with C_N a constant of d, L, and Bałaban's constants, under ⅛δ₀RM ≥ 4 log L + 1 and (2.59) at α = 1/128.   - {#4.34} (i) *The vertices.* Each vertex of VAR's formulas is a function of the field on the bonds near one block or plaquette. The block functions C_j(·,c) and δC_j/δA (VAR (49), (69), (72), [4] Prop. 5) are analytic on the local polydisc of a fixed radius r_v in the units a_j|·| and are bounded there by M_v, both constants of d and L, by (44), (52)–(54), (72), the range argument of (59)–(62) (p.287), and locality. On the complex line through the local field X, of local size s, Schwarz's lemma, applied to τ ↦ f(τX/s) on |τ| < r_v, bounds a vertex f that vanishes to order m at 0 by M_v(s/r_v)^m. For s ≥ ½r_v the direct bound (72) at the actual field gives |f| ≤ M_v ≤ M_v(2s/r_v)^m, so |f| ≤ M_v(2s/r_v)^m for every s, and the factor 2^m enters C_v. For δC_j/δA, m = 1 by (44) and (56), which gives |a_j(δC_j/δA)(X)(c,·)| ≤ C_va_j^{1−d}s, the local form of (72); for its part beyond the linear one, m = 2, which gives C_va_j^{1−d}(s/r_v)s. The plaquette functions (∂/∂A)V₀′(·,∂p) and the commutator terms of (91)–(96) have explicit bounds in the field on ∂p and its differences (VAR (40), p.291, (94)–(96)), of order ≥ 2, so one factor is the local size and the others are ≤ 2ε₃. A local size at a block c is ≤ L·max ‖·‖_{y′} over the blocks y′ meeting the bonds of the vertex for the vertices that depend on the field alone, and ≤ L²·max ‖·‖_{y′} for the gradient vertices of (91)–(96), since adjacent layers differ by one factor L in a_j and L² in a_j².

  - {#4.36} (iii) *The chains.* Every term of N in (85), (88)–(90), and (91)–(96) is a chain of at most six links. The links are the kernels H, H*, Q, Q*, (QGQ*)^{−1}, a, 𝔇*(A), and 𝔇₂(A), at the bounds (69), (71), (73), and (3.132)–(3.133), with Q and Q* at the bound of a local average (a kernel ≤ 1, supported within one block and its neighbours), together with the vertices and fields of (i)–(ii); Δ_πH enters only through (89), which reduces it to these links. In each term one link carries the local size: D(A) by (ii) in the first line of (88) and in (89); QA in the second line of (88); 𝔇₂ by (ii) in (85); and the vertex by (i) in (90)–(96). Every other link is at its printed bound. The factor ε₃ comes from the bound of the local-size link itself in the first line of (88), the first part of (90), and the direct terms of (91)–(96), and from another link in the other terms; in (85) the current J also supplies ε₁. The variants of (91)–(96) that VAR sketches are chains of the same kinds. The sum over each intermediate block uses the triangle inequality (2.54) and the count c_tot(1/128), which costs δ₀/128 of the decay per link. In d = 4 a pairing of a source with a field over a block is scale-invariant, Σ_{b∈Δ(y)}η^da_j^{−3}a_j^{−1} ≤ d, so in the variables a_j|A|, a_j³|f|, and D the links are dimensionless kernels.

The links decay at the rates r_i: δ₀ for H, H*, (QGQ*)^{−1}, and ℜ (after PBG p.423 l.39), ½δ₀ for (71) and (73), and ¼δ₀ for the bounds of (ii). A ratio costs δ₀/32 of its own link's rate, so the i-th link decays at r′_i ≥ r_i − δ₀/32, and {#D.δ_ch} δ_ch := min_ir′_i ≥ 7δ₀/32 (a rate, not the residual ρ(x) of #4.9). With d_i the distance spanned by the i-th link, Π_ie^{−r′_id_i} ≤ e^{−(δ_ch−δ₀/128)Σ_id_i}Π_ie^{−(δ₀/128)d_i}, with Σ_id_i ≥ d(y,y″) by (2.54). The sums over the at most five intermediate blocks, taken one at a time, each use one factor e^{−(δ₀/128)d_i} and give ≤ c_tot(1/128)⁵ in all. So the chain decays from y to y″ at the rate ≥ δ_ch − δ₀/128 ≥ 27δ₀/128 > ⅛δ₀, which gives the stated bound.

Put {#D.u(y)} u(y) := ‖A₁*‖_y. The propagator bound and the kernel form at {#D.ε₃} ε₃ := ε₄ give u(y) ≤ π(y)|ρ|_π + 2B₀C_Nε₄Σ_{y′}(a_j/a_{j′})³e^{−δ₀d(y,y′)}Σ_{y″}e^{−⅛δ₀d(y′,y″)}u(y″). Write π(y″)/π(y) = [π(y″)/π(y′)][π(y′)/π(y)]. The first factor is ≤ L^{1−ε₀}e^{η_πd(y′,y″)} by *The ratio.*, so the y″-sum is ≤ L^{1−ε₀}c_tot(1/128)π(y′)|u|_π, since ⅛δ₀ − η_π ≥ δ₀/128. The lattice is finite, so |u|_π < ∞, and under (T-π) below |u|_π ≤ (4/3)|ρ|_π. No contraction in |·|_π is needed.

Here A′* is the field of (112), not the variable A′ of {#D.N.3} N := δV/δA′. Hence, for X = A₁* and X = A′*, a_{j(x)}|X(x)| + a_{j(x)}²|∇X(x)| ≤ {#D.ρ̄(x)} ρ̄(x) := 2C_G(ε₀)c″_K(ε/a_{j(x)})^{1−ε₀}ε₁ at every x. The condition (T-π) is 8B₀C_NLc_tot(1/128)c″_Kε₄ ≤ 1, 2C_{HD}Lc_tot(1/128)ε₄ ≤ 1, ε₄ ≤ ¼a₃ (for the kernel form at {#D.ε₃.3} ε₃ := ε₄), and VAR's ε₄ = 3B₀C₁B₃ε₁ ≤ a₄ (for Proposition 6 and (115)), smallness conditions on ε₁ uniform in k, K, ε, the volume, and the number of layers.
  - {#4.39} *The result.* On a problem whose finest layer is the history's, j(x) ≥ n, and this is the bound ρ̄ above with c″_K in place of c_K. In the presence of layers finer than the history's, those of older histories, U^A and MU^B at equal data, compared in VAR's gauge relative to MU^B, differ at x by an amount set by the layer of x, not by the finest layer of the set. This is the coarse-side comparison; the fine-side comparison of ι(U^A) with U^B in the Cauchy note's §9.7 is not covered by this bullet.
- {#4.40} *The gap.* Every term of §9.6 is a sum over the lattice of products of A₁*, its gradient, and the local quantities J, F, and Δ at the same point, up to the non-local links ℒ and H of #4.40.1, so the bounds of §9.6 hold point by point with the uniform ρ̄ of #4.9 and a_{j(x)}, with C_ℒ^π of #4.40.1 in place of C_ℒ: A_ε(Ũ) − A_ε(U^A) ≤ Σ_x[32C_rC_ℒ^π(ε/a_{j(x)})ρ̄ε₁ + Cρ̄²], 32C_rC_ℒ^π being the coefficient of the linear term of §9.6 and C that of its quadratic terms, the sum over the points of the layers in their own units. Since ε/a_{j(x)} ≤ ε/a_n, the gap is ≤ C′_gap(ε₀)Σ_x(ε/a_n)^{2−2ε₀}ε₁², {#D.C′_gap(ε₀)} C′_gap(ε₀) := 2C_G(ε₀)c_K(32C_rC_ℒ^π + 2CC_G(ε₀)c_K).
- {#4.40.1} *The non-local links.* Two links of §9.6 are not local: ℒ, in ⟨A₁*, J⟩ = db(U^B)[ℒA₁*], and H, in HD(A₁*) and HC^{(2)}(A₁*). H is handled by *The ratio.* (#4.31) as in #4.38, and its cost Lc_tot(1/128) is part of the constant C of the quadratic terms. ℒ = I + Q₁^{pl}*(T^{pl})^{−1}(1 − Q₁^{pl}I) on T_ε satisfies |ℒg(x)| ≤ Σ_{x′}C_ℒ^{ker}e^{−δ_Q^{pl}d_ε(x,x′)}|g(x′)| and |D(ℒg)(x)| ≤ Σ_{x′}C_ℒ^{ker}e^{−δ_Q^{pl}d_ε(x,x′)}(|∇g(x′)| + (ε₁/a_{x,x′})|g(x′)|), a_{x,x′} := min(a_{j(x)}, a_{j(x′)}), since the commutator part carries the regularity (#4.7) of a layer of x or of x′; these are the local forms of the bounds sup|ℒg| ≤ C_ℒsup|g| and sup|D(ℒg)| ≤ C_ℒ(sup|∇g| + (ε₁/a)sup|g|) of the Cauchy note's §9.4 (*The decay.*, and #4.316), {#D.C_ℒ^ker} C_ℒ^{ker} := the constant of these local bounds, a constant of L, d, G, and C₀, as §9.4's C_ℒ (not the double-bar lift's C_ℒ′).
- {#4.40.2} A point x′ in the layer j′ with n := |j(x) − j′| ≥ 2 is at least RM(n − 1) spacings ε from x, by PRT2 (2.60) (p.234 l.5) and since each layer's unit is ≥ ε, and a_{j(x)}/a_{j′} ≤ L^n and a_{j(x)}²/a_{x,x′} ≤ L^{2n}a_{j′} for every n ≥ 0. So, with {#D.c_ε} c_ε := Σ_{x′}e^{−½δ_Q^{pl}d_ε(x,x′)}, a constant of L and d, a_{j(x)}|ℒA₁*(x)| + a_{j(x)}²|D(ℒA₁*)(x)| ≤ (1 + ε₁)C_ℒ^{ker}c_εL²(1 + Σ_{n≥2}L^{2n−2}e^{−½δ_Q^{pl}RM(n−1)})ρ̄ ≤ C_ℒ^πρ̄, {#D.C_ℒ^π} C_ℒ^π := 4L²C_ℒ^{ker}c_ε, under ε₁ ≤ 1 and ½δ_Q^{pl}RM ≥ 2 log L + 1, the latter a condition on Bałaban's R and M (at the joins and the top N₀ layers of 𝐁″_k, with LM₁ in place of RM by #4.16, a lower bound on M₁ of d and L that joins those of #4.29), since then Σ_{n≥2}L^{2n−2}e^{−½δ_Q^{pl}RM(n−1)} ≤ Σ_{n≥1}e^{−n} < 1.
- {#4.41} *The weighted action.* LFR II (1.70) evaluates A(ζ₁/(g″)², ·) at the minimiser of the unweighted action, so for the weights {#D.w} w := ζ₁/(g″)² the first-order term of the gap does not vanish. It is ⟨J_w, A₁*⟩ with |J_w| ≤ C(|w| + a_{j(x)}|∇w|)ε₁/a_{j(x)}³ at x, so it is ≤ Σ_xC sup|w|(ε/a_n)^{1−ε₀}ε₁² per point, by the bound ρ̄ on A₁*.
- {#4.42} *The result.* For the action of (1.70) at equal data, |A(w, U″^B) − A(w, U″^A)| ≤ Σ_xC_w(ε₀)g_{j(x)}^{−2}(ε/a_n)^{1−ε₀}ε₁², the sum over the points of the layers, with C_w(ε₀) a constant of Bałaban's and VAR's constants and of ε₀, and a_n = εL^n the spacing of the history's finest layer. With g_{j(x)}^{−2} ≤ g_a^{−2} + β′k by CRE (2.6) and ε₁ ≤ Cḡp₀(ḡ) by §1, this is ≤ C_hθ̃^n per point of the history, since θ̃ ≥ L^{−(1−2ε₀)} and the factor linear in k is absorbed by L^{−ε₀n}, n > k/8, into C_h, a constant of ε₀, ḡ, j(C), and Bałaban's constants. This is the birth-scale form of (LF) (the Cauchy note's (LF) line). Outside the history the layer is the stopping layer, and the per-point bound is that of the single-scale (9.10), with the tails of the history's sources included in the sum.

{#4.43} (c) *(A-ii), the depth of U_0 (derived).* Let a be the spacing of the scale of (1.3) in run A's units, so ε/a ≤ L^{−(k/2−1)} in a young history (§1). Λ is a rectangular parallelepiped in a cube of side 100M, with the graph G₀ fixing the axial gauge in Λ (LFR II p.358 l.5–8). The data of (1.3) and the field U_0 are regular with {#D.ε₁.2} ε₁ := C(M)R_kε_k, by the regularity of Sect. F (LFR II p.357 l.37–40), with C(M) ≥ C_X(M) of the a priori location below.
- {#4.44} *The nested problem.* For V′ on the bonds of Λ^{(k)} with δ_{G₀}(V′), U_{k,Z}(V′V_Λ) is the minimiser with data on all of Z. By LFR I Proposition 1 (p.194 l.37–48), V′ ↦ A(U_{k,Z}(V′V_Λ)) has exactly one critical orbit, a minimum, and U_0 = U_{k,Z}(V′₀V_Λ) at its minimiser V′₀ ((1.79), p.195 l.7; LFR II p.357 l.10–14). Here V_Λ denotes the data off Λ; LFR I's V_Λ is V′₀V_Λ, and LFR I's axial gauge in Λ^{(k)} is LFR II's G₀. So V′₀ minimises {#D.Φ(V′)} Φ(V′) := A(U_{k,Z}(V′V_Λ)). This is the point around which LFR II expands (p.356 l.29–30, by RG I (2.8)). Each run X has its own Φ^X, built on its own fine lattice, as a function of the same variables V′, with the minimiser V′^X₀. Define X on the bonds of Λ^{(k)} ∖ G₀ by V′^B₀ = e^{iX}V′^A₀, and {#D.Δ} Δ := ‖X‖₂.
- {#4.45} *The expansion at a minimum.* In the variables V′ = e^{iY}V′^X₀, RG I (2.8) (p.266 l.39–42) with ζ₀ ≡ 1 gives Φ^X(V′) = Φ^X(V′^X₀) + ⟨H_{1,k}Y, J_0⟩ + ½⟨H_{1,k}Y, Δ₁H_{1,k}Y⟩ + W^X(Y), with W^X of at least third order. The linear term vanishes by (1.4) (LFR II p.357 l.15–20). The form is ≥ κ_Λ‖Y‖₂², {#D.κ_Λ} κ_Λ := γ₀/(2d(100M)⁵), by (1.9) (p.358 l.13–16): the proof (1.7)–(1.8) replaces ζ₀ by 1 as one of its steps.
- {#4.46} *The remainder.* VAR Sect. G ((172)–(175), p.305) writes U_{k,Z}(e^{iY}V′^X₀V_Λ) = e^{iηℋ(Y)}U_0 as an analytic function of Y. Let {#D.P} P := {‖Y‖_∞ < 2C₁ε₁}. For Y ∈ P, H₁Y satisfies the bounds (103) (p.293 l.36–37) with {#D.C₁′} C₁′ := 4C₁, since |H₁Y|_{(−1)} and |∇H₁Y|_{(−2)} are ≤ B₀‖Y‖_∞ < 2B₀C₁ε₁ ≤ 8dLB₀C₁ε₁. So by the complex clause of Proposition 6 (p.295 l.49–p.296 l.2), 𝒜₁ is analytic on P, and so is ℋ, by (174) and the analyticity of HD (VAR Sect. C). For real Y ∈ P, (172) holds with C₁′, since |e^{iY} − 1| < 4C₁ε₁ for ε₁ small, and ℋ(Y) represents U_{k,Z}(e^{iY}V′^X₀V_Λ). Here ℋ = 𝒜₁ + H₁Y − HD(𝒜₁ + H₁Y) and 𝒜₁ is the solution of (175). VAR takes C₁ an absolute constant (p.305 l.44); a constant C₁(M) is used here, with ε₁ small depending on it, which is the condition (T-Λ) below (VAR's B₅ = 6B₁B₃C₁ then depends on M; it is not LFR I's geometric B₅). At the real background U_0, the operators H₁ and H decay at the rate δ₀ (PBG (3.133) and Theorem 3.12, with the rate renamed δ₀ on p.423 l.39–40), and so does 𝔊 (Theorem 3.13, p.426). The extra factor (L^jη)^{−1} or (L^{j′}η)^{−1} that p.422 l.32–33 adds for the H of the variational problem is harmless here, since the data lie on the layer of the scale k, the coarsest one, so a_j ≤ a_k. δV/δA′ in (175) is of at least second order, with the kernel form of (b) (*The kernel form of VAR Proposition 4.*, at complex arguments), and 𝒜₁ = −𝔊(δV/δA′)(𝒜₁ + H₁Y) by (175).
  - {#4.47} *The weighted bound.* Let {#D.w.2} w := e^{(δ₀/16)d(·,Λ)} ≥ 1, {#D.f_w} |f|_w := sup_yw(y)‖f‖_y for fields, and {#D.f_w,(−3)} |f|_{w,(−3)} := sup_yw(y)sup_{Δ(y)}a_{j(y)}³|f| for sources, with ‖·‖_y of (b). The triangle inequality (2.54) gives w(y)/w(y′) ≤ e^{(δ₀/16)d(y,y′)}. So the plain-source bound of (b) and its count give |𝔊f|_w ≤ 2B₀c_K|f|_{w,(−3)}. The lattice is finite, so |𝒜₁|_w < ∞, and |𝒜₁|_w ≤ 2B₀c_KC_Nc_tot(1/128)ε₃(|𝒜₁|_w + |H₁Y|_w) ≤ |H₁Y|_w when 4B₀c_KC_Nc_tot(1/128)ε₃ ≤ 1.
