Hence ‖ℋ(Y)‖_y ≤ C_ℋe^{−(δ₀/16)d(y,Λ)}‖Y‖_∞ on every block y, for Y ∈ P, with C_ℋ independent of C₁; the smallness conditions on CC₁ε₁ that this uses are part of (T-Λ).
  - {#4.48} *The bound on P.* The block densities of the action change by ≤ C(ε₁ + |ℋ|)|ℋ| per block, with |ℋ| the maximum of ‖ℋ‖ over the block and its neighbours, since plaquettes cross block boundaries: the first-order term is ⟨J₀, ℋ⟩ with |J₀| ≤ Cε₁a_j^{−3}, and the higher orders are ≤ C|ℋ|² when η|ℋ| is small. So |Φ^X(e^{iY}V′^X₀) − Φ^X(V′^X₀)| ≤ ½C_Φ(M)C₁²ε₁² on P (C₁ ≥ 1), and the same bound holds for |½⟨H_{1,k}Y, Δ₁H_{1,k}Y⟩| by Cauchy's estimate on the complex line through Y, since the linear term vanishes and the form is the second-order Taylor coefficient, with C_Φ(M) a constant of d, M, δ₀, B₀, and C_ℋ, enlarged by a fixed factor for this estimate. W^X vanishes to third order at 0 and is ≤ C_Φ(M)C₁²ε₁² on P, so Schwarz's lemma on the complex line through Y gives |W^X(Y)| ≤ C_Φ(M)C₁²ε₁²(‖Y‖_∞/(2C₁ε₁))³ ≤ (C_Φ(M)/(8C₁ε₁))‖Y‖_∞‖Y‖₂².
- {#4.49} *The growth.* So Φ^X(e^{iY}V′^X₀) − Φ^X(V′^X₀) ≥ (κ_Λ/2 − (C_Φ(M)/(8C₁ε₁))‖Y‖_∞)‖Y‖₂² ≥ (κ_Λ/4)‖Y‖₂² for real Y with ‖Y‖_∞ ≤ 2C₁κ_Λε₁/C_Φ(M) and ‖Y‖_∞ < 2C₁ε₁.
- {#4.50} *The a priori location.* In the axial gauge of G₀, |V′^X₀(b) − 1| < O(1)B₅M⁶ε_k on Λ^{(k)} in each run, by LFR I (1.83) (p.197 l.2–6, M^k(U_0) = V_Λ there). So ‖X‖_∞ ≤ C_X(M)ε_k, {#D.C_X(M)} C_X(M) := C·O(1)B₅M⁶, with LFR I's B₅. With {#D.C₁} C₁ := max(1, C_X(M)C_Φ(M)/κ_Λ), the growth applies at Y = X in run A and at Y = −X in run B, since V′^A₀ = e^{−iX}V′^B₀. The condition (T-Λ) on the coupling window, of the same kind as (T2-v) of the Cauchy note, is: ε₁ is below the smallness that VAR Sect. G needs for this C₁, which depends only on M and Bałaban's constants; the conditions of *The weighted bound.* and *The bound on P.*, 4B₀c_KC_Nc_tot(1/128)ε₃ ≤ 1, C_{HD}c_tot(1/128)ε₃ ≤ ½, ε₃ ≤ ¼a₃ for the kernel form, and the smallness of η‖ℋ‖ ≤ 2ηC_ℋC₁ε₁ that the block densities need, each of the form C·C₁(M)ε₁ ≤ c with c independent of k, K, ε, and the volume; and the smallness conditions on ε₁ of the alignment of §4(d), listed there (*The intermediate current and the estimate.*), at PBG's α₁ lowered to 16dLα₁ ≤ 1; and those of *The Current at the Multiscale Chain.* in (ii): (T-E), the conditions 2C_U(M)ε₁ ≤ α₁ and 4C₀ε₁ ≤ α₁ of its (I), and the condition on κ_W of its ΔJ_c.
- {#4.51} *The comparison.* Adding the two growth inequalities, (κ_Λ/2)Δ² ≤ [Φ^A(V′^B₀) − Φ^A(V′^A₀)] + [Φ^B(V′^A₀) − Φ^B(V′^B₀)] = D(V′^B₀) − D(V′^A₀), with {#D.D.2} D := Φ^A − Φ^B. Write D = Σ_yd_y over the scale-k blocks y of Z, {#D.d_y} d_y := [a_y(U^A) − a_y(MU^B)] + b_y(U^B), {#D.U^X} U^X := U^X_{k,Z}(V′V_Λ), and b_y the blocking artifact of (b). MU^B has the data of U^A, by the composition of the averagings. At fixed V′ the problem is that of (b), with the layers of the multiscale set 𝐁_k(Z) (LFR I (1.74)), whose finest layer is the history's, of spacing a_n ≤ a. By the bound ρ̄ of (b), |a_y(MU^B) − a_y(U^A)| ≤ Cε₁ρ̄ at first order per block, and |b_y| ≤ C_b(ε/a_n)ε₁², so |d_y| ≤ {#D.σ̄} σ̄ := C_σ(ε/a_n)^{1−ε₀}ε₁², {#D.C_σ} C_σ := C(2C_G(ε₀)c_K + C_b). This holds on the segment {#D.V′_t} V′_t := e^{itX}V′^A₀, whose data are regular with 2ε₁, since ‖X‖_∞ ≤ C_X(M)ε_k ≤ ε₁/4, with ε_k the larger of the two runs' values and C(M) ≥ 4C_X(M). Along it, a data change on Λ moves each of U^A, U^B, and MU^B at y by ≤ B₀Σ_{b∈Λ}e^{−δ₀d(y,b)}|X(b)|, by (3.133) for each run's H at its real regular configuration, with M local; and the block densities have derivatives ≤ Cε₁ per unit field. So |d_y(V′^B₀) − d_y(V′^A₀)| ≤ C_Lε₁K_Λ(y)Δ, with {#D.K_Λ(y)} K_Λ(y) := Σ_{b∈Λ}e^{−δ₀d(y,b)}. Since min(u, v) ≤ (uv)^{1/2}, D(V′^B₀) − D(V′^A₀) ≤ Σ_ymin(2σ̄, C_Lε₁K_Λ(y)Δ) ≤ (2σ̄C_Lε₁Δ)^{1/2}c′_Λ, since c′_Λ ≥ Σ_bΣ_ye^{−(δ₀/2)d(y,b)} ≥ Σ_yK_Λ(y)^{1/2}. Hence Δ^{3/2} ≤ (2c′_Λ/κ_Λ)(2σ̄C_Lε₁)^{1/2}, i.e. Δ ≤ C_Δ(M)(ε/a_n)^{(1−ε₀)/3}ε₁, with {#D.C_Δ(M)} C_Δ(M) := (2c′_Λ/κ_Λ)^{2/3}(2C_σC_L)^{1/3}.
- {#4.52} *The gauge of the data.* By (1.50) and (1.25) (p.362 l.22–27), the data of U″_k on Λ ∩ Ω″^{∼2}_{h+1} are M^·(U^{(AL)}_0) = (M^·U_0)^{ū₀}: the averages of 𝐁₁ = 𝐁″_k(Z) ∪ 𝐁_h(Ω″^{∼2}_{h+1}) (p.361 l.36–38), at the shared scales k and h, transformed by ū₀, which is constant on the blocks and equal at their centres to the u₀ of LFR I (1.86). The expressions of the integral are invariant under the compensating gauge transformations of V_h on ∂⁺(Z′^∼_h)^{(h)} and of V′ (LFR I p.197 l.36–40). At fixed V_k these are changes of variables of the Haar measure, and u₀ and the gauge of U_0 at the shared centres are functions of V_k. So each run's integral is unchanged when both runs use run A's ū₀ and one gauge of U_0 at the shared centres, that of the comparison of the Cauchy note's §9.8. The two runs' data are then at distance |M^·U^A_0 − M^·U^B_0|, since a common gauge transformation preserves |·|. Every run-B quantity evaluated there is a run-B integrand at transformed variables, so Bałaban's run-B bounds and analyticity domains apply to it.
- {#4.53} *The data difference.* On Λ^{(k)}, M^k(U^X_0) = V′^X₀, so the difference is e^{iX}, ≤ C‖X‖_∞ ≤ CΔ. At a scale m of 𝐁″_k(Z) between h and k (Λ ⊃ Z″_k ⊃ ⋯ ⊃ Z″_{h+1}, LFR I p.195 l.42), M^m(U^A_0) − M^m(MU^B_0) = [M^mU^A(V′^A₀) − M^mU^A(V′^B₀)] + [M^mU^A(V′^B₀) − M^mMU^B(V′^B₀)], with M^m(MU^B) = M^m(U^B) by the composition of the averagings. The first bracket is ≤ B₀c_K‖X‖_∞ by (3.133) and the count of (b). The second is ≤ Cρ̄ ≤ 2CC_G(ε₀)c_K(ε/a_n)^{1−ε₀}ε₁ by the bound ρ̄ of (b) at equal data, since a scale-m block average of a field difference ≤ ρ̄/a_m has path length ≤ a_m. So the data difference is ≤ C′_Δ(M)(ε/a_n)^{(1−ε₀)/3}ε₁ per data point of Λ ∩ Ω″^{∼2}_{h+1}, at every scale.
- {#4.54} *The propagation.* The data enter U″_k = U_{𝐁″_k}(·) through the data derivative of the multiscale set 𝐁″_k, the H₁-type operator of (1.54) (H″_{1,k}Q̃(η𝐀₀)), which decays at the rate δ₀ at a regular background (PBG Theorem 3.12). The action A(w, U″_k) of (1.70), w = ζ₁/(g″)², changes at first order by ⟨J_w, H″_{1,k}δD⟩, with |J_w| ≤ C sup|w|ε₁/a_m³ per point as in (b), and at second order by ≤ C sup|w||δD|² per data point. Each data point contributes ≤ C sup|w|ε₁|δD| at its own scale, summed with the decay by the count of (b). The change of A(ζ₀, U_0) in (1.10) at fixed data is (b). Its change from V′^A₀ to V′^B₀ in run A has the linear term (1.5), which is localised by 1 − ζ₀ as in (1.6), plus a quadratic term ≤ C(M)Δ². Both are ≤ C(M)ε₁Δ, with Δ ≤ C(M)ε₁ (the a priori location).
- {#4.55} *The result.* Per data point of Λ ∩ Ω″^{∼2}_{h+1} at its own scale, and per bond of Λ^{(k)}, the change of these actions is ≤ C_A(M)g_{j}^{−2}(ε/a_n)^{(1−ε₀)/3}ε₁², with a_n = εL^n the history's finest spacing. In a history with n > k/8, K − j ≤ 7k/8 + j(C), so g_j^{−2}ε₁² = C(M)²R_k²p₀(g_k)²g_k²/g_j² ≤ C(M)²(1 + β₀)²(k − j + 1)R_k²p₀(g_k)² by CRE (2.6), with g_k^{−2} ≥ ḡ^{−2}: a power of log(k + j(C) + ḡ^{−2}) times k < 8n, polylogarithmic times linear in n and independent of K. Since θ̃ ≥ L^{−(1−ε₀)/4} (the Cauchy note's §8.7), L^{−(1−ε₀)n/3} ≤ θ̃^nL^{−(1−ε₀)n/12} absorbs it, so the change is ≤ C_hθ̃^n per point of the history, with C_h a constant of M, ε₀, ḡ, j(C), and Bałaban's constants. This is the birth-scale form of (LF).

{#4.56} (d) *The forms and the functions of the configurations at the step of the R-operation (derived, with the points (3), (6), and (7) of (LF-A) not reviewed, and with the gauge-fixing part of the Cauchy note's §10.4; the π-part of β with multiscale data, its diagonal value and its source form, and the twist term are derived, not reviewed).* The notation is that of (b): a_j = εL^j, j(x) the layer of x, a_n the history's finest spacing. The Hölder exponent of PBG (3.133) is fixed at {#D.γ_d} γ_d := (1 + ε₀)/2 throughout (d). In (d), k is Bałaban's index of LFR II §1, the step of the R-operation, which the Cauchy note's §8.6 calls j. It is at most the stopping scale, so the bounds k < 8n and n ≥ k/2 − 1, which §1 states for the stopping scale, hold for it as well.
- {#4.57} *The objects.* H″_{1,k,Z} is the linear term of 𝐇″_{k,Z}(g_kB) in (1.19)–(1.20) (LFR II p.360 l.44–50, p.361 l.3–8): the data derivative at B = 0 of the minimiser U″_{k,Z} of the multiscale determining set 𝐁″_k(Z), at the background U^0_{k,Z}. Bałaban writes the quadratic term ½g_k²⟨H″B, Δ₁(ζ)H″B⟩ of (1.20) as the form (1.21), Σ_pη⁴ζ(x(p))|(DH″B)(p)|², which (1.70) keeps, plus a small form bounded by O(1)B₃⁵B₅M^{5+d}A₁²p₁²(g_k)R_k^{d+2}ε_k (p.361 l.14–28). H_{1,k} of (1.2) is the data derivative of U_{k,Z}(V′V_Λ) in V′ = exp ig_kB′ on Λ^{(k)}, at the background U_0; the form of (1.2) carries the weight ζ₀ (p.356 l.31–p.357 l.8). On the supports of the cutoffs, |g_kB| < δ′_k by χ′ (p.360 l.41–43) and |B′| < M₀g_k^{−1}ε_k (p.356 l.37). So the fields are ≤ {#D.b_k} b_k := max(A₁p₁(g_k), M₀p₀(g_k)) per point of 𝐁₀ or of Λ^{(k)}. These are Bałaban's dimensionless data: B on a layer j′ is the variable of the constraint L^{j′}ηQ_{j′}A = B of PBG (3.109)–(3.110), so its lift carries the factor (L^{j′}η)^{−1} = a_{j′}^{−1} relative to (3.133) (PBG p.422 l.32–33). Bałaban's bounds of these forms are sums over 𝐁₀, with |𝐁₀| ≤ (100MR_k)^dN² (p.361 l.11–13 and l.19–20), and (d) compares the two runs per point of 𝐁₀ or of Λ^{(k)}.
- {#4.58} *The lifts and the chain rule.* VAR's constraint (3) (p.278 l.11–13) is the plain average, Ū^j = V on Λ_j, while PBG's lift belongs to the double bar. In each run the data derivative of a VAR minimiser with a multiscale determining set, in VAR's gauge (153), is H₁(1 + Ξ), with PBG's H₁ = G₁Q*(QG₁Q*)^{−1} of (3.129) for that set, Q PBG's linearised multiscale double bar, and Ξ the interface twist of *The interface twist.* below (derived there), each run with its own Ξ at its own data. So the lifts of (1.2) and (1.21) are H₁B̃, with the twisted data {#D.B̃} B̃ := (1 + Ξ)B, and |B̃| ≤ (1 + 2dL)|B| per point. PBG Theorem 3.12 gives it (3.132)–(3.133) between any two layers (p.422 l.17–30, p.423 l.30–36): for x ∈ Δ(y), y ∈ Λ_j, y′ ∈ Λ_{j′}, |∇H₁(x, y′)| ≤ O(1)a_j^{−1}a_{j′}^{−d}e^{−½δ₁d(y,y′)}, and ‖ζ′∇H₁(·, y′)‖_β ≤ O(1)(‖ζ′‖^ξ_β + |ζ′|)a_j^{−1−β}a_{j′}^{−d}e^{−½δ₁d(y,y′)} for ζ′ ∈ C₀^∞(Δ̃(y)). So the Hölder bound is at the scale of the receiving layer; in run B, PBG's L^jη is L^{j+1}(ε/L) = a_j at the shared scale j. The proof of (10.2) uses only the positivity of G₁^{−1} and the surjectivity of Q, so H₁B minimises ⟨A, (Δ₁ + DRD*)A⟩ under QA = B for the multiscale problem too. Every layer of run B's set lies at a shared scale j ≥ k/2 − 1 ≥ 1, where its averaging is d(M^{j+1}) = d(M^j)∘dM.
  {#4.58-1} So at aligned backgrounds Q^B = Q^AQ₁ layer by layer, for the double bar by (B4) of the Cauchy note's §10.1 with Q₁ = Q̄₁(U^B), and for the plain averaging by composition with Q₁ = Q₁^{pl} = dM(U^B). Hence (10.4)–(10.5) and the characterisation of E hold with the multiscale double bar Q and H₁. The characterisation identifies E with the Green operator on ker Q^A at run A's pair, {#D.G₁^Q.2} G₁^Q := G₁ − G₁Q*(QG₁Q*)^{−1}QG₁ = (I − H₁Q)G₁: for ψ ∈ ker Q^A the double-bar lift ℒ of §10.4 gives ℒψ ∈ ker Q^B and Q₁ℒψ = ψ, so ⟨ψ, G_A^{−1}E⟩ = β(ℒψ, 𝒜^B), and QG₁^Q = 0 and ⟨ψ, G₁^{−1}G₁^Qs⟩ = ⟨ψ, s⟩ for ψ ∈ ker Q give E₀ = G₁^Qs with {#D.⟨ψ,s⟩} ⟨ψ, s⟩ := β(ℒψ, 𝒜^B), {#D.E₀} E₀ := (I − H₁Q)E the part of E in ker Q^A, which is all of E at equal twisted data (*The terms in E.*). The bounds of G₁^Q follow from (3.132) for G₁ and (3.133) for H₁, with Q local, as in the Cauchy note's §10.4. The J-term paragraph of §10.4 holds by *The intermediate current and the estimate.* below.
- {#4.59} *The alignment.* In the common gauge of (c) ("The gauge of the data"), each run's background is compared with the other run's averaged one: U^{0,A}_{k,Z} against MU^{0,B}_{k,Z}, and U^A_0 against MU^B_0. In each pair U^A and U^B minimise the action under the multiscale constraints of their determining sets, each with its own data, and U^A = e^{iεA}Ũ, {#D.Ũ.2} Ũ := MU^B, with a_{j(x)}|A(x)| + a_{j(x)}²|∇A(x)| ≤ {#D.d̄} d̄ := 2ρ̄ + 2B₀c_KC′_Δ(M)(ε/a_n)^{(1−ε₀)/3}ε₁ ≤ C_U(M)(ε/a_n)^{(1−ε₀)/3}ε₁, {#D.C_U(M)} C_U(M) := 4C_G(ε₀)c″_K + 2B₀c_KC′_Δ(M) + C_T, with C_T the strip constant of (iv), *The strips at ∂□₀.*, used only at the composites and the representation configurations. The first term is (b) at equal data, where ρ̄ bounds the displacement A′* of VAR (112) itself; the second is the data difference of (c), propagated by (3.133) with the count of (b). The factors 2 cover the composition of the two displacements: its Baker–Campbell–Hausdorff term is ≤ (ε/a_j)(a_j|X|)(a_j|Y|)/a_j for displacements X and Y, and the change of background in the covariant gradient is of the same order, so both are at most the sum of the two bounds when C_U(M)ε₁ ≤ 1. Throughout (d), ε₁ is the larger of the ε₁ of §1 and the C(M)R_kε_k of (c). The forms of (1.2) and (1.21) depend on the current through Δ₁ and H₁, and the currents of U^A and Ũ differ by second differences of A, which d̄ does not bound. So the argument of the Cauchy note's §10.3 is run for the multiscale problem, with d = 4 and PBG's common rate δ₀ (p.423 l.39–40).
  - {#4.60} *The pair class.* 𝒟̄ is the set of pairs (𝐔, 𝐉) with 𝐔 satisfying PBG (3.37) (p.396), which is stated layer by layer (|A′| < α₁a_j^{−1} and |∇A′| < α₁a_j^{−2} on Ω_j), and |𝐉(x)| < α_Ja_{j(x)}^{−3}, {#D.α_J} α_J := Mα₀. PBG's series for G and G₁ use the current through |J| in (3.131) (p.421 l.38–42), which is this bound, and through |(H*J)(b)| ≤ O(1)Mα₀(L^jη)^{−3} for b ∈ Λ_j (p.422 l.50) in (3.137), which (3.133) gives from this bound with the cross-layer count of (b): the layer j′ enters H*J at b ∈ Λ_j with the factor (a_{j′}/a_j)^{d−3}e^{−½δ₁d(·,·)}, which the row sums c_K pay. So the pair-class paragraph of the Cauchy note's §10.3 holds for the multiscale problem: Δ_{(𝐔,𝐉)} and its propagators are analytic on 𝒟̄ and obey the multiscale (3.132)–(3.133) and Theorems 3.10–3.12, and PBG's (3.38) is not needed.
  - {#4.61} *The interface twist.* By PRT2 (2.3) (p.224), Λ_j = Ω_j^{(j)}∖Ω_{j+1}^{(j)} "for the sets of sites and the sets of bonds", where Ω also denotes "the set of bonds ∪_{x∈Ω}st(x)". So the bonds of Λ_j include the interface bonds {#D.S_j} S_j := {⟨x, x′⟩ ∈ Λ_j : x ∉ Ω_j^{(j)}, x′ ∈ Ω_j^{(j)}}, whose outer endpoint x is a site of the finer layer j − 1; this is the case "x ∈ Λ′_{j−1}, x′ ∈ Λ′_j" of VAR (154). PRT1 uses the corner blocks B(x) = {x₁ : x_μ ≤ x₁,μ < x_μ + L} (p.018 l.41), with contours Γ_{x,x₁} inside B(x) (p.018 l.44). Since Ω_j is a union of such blocks (PRT2 (2.2), first line), B(x) ∩ Ω_j = ∅ for x ∉ Ω_j^{(j)}, so the bonds of the contours of B(x) belong to Λ_{j−1}. VAR states, in the gauge (153) (p.301 l.62–64, p.302 l.1–18): "Ū̄^j_1(x,x′) = V″(x,x′) for ⟨x,x′⟩ ∈ Λ′_j, x,x′ ∈ Λ′_j," and "Ū̄^j_1(x,x′) = exp[−iΣ_{x₁∈B(x)}L^{−d}(1/i)log V″(Γ_{x,x₁})]V″(x,x′) for ⟨x,x′⟩ ∈ Λ′_j, x ∈ Λ′_{j−1}, x′ ∈ Λ′_j, (154) by Eqs. (1.31) in [6]. If we denote by V₁ the configuration on the right-hand sides of (154), then V₁ = e^{iB} with |B| < 18d²L³Mε₀, (155) for c₁ sufficiently small, and the equalities (154) can be written as Q_j(ηA) = B on Λ′_j, j = 0, 1, …, k, or simply Q(ηA) = B. (156)" Here V″ is the plain data, V″ = Ū′^j_k on Λ′_j by (149), and Ū̄ is the double bar. The exponent in (154) is the factor of level j, at the site x, of the gauge transformation v of CMP 98 (97) and (160): by (162) it is the mean over x₁ ∈ B(x) of the logarithms of the transported contour holonomies.
    - {#4.62} The twist. The chart is the relative one of PBG and CMP 98 (159)–(162), at the run's own configuration U as the base: plain data V″ = e^{iY}V″(U) on the bonds of the layers. In it the right side of (154) is e^{i(1 + Ξ)Y + O(|Y|²)} times its value at Y = 0, where Ξ, the interface twist, is the derivative at Y = 0 of the level-j factor of (154), Ad of the background transports composed with dexp^{−1} at the background holonomies: {#D.(ΞY)(x,x′)} (ΞY)(x, x′) := −Σ_{x₁∈B(x)}L^{−d}d[(1/i)log V″(Γ_{x,x₁})][Y] for ⟨x, x′⟩ ∈ S_j, and {#D.ΞY} ΞY := 0 on the other bonds. Along a contour the derivative is Σ_{b′∈Γ}dexp^{−1}_h∘Ad(g_{b′})[Y(b′)], with h the logarithm of the holonomy and g_{b′} the partial holonomy. A contour has at most d(L − 1) bonds, and in the operator norm of a faithful unitary representation |[X, Y]| ≤ 2|X||Y|, so ‖Ad(e^{X₁}⋯e^{X_m})‖ ≤ e^{2Σ|X_i|}. So for 16dLα₁ ≤ 1 and data, real or complex, with |Y| < α₁, Ad(g_{b′}) ≤ e^{2dLα₁} ≤ e^{1/4}; the background factors are unitary, so they add nothing to Ad.
      {#4.62-1} The holonomy also contains the background: its exponents are the |Y(b′)| < α₁ and the background angles, ≤ 18dL²Mε₀ per bond by VAR (151) (|V″ − 1| < 9dL²Mε₀), over at most dL bonds, so they add up to ≤ dLα₁ + 18d²L³Mε₀ ≤ 1/16 + 1/36 < 1/4 under 648d²L³Mε₀ ≤ 1 (the condition of *Its size.* below), and |h| ≤ |E|/(1 − |E|) ≤ 0.105 with |E| ≤ e^s − 1, s ≤ 0.0903 the exponent sum. Then ‖ad_h‖ ≤ 0.21, and dexp^{−1}_h = Σ_n(B_n/n!)ad_h^n, B_n the Bernoulli numbers, is ≤ 1 + 0.105 + 0.004 ≤ e^{1/4}. Their product is ≤ e^{1/2} ≤ 2. Hence |(ΞY)(b)| ≤ 2dL max|Y| over the bonds of B(x) for b ∈ S_j at x, and the entries obey |Ξ(b, b′)| ≤ 2L^{−d}N(b′) ≤ 2, with N(b′) ≤ L^d the number of contours of B(x) through b′. A bond b′ of Λ_{j−1} lies in at most one block B(x), and at most 2d bonds of S_j have the endpoint x. On these sets, with |log g| ≤ 0.105, Ad has the Lipschitz constant 2e^{0.21} ≤ 2e^{1/4} in the logarithm of its argument and dexp^{−1} the constant 2, and the logarithms of the partial holonomies and of the holonomy, whose derivative is dexp^{−1}_h∘Ad(g)∘dexp, move by at most e^{0.4}dL max|Y_A − Y_B| between two runs with data Y_A and Y_B. So each term of a contour moves by at most (2e^{1/4} + 2e^{1/2})e^{0.4}dL max|Y_A − Y_B| ≤ 9.2dL max|Y_A − Y_B|, and |Ξ_A(b, b′) − Ξ_B(b, b′)| ≤ 12dLL^{−d}N(b′)max|Y_A − Y_B|, the maximum over the bonds of B(x).
      {#4.62-2} These bounds are per bond, hence uniform in the volume.
    - {#4.63} Ξ² = 0. Ξ writes on the bonds of S_j, which lie within a_j of Ω_j^c, and reads the bonds of Λ_{j−1}. At the next interface Ξ reads bonds of Λ_j in the blocks B(z) of the outer endpoints z of S_{j+1}; these lie within (d + 1)a_{j+1} of Ω_{j+1}. So no bond of S_j is read by Ξ if every layer is wider than (d + 1)L + 1 in its own units. For a sequence satisfying PRT2 (2.2), (L^jη)^{−1}dist(Ω_j^c, Ω_{j+1}) > RM, and in d = 4 RM ≥ 12L covers the condition. For 𝐁″_k and the joins, whose layers are at least M or LM₁ wide in their own units (*The joins.* in §9, with its middle layers), the condition holds for M₁ ≥ 6. Two interface corrections therefore cannot chain: Ξ² = 0 and (1 + Ξ)^{−1} = 1 − Ξ.
    - {#4.64} The two averagings. Let 𝐐^{pl}(U) be the linearised plain multiscale averaging of VAR (3), layer by layer, and Q_db(U) PBG's linearised multiscale double bar: on each layer the double bar of (B1) and (B4) of the Cauchy note's §10.1, and on S_j the double bar (154). By (B1) on each layer and (154) on S_j, for every X,

- {#4.131} *The π-part of β for multiscale data (derived, not reviewed).* Notation as in the Cauchy note's *The π-Part of β.* (its #C10.4.98–#C10.4.101) and *The Gauge-Fixing Part of β.* (#C10.4.63–#C10.4.86), at d = 4, with {#D.ν.3} ν := ν_π = 𝒬′*λ^B, {#D.ℓ.2} ℓ := a_j at an interface site of the layer j, τ̂_n for τ̂, and {#D.𝔰} 𝔰 := σ_ka_j^{−2}, as for the gauge-fixing sources above.

In run X, the bracket of (3.120) and the term Q_Xc_X of (B5) cancel as in the Cauchy note's two bullets, and the term −c̄(Q′_Xμ_A, Q_XA) of (B5) vanishes by Q′_Xμ_A = 0. The gauge factor w of (B5) composes as the double bar does ((B4), CMP 98 (90)–(92)): run B's w is run A's w about MU^B, applied to the gauge parameter (1/i)log w₁ = Q′₁λ + q₁(λ, 𝒜) + … of the one-step factor w₁ and to the field Q₁𝒜. Its bilinear part gives q_B(λ, 𝒜) = q_A(Q′₁λ, Q₁𝒜) + Q′_Aq₁(λ, 𝒜). The first order of (B5) in λ gives Q₁D_Bλ = D_AQ′₁λ, so Q₁P_B𝒜 = Q₁𝒜 − D_AQ′₁μ^B. With {#D.δμ} δμ := Q′₁μ^B − μ^A and bilinearity,

  - {#4.135} The bound of q. The one-step factor is v₁(U₁^u)^{−1}·u(y)·v₁(U₁) with v₁(U₁)(y) = (R_{0,y}U₁)‾^{−1} of CMP 98 (87) and (89) at one step: the average over x ∈ B(y) of the logarithms of the holonomies h(x) of U₁U₀^{−1} along Γ_{y,x}, transported by the real background, each path having at most dL fine bonds of length η = ε/L. Under u = e^{iλ}, h(x) becomes u(y)h(x)u_x^{−1}, with u_x the transported u(x). The averages are linear in the logarithms, so the bilinear part of (1/i)log w₁ in (λ, A) consists only of the second-order Baker–Campbell–Hausdorff terms ½[X, Y] of the compositions: the two products u(y)h(x)u_x^{−1} and the product of the three factors of w₁. Each such term pairs one value of λ on B(y) with a sum of at most dL values of ηA on the paths, and |[X, Y]| ≤ c_G|X||Y|. At most four such terms occur, so |q₁(λ, A)(y)| ≤ c_qε sup_{B(y)}|λ| sup|A|, {#D.c_q} c_q := 4dc_G, the second supremum over the bonds of the paths. Iterating the composition over the scales m < j, with |Q′| ≤ 1 and |Q₁A| ≤ sup|A| (averages), gives |q_A(λ, A)| ≤ Σ_{m<j}c_qL^mε sup|λ| sup|A| ≤ 2c_qa_j sup|λ| sup|A|, the suprema over the block of the scale j.

  - {#4.139} The pairing. The multiplier is PBG's double-bar one, Q_db*ν = 𝐉, so ν = R₀*J = (1 − Ξ)*λ (*The two averagings.*). At a coarse interface site the weighted condition is a_{j−1}^dD*λ_{j−1} + a_j^dD*λ_j = 0, so |D*λ_j| ≤ L^{−d}·2d|λ_{j−1}|/a_{j−1} ≤ 2dL^{4−d}B̄_λε₁a_j^{−4}, and the fine layer's own divergence D*λ_{j−1}, paired with its measure, contributes the same amount per coarse site; together 4dL^{4−d}B̄_λε₁a_j^{−4}.   - {#4.140} *The π-part in the pairings (derived, not reviewed).* π_A and π_B are symmetric bilinear forms, and μ_A, P_XA, and δμ are linear in the field, so {#D.β_π(ℱ,𝒜)} β_π(ℱ, 𝒜) := π_A(Q₁ℱ, Q₁𝒜) − π_B(ℱ, 𝒜) = ⟨Θ(ℱ, 𝒜), D̄*ν⟩ with Θ(ℱ, 𝒜) the polarisation of Θ, a sum of terms q_A(X, Y) and Q′_Aq₁(X, Y) in which one argument is linear in ℱ and the other in {#D.𝒜} 𝒜 := 𝒜^B.
    - {#4.141} The polarised bound. The bound of q is sup to sup, and (G1), (G2), the Cauchy note's #C10.4.86, (3.42), and (3.44) bound μ_ℱ, δμ_ℱ, D_Aμ_ℱ, and P_Bℱ for any field ℱ as they bound them for 𝒜. For a field X let ψ_X ∈ ker Q^A solve ⟨φ, G₁^{−1}ψ_X⟩ = ⟨φ, WX⟩ for φ ∈ ker Q^A, with W the operator of F_w^A, so ψ_X = G₁^Q(WX). The entry G₁^QD* of (3.42), with B₀ + 2c_δ′B₀² in place of B₀, bounds a_j|ψ_X|. The gradient a_j²|∇ψ_X| needs the entry ∇G₁^QD*, which (3.42) does not list; (3.44) gives it with the Hölder norm of wDX, bounded by the lattice Hölder bound 3(a_j/ε)^{β′} times its supremum, as for ∇δμ. With the row sums c_K and (3.133) for ℒ this gives σ_k(ℒψ_X) ≤ C_ψ(β′)(a_j/ε)^{β′}Σ_ye^{−½δ₀d(·,y)}‖X‖_y, C_ψ(β′) a constant of B₀, B₀′(β′), c_δ′, c_K, C₀, and C_ζ. At β′ = ε₀/16 the factor (a_j/ε)^{β′} ≤ L^{j(C)ε₀/16}(a_n/ε)^{ε₀/2} is absorbed as in *The pairing.*, with {#D.C_ψ} C_ψ := L^{j(C)ε₀/16}C_ψ(ε₀/16). So |F_w^A(E₀^π, X)| ≤ 2d²C_ψC_π(ε/a_n)^{(1−ε₀)/2}ε₁σ_k times the decay-weighted supremum of X, per interface point, for X = Q₁𝒜^B and for the parts E_Ξ and E₀ − E₀^π of E, which are bounded pointwise above.
    - {#4.143} *The π–π term (derived, not reviewed).* The pairing route bounds F_w^A(E₀^π, E₀^π) once E₀^π has a pointwise bound with any constant: X = E₀^π in the last display. That bound comes from the source form of β_π. The source is spread at the scale of the cells, because the composition dilutes the weight of each block centre.
      - {#4.144} The source. β_π(ℱ, 𝒜) is linear in ℱ, so β_π(ℱ, 𝒜) = ⟨s_π, ℱ⟩_B for a field s_π of run B, and E₀^π = G₁^Qℒ*s_π, since ⟨ψ, G₁^{−1}E₀^π⟩ = ⟨ℒψ, s_π⟩_B for ψ ∈ ker Q^A and G₁^Q = G₁ − G₁Q*(QG₁Q*)^{−1}QG₁ is the symmetric Green operator on ker Q^A. Each term of Θ(ℱ, 𝒜) reads ℱ in one slot of q_A or q₁: in the field slot raw, through Q₁ℱ, or through P_Bℱ = ℱ − D_Bμ_ℱ, or in the parameter slot through μ_ℱ, δμ_ℱ, or Q′₁μ_ℱ, with the other slot a field of 𝒜, at most O(1)σ_ka_j^{−1}, or a parameter of 𝒜, at most O(1)σ_k (*The other factors.*, *δμ.*).
      - {#4.145} The weights. In the composition of *The bound of q.*, the step of the scale m reads the m-fold averages Q′^{(m)}λ and Q^{(m)}A at the sites and bonds of the scale m, and its output is carried to the scale j by the averages Q′ of the scales m + 1, …, j − 1. So each of the (a_j/a_m)⁴ blocks of the scale m in a cell of the scale j carries the weight (a_m/a_j)⁴. Within one block, q₁ pairs the parameter at the centre and at the points x of the block with the transported path sums of at most dL bonds of the scale m, and a bond lies on at most all L^d paths of its block, so its coefficient is at most a_m/L times the parameter, while the mean over the dL^d bonds of the block is a_mL^{−d} times it. The coefficient of a bond therefore exceeds the block mean by at most L^{d−1}. A Q^{(m)} average or a Q′^{(m)} average is an average over a block of the scale m with bounded weights, so its transpose spreads a coefficient over that block. With the measure a_j⁴ of the interface site and |D̄*ν| ≤ c_νB̄_λε₁a_j^{−4} per coarse cell (*The pairing.*), the field-slot part of s_π therefore has, on every bond of the cell, the density at most c_qL^{d−1}c_νB̄_λε₁Σ_{m<j}a_m a_j^{−4}|λ| ≤ 2c_qL^{d−1}c_νB̄_λε₁a_j^{−3}|λ|, |λ| the parameter in the other slot. The parameter-slot part is a transpose T*n of an operator T ∈ {μ_·, δμ_·, Q′₁μ_·} applied to a scalar density n with |n| ≤ 2c_qL^dc_νB̄_λε₁a_j^{−4}σ_k (the parameter is read at the run-A points of the cell, a sublattice of run B's points, whence L^d in place of L^{d−1}). On the layer j − 1 the same holds with the factor L of *The pairing.*.
      - {#4.146} The gradient terms. The field-slot entries D_Bμ_ℱ, D_Aμ_ℱ, and D_Aδμ_ℱ are covariant differences of parameters. At the scale m, Q^{(m)}D_A = D_{(m)}Q′^{(m)} by the first order of (B5) iterated (Q₁D_Bλ = D_AQ′₁λ), and a transported path sum of a covariant difference telescopes to the difference of the transported end values. So these entries are parameter-slot reads at the two ends of each path, at most two per path, without a derivative: the step of the scale m contributes at most 2c_q|λ| times the end values, with no geometric factor a_m/a_j, and the sum over m < j gives the factor j. Their part of s_π is T*n with |n| ≤ 4c_qjL^dc_νB̄_λε₁a_j^{−4}σ_k.
      - {#4.147} The transposes. μ_ℱ = G′_Br_B(ℱ) and δμ_ℱ = −𝔠(r_B(ℱ)) − G′_Aδr(ℱ) are products of G′_X, R_X = 1 − P_X, Q′_X, Q′_X*, D_X, D_X*, Q₁, and the averages of 𝔠 and *The Defects.* G′_X and R_X = 1 − G′_XQ′_X*K_X^{−1}Q′_XG′_X (the Cauchy note's #C10.4.65) are symmetric, and, once R_X is expanded, every derivative in these products stands next to a G′ (f_X = D_X*ℱ, and the forms G′_AD_A* and D_AG′_A of 𝔠). So T* is a product of the same factors in the reverse order, with D and D*, Q′ and Q′* exchanged, and its sup bound is a product of the entries G′D* and DG′ of (3.42) and of the averages' bounds, |T*n| ≤ c_Ta_j sup|n|, with c_T a polynomial in B_G, d, and C_tr. The factor τ̂ of (G1)–(G3) comes from the regularity of the argument and is not used here.
      - {#4.148} The bound. So |s_π(x)| ≤ c_s(1 + j)ε₁a_j^{−3}σ_k e^{−½δ₀d(x, I)}, I the interface, with the layer factors of (3.42), {#D.c_s} c_s := 4c_qL^{d+1}c_νB̄_λ(B_G(c_𝔠c_{g2} + 2c_{g6}) + c_T) times the multiplicities of the terms, with c_𝔠 of *The Commutator.* for the 𝔠-part of δμ, as in c_μ, and with c_T including c_𝔠; the tail comes from G′ and its transpose in T*n and in the telescoped entries, and the row sums c_K below absorb it. ℒ* = I* + (1 − Q₁I)*(Q₁Q₁*)^{−1}Q₁ is sup-bounded with the exponential tail at the rate δ_Q, by c_ℒ*. The entries G₁^Q and ∇G₁^Q of (3.42), with B₀ + 2c_δ′B₀² in place of B₀, and the row sums c_K give a_{j(x)}|E₀^π(x)| + a_{j(x)}²|∇E₀^π(x)| ≤ x_π(1 + j)ε₁σ_k, {#D.x_π} x_π := 2(B₀ + 2c_δ′B₀²)c_Kc_ℒ*c_s, at the points x within the decay of the interface, the layer factors a_{j(x)}/a_j taken by (3.132)–(3.133) as in *The pairings.*

  - {#4.150} For f^A two further terms are of relative size ε₁. The curvature terms of PBG (3.10), with |F| ≤ 2C₀ε₁/a_j² at Ũ, add at most 2(1 + d²)C₀ε₁ times these bounds. The constraint term is ⟨C_A^{(2)}[X, Y], ν^B⟩ = ⟨H^AC_A^{(2)}[X, Y], J′⟩, by J′ = Q_db(Ũ)*ν^B, with |C_A^{(2)}[X, Y]| ≤ C₂a_{j′}|X||Y| at a point of the layer j′ (VAR (44) at the block scale), H^A bounded by (3.133) as for 𝒜 above, and a_j³|J′| ≤ B̄_Jε₁. With the row sums c_K it adds at most 4dB₀c_KC₂B̄_Jε₁ times these bounds. So the bounds hold for f^A with the factor 1 + c_bfε₁, {#D.c_bf} c_bf := 2(1 + d²)C₀ + 4dB₀c_KC₂B̄_J; the name c_bf keeps it apart from the Cauchy note's c_f.
- {#4.151} *The complementary-weight parts.* The parts −2⟨𝒜₂, J(1 − ζ₀)⟩ of the form of (1.2) and −2⟨𝒜₂, J(1 − ζ)⟩ of the small form of (1.20) need no comparison of their own. The form of (1.2) enters the main proof only through the denominator d of (1.1), and the small form of (1.20) only through the sum 𝐂_k of LFR II p.369 l.2–7. Both are compared below through the weighted actions of (b) and (c), with no use of 𝒜₂, E₂, or the remainders V(ζ₀, ·) and V(ζ, ·), so bounds of 𝒜₂ and E₂ are not needed. The comparison of d and of 𝐂_k as a whole is derived. LFR II then localises 𝐂_k and re-sums its pieces into V(X^∼) and V(Y) (p.373 l.10–17, (1.59)–(1.64), (1.68)), and the comparison of these pieces, *The Localised Pieces of 𝐂_k* below, is derived, not reviewed. The comparisons are at real configurations and at equal shared variables and couplings, as in (b)–(d), except in the item on the couplings.
  - {#4.152} *The denominator.* By (1.1) (p.356 l.19–20), d = ∫δ_{G₀}(V′)χ exp[−g_k^{−2}A(ζ₀, U_{k,Z}(V′V_Λ))] dV′|_Λ, where Bałaban's V_Λ carries on Λ the data of U_0 (LFR I (1.79), p.195). So V′ is the deviation from this data, V′ = 1 gives U_0, and the cutoff χ̄, the soft form of χ(|(1/i)log V′(b)| < M₀ε_k) (LFR I (1.101), p.201; §3(d)), is centred there. In the notation of (c), run X's integrand at V′ is exp[−g_k^{−2}A_X(ζ₀, U^X_{k,Z}(V′V′^X₀V_Λ))], with V_Λ the shared data off Λ. At equal V′ the two runs' data on Λ^{(k)} differs by e^{iX}, since V′V′^B₀ = V′e^{iX}V′^A₀ and the norm is bi-invariant. On the support of χ̄, |V′ − 1| < (1 + κ_s)M₀ε_k. With C(M) ≥ 8(1 + κ_s)max(M₀, C_X(M)), V′ and e^{itX} each move the data by at most ε₁/8 per bond, so the data V′e^{itX}V′^A₀V_Λ, 0 ≤ t ≤ 1, is regular with 2ε₁, as in (c), "The comparison". At each V′ of the support the two runs' exponents therefore differ by at most the sum of two bounds.
    - {#4.153} The equal-data difference of g_k^{−2}A(ζ₀, U_{k,Z}(·)) at the data V′V′^A₀V_Λ. As for A(ζ₀, U_0) in (c), "The propagation", (b) bounds it by Σ_xC_w(ε₀)g_k^{−2}(ε/a_n)^{1−ε₀}ε₁² over the points x of the layers of 𝐁_k(Z). The weight has a_{j(x)}|∇ζ₀| ≤ C, since |∇ζ₀| ≤ C/a_k (*The weighted defect.*) and a_{j(x)} ≤ a_k.
    - {#4.154} The change of run B's g_k^{−2}A(ζ₀, U_{k,Z}(·)) from the data V′V′^A₀V_Λ to V′V′^B₀V_Λ. (c), "The propagation" and "The result", bounds it by C_A(M)g_k^{−2}(ε/a_n)^{(1−ε₀)/3}ε₁² per bond of Λ^{(k)}. That bound uses only that each data point contributes ≤ Cε₁|δD| at first order and ≤ C|δD|² at second order at regular data, with |δD| ≤ CΔ, so it holds at every V′ of the support and not only at V′ = 1.

    {#4.155} The Haar measure, δ_{G₀}, and χ̄ are the same in both runs at equal couplings, and the integrands are positive. So the Lemma of the Cauchy note's §8.6 (real backgrounds) gives |log d^B − log d^A| ≤ φ_d, with φ_d the sum of the two bounds. By the results of (b) and (c), φ_d is ≤ C_hθ̃^n per point of the layers of 𝐁_k(Z) plus C_hθ̃^n per bond of Λ^{(k)}. The decomposition (1.10), the bulk form f, the part −2⟨𝒜₂, J(1 − ζ₀)⟩, the linear term of (1.2), and V(ζ₀, ·) enter d only through the action A(ζ₀, U_{k,Z}(V′V_Λ)), so none of them is compared separately. On the complex class the complex version of the Lemma uses the lower bound of |d| by e^{−c(M)} times the integral of the modulus of its integrand, with {#D.e^−c(M)} e^{−c(M)} := exp(−O(1)|Λ|) = exp(−O(M⁴)) (p.358 l.24–30 with (1.10)–(1.11)). For a pointwise bound φ of the two runs' difference of the exponents it needs (e^φ − 1)e^{c(M)} ≤ ½, and it gives |log d^B − log d^A| ≤ 2(e^φ − 1)e^{c(M)} ≤ 4e^{c(M)}φ. The value D(1) at V′ = 1 of that difference does not depend on V′ and factors out of both integrals exactly, so φ is only the oscillation {#D.φ′_d} φ′_d := sup_{V′}|D(V′) − D(1)| over the support of χ̄. The data at V′ differs from that at V′ = 1 on Λ only, so by the kernel form of VAR Proposition 4 in (b) (rate ⅛δ₀) both runs' changes of U_{k,Z}, and their run difference, decay from Λ, and φ′_d ≤ C_d(M)C_hθ̃^n, with C_d(M) a constant of M that counts the points of the layers within the decay length of Λ, |Λ| = O(M⁴). The second bound above is already on the bonds of Λ^{(k)}. So (e^{φ′_d} − 1)e^{c(M)} ≤ ½ for n ≥ n_d(M), and then |log d^B − log d^A − D(1)| ≤ 4e^{c(M)}C_d(M)C_hθ̃^n, with |D(1)| ≤ φ_d. For n < n_d(M), each run's log d is bounded by Bałaban's bounds, and the factor θ̃^{−n_d} is absorbed in C_h. This uses the bounds of (b) and (c) on the class, which *The complex class.* derives under (T-c).
  - {#4.156} *The sum 𝐂_k.* LFR II collects the small terms of all the expansions of the Wilson actions, together with I(U_0) of (1.10), into 𝐂_k (p.369 l.2–7). 𝐂_k enters (1.49) as one term, and the expressions V(Y) of (1.68)–(1.69) through the re-summation of p.377 l.2–9. Among these small terms are the linear term of (1.20), the small form of (1.20) with its part −2⟨𝒜₂, J(1 − ζ)⟩, V(ζ, ·), the last three terms of (1.24), the pieces of (1.26)–(1.29), and A(ζ₁, U_0) of (1.31) (p.361 l.10–28, p.362 l.29–40, p.363 l.11–45, p.364 l.1–16). Since (1.49) is an equality for (1.1), 𝐂_k is given exactly by (1.37) (p.365 l.43–50, with the second term of its right-hand side included in O(1) by p.366 l.12), the localisation of p.367 l.50–p.368 l.4 with (1.48) (p.368 l.32–36), and (1.10). In the notation of (c), with {#D.(g″)^−2} (g″)^{−2} := 1/(g″_k(·))², and with the weights split as ζ₀ + (1 − ζ₀),

    {#4.157} 𝐂_k = W_ext + g_k^{−2}A(ζ₀, U_k) − A((g″)^{−2}ζ₀, U″_k) − g_k^{−2}A(ζ₀, U_{k,Z}(V′_kV′₀V_Λ)) + A((g″)^{−2}ζ₁, U″_{h+2}(exp ig_kB, V″)) + ½Σ_{p∈T_η}η⁴ζ(x(p))|(DH″_{1,k,Z}B)(p)|² − log d + E_k(Λ),

    {#4.158} {#D.W_ext} W_ext := A(w_e, U_k) − A(w_e, U″_k), {#D.w_e} w_e := (g″)^{−2}(1 − ζ₀).

    {#4.159} Here (g_k(·))^{−2} is g_k^{−2} on Z and (g″)^{−2} off Z (p.365 l.19), and the support of ζ₀ lies in Z (ζ_i ∈ C₀^∞(X_i), LFR I p.201 l.28, as p.365 l.33–40 uses it), so (g_k(·))^{−2}ζ₀ = g_k^{−2}ζ₀. On Z, (g″)^{−2} − g_k^{−2} is localised in Λ (p.359 l.36–39), and the support of 1 − ζ₀ is localised away from Λ, at a distance larger than 8MR_k from the support of B (p.363 l.43–44; the distance dist(Ω_k, Λ) of (1.6), p.357 l.33–38), so (g_k(·))^{−2}(1 − ζ₀) = w_e. Bałaban uses this identity himself: he combines the weights ((g″)^{−2} − g_k^{−2})(Z_k ∖ Z) and g_k^{−2}(1 − ζ₀) into (g″)^{−2}(1 − ζ₀) (p.364 l.36–45) and expands the result around U_k with the weight (g_k(·))^{−2}(1 − ζ₀) (p.365 l.29–34). The A(ζ₀, U_0) of (1.37) cancels against that of the denominator.
    - {#4.160} The part 𝐂_k − W_ext. At equal couplings E_k(Λ) is the same in both runs. Each of the four actions is a sum over the plaquettes in the support of its weight, which lies in Z, and its weight is of the kind treated in (b): g_k^{−2}ζ₀ as for d above, and (g″)^{−2}ζ₀ and (g″)^{−2}ζ₁ as the weight ζ₁/(g″)² of (1.70). The configurations are VAR minimisers with multiscale data. The shared variable is V_k, as in *The lines.*; then V′_k = V_k(V^X_Λ)^{−1} (p.378 l.12) depends on the run. U_k and U_{k,Z}(V′_kV′₀V_Λ) carry on Λ the data V′_kV′^X₀ (p.365 l.10–13), compared at equal V_k and regular as for d above, since χ̄ restricts V′_k in (1.1). U″_k carries the data exp(ig_kB)M^·(U^{(AL)}_0) of (1.50), and U″_{h+2}(exp ig_kB, V″) carries exp(ig_kB) and V″ only; both are regular as for the action of (1.70). So each action differs between the runs by ≤ C_hθ̃^n per point of the layers of its configuration in Z, by (b), plus ≤ C_hθ̃^n per data point of Λ, by (c). The form differs by ≤ ½r̄_nN_k ≤ ½C_hθ̃^n per point of 𝐁₀, by *The result for the forms.*, and log d by ≤ φ_d. Hence the two runs' values of 𝐂_k − W_ext differ by ≤ 11dC_hθ̃^n per point of the component's history: a point of a coarser layer of Z, a point of 𝐁₀, a data point, and a bond of Λ^{(k)} are each counted at a point of the history that contains it, and the factor d covers the bonds at a point. This uses the Cauchy note's (10.6c) through the form, the form's interface pieces, the point (6) of (LF-A), and *The complex class.* with (T-c) on the class, derived, not reviewed. It is derived at real configurations, and on the class by *The complex class.*, under (T-c).
    - {#4.161} *The shell of χ̄(Λ)(V′_k) (derived).* The first factor χ̄(Λ)(V′_k) of (1.1) depends on the run through V^X_Λ. It stands on the components of the second class only (p.378 l.10–16), and it is soft (§3(d), LFR I (1.101)).
      - {#4.162} At equal V_k the two runs' arguments {#D.f^X_b} f^X_b := |(1/i)log V′^X_k(b)| differ by at most the data difference {#D.s_n} s_n := C_Δ(M)(ε/a_n)^{(1−ε₀)/3}ε₁ per bond of (c), by the triangle inequality of the bi-invariant distance, since V′^B_k = V′^A_k·V^A_Λ(V^B_Λ)^{−1}.
      - {#4.163} The thresholds are {#D.t^X.2} t^X := M₀ε^X_k, with M₀ the same in both runs (§3(d), p.378 l.10–14) and |t^A − t^B| ≤ Ct^Ag_k²|δ_k| ≤ ½t^A (§2(b)).
      - {#4.164} Everywhere, χ̄(f/t) is Lipschitz in f with the constant 1/(κ_st), and |∂_tχ̄(f/t)| ≤ (1 + κ_s)/(κ_st), since the derivative vanishes where f ≥ (1 + κ_s)t. So per bond |χ̄(f^A_b/t^A) − χ̄(f^B_b/t^B)| ≤ δ^χ_n + δ^χ_c, with {#D.δ^χ_n} δ^χ_n := s_n/(κ_st^A) the data part and {#D.δ^χ_c} δ^χ_c := (1 + κ_s)|t^A − t^B|/(κ_s min(t^A, t^B)) ≤ 4Cg_k²|δ_k|/κ_s the coupling part.
      - {#4.165} The factor enters the split of §2(b) with the other tests of Π_X (§3(d), *The shell bound.*). Since (Π_A − Π_B)₊ ≤ 1{Π_A > 0}|Π_A − Π_B|, with every factor in [0, 1], and 1{Π_A > 0} is the product of run A's sharp tests at the thresholds (1 + κ_s)t^A for the passed tests, t^A for the failed ones, and the cascade thresholds of §3(d) (*The shell bound.*), telescoping over the bonds gives (Π_A − Π_B)₊ρ_A ≤ |Λ^{(k)}|(δ^χ_n + δ^χ_c) times run A's own term with these sharp tests, which (R-s) covers (§3(d)), and the same with A and B exchanged. So the shell is bounded as the shells of §3(d): by δ^χ_n + δ^χ_c per bond of Λ^{(k)}, times a run's own term with Bałaban's bounds. The coupling part is carried with |δ_k|, as in (b).
      - {#4.166} δ^χ_n ≤ C_χ(M)θ̃^n. Here ε₁/ε_k = C(M)R_k, with R_k ≤ L(log g_k^{−2})^r (CRE (2.5)), log g_k^{−2} ≤ log(ḡ^{−2} + b′(K − k) + C) (BETA_FUNCTION_WILSON_LOOPS.md Lemma 2.1(i)), and K − k < 8n + j(C) (*The Ratio.* in (d)), so R_k is at most a power of log(ḡ^{−2} + 8bn + bj(C) + C). And (ε/a_n)^{(1−ε₀)/3} = L^{−(1−ε₀)n/4}L^{−(1−ε₀)n/12} ≤ θ̃^nL^{−(1−ε₀)n/12}, since θ̃ ≥ L^{−(1−ε₀)/4} ((c), the Cauchy note's §8.7). The slack L^{−(1−ε₀)n/12} absorbs R_k, and also the factor (k_s − k + 1)^{1/2} of ε₁/ε_k when §1's ε₁ is the larger one. So C_χ(M) depends on M, j(C), ḡ, L, ε₀, r, b, κ_s, and Bałaban's constants, and not on k, K, ε, or the volume.
    - {#4.167} *The linear term of (1.20).* g_k⟨DH″_{1,k,Z}B, ζη^{−2}Im∂U^0_{k,Z}⟩ is not compared term by term in this section. It enters only through 𝐂_k, so its run difference is inside the bound of 𝐂_k − W_ext above (derived), and a bound of its own, of the type of C_ℓ(M), is not needed. The same holds for the small form of (1.20) and V(ζ, ·). So, of *The result for the forms.*, the main proof uses only the bound of (1.21), which (1.49) and (1.70) keep: the bulk form f, the small form of (1.20), and the linear term of (1.2) lie inside d or 𝐂_k, and so do the remainders V(ζ₀, ·) and V(ζ, ·).
    - {#4.168} The couplings. Their differences enter 𝐂_k − W_ext in four ways. Through the weights they enter as the coupling enters the action in the Cauchy note's §8.4, ≤ Cε₁²(|δ_{j(x)}| + |δ_k|) per point. Through the data exp(ig_kB) at fixed B they enter by ≤ C(1 + β₀)²(k − j + 1)ε₁δ′_k|δ_k| per data point of the scale j, by (c), "The propagation", since |g^A_k − g^B_k||B| ≤ g_k²|δ_k|δ′_k on the support of χ′ and g_k²/g_j² ≤ (1 + β₀)²(k − j + 1) by CRE (2.6). Through log d and E_k(Λ) they enter as in the coupling items of the Cauchy note's §8.6. The form ½⟨DH″B, ζDH″B⟩ depends on them through its background U^0_{k,Z}, whose data contain exp(ig_kB); this is a data derivative of the same kind as the second, and it is bounded in the same way, per data point of the scale j.
    - {#4.169} *The Localised Pieces of 𝐂_k (derived, not reviewed).* LFR II localises 𝐂_k with the old terms: the terms of the first part of (1.49), except the first two, are treated by (1.59) or (1.60) and the decoupling of σ₀, then by the representation (1.61)–(1.64) (p.373 l.10–17), and re-summed into V(X^∼) and V(Y) ((1.68), pp.376–377). So the comparison of each piece is that of *The functions of the configurations.* with the localised terms 𝐂(X) of 𝐂_k (p.367 l.50–p.368 l.4, (1.48)) in place of 𝐓(X), in three parts. (i) Their own run differences at a common configuration: the action pieces are sums over the plaquettes of X, bounded per point by (b) and (c) as in *The part 𝐂_k − W_ext.*, and the piece of −log d is the single term I(U₀) of (1.10), with |I(U₀)| < O(1)log M|Λ| on the analytically extended class ((1.11), p.358), which 𝐂_k contains ("including the term I(U₀) from the denominator", p.369 l.7) and which is not a polymer expansion. It is localised as the other terms are, through the representation of its background (1.61)–(1.64), so its pieces are I at the representation configurations, which lie in the class (*(1.65) at complex decoupling parameters*).
      {#4.169-1} Its run difference at a common configuration is that of *The denominator.* above for log d (the complex version of the Lemma of the Cauchy note's §8.6, with the lower bound e^{−c(M)} of (1.10)–(1.11)), which holds at every configuration of the class under (T-c) (derived, not reviewed). (ii) The variation along the joint line of (ii) of that item, term by term with Bałaban's class bounds of 𝐂(X); these terms are of the generation k, so no age factor and no generation sum enter. (iii) The decoupled propagators, which need (W-δ). The fine side and the current of the joint line, the inputs of (ii), are derived, not reviewed (*The Fine Side at the Multiscale Chain.*, *The Current at the Multiscale Chain.*). (iii) is the relative walk-term bound (W-δ) for the decoupled propagators of the pieces, applied as in *The functions of the configurations.* (the (W-δ) note, derived, not reviewed).
    - {#4.170} *The exterior part W_ext (derived).* U_k and U″_k have the same determining set and data off Λ (p.370 l.7–9), so W_ext is one weighted action at two configurations whose determining sets and data differ only on Λ (by (1.33)). Each of its two actions is a sum over the whole lattice, so (b) and (c) alone bound its run difference only by a sum over all points. The data on Λ is not close either. On the deep part {#D.Λ_1} Λ_1 := Λ ∖ Λ_0, {#D.Λ_0} Λ_0 := Λ ∩ Ω″^{∼2}_{h+1} (LFR I p.195 l.27–29), U″_k carries the large-field data V″ of (1.50), and U_k carries the averages of a configuration that is small inside Λ. So no short segment of data joins the two. The comparison below localises each run's change near Λ through Bałaban's expansion of U″_k around U_k (p.370 l.10–p.371 l.49), sizes it by the per-block depth of (b), and combines the two bounds by min(u, v) ≤ u^{1/3}v^{2/3}. The decay budget is the following: the chain's fields decay at the rate δ₀/16 of the weight of (c), *The weighted bound.*; the power v^{2/3} keeps the rate δ₀/24; and the whole rate δ₀/24 goes into the count (2.58) at α = 1/24, which needs (2.59) at α = 1/24. It is at equal couplings, except in *The couplings of W_ext.* below, and in the common gauge of (c), "The gauge of the data", with U_0 in the AL-gauge from the beginning (LFR I p.197 l.42). Here ε₁ is the larger of the constants of §1 and (c), {#D.ε̂} ε̂ := ε₁ + δ′_k, and {#D.w̄} w̄ := sup|w_e| ≤ g_k^{−2} + O(1)k (p.364 l.35–36). A point of Λ is a block of a layer of 𝐁″_k ∩ Λ or a bond of Λ^{(k)}; it is a point of the component's history at a layer ≥ n. A point of the history carries at most one block and d bonds, so a bound per point of Λ is at most d + 1 times the same bound per point of the history, a factor absorbed in C_h.
      - {#4.171} *The weight.* The weighted blocking artifact and the current of A(w_e, ·) need a_{j(x)}|∇w_e(x)| ≤ Cw̄, as in *The weighted defect.* For ζ₀ this is the choice made there, with a_{j(x)} ≤ a_k. At a point x of the layer m, (g″)^{−2}(x) − g_k^{−2} = β_m(1 − φ_m(x)) + Σ_{m<l≤k}β_l, as in the coupling-term item of (e), *The step map.*, with the layers of the sequence of domains of g″_k(·), whose bound O(1)(k − j) is p.364 l.35–36. The form of g″_k(·) through the functions φ_m is that of CRE (2.24). Here φ_m ∈ C_0^∞(Λ_m), φ_m = 1 on Λ_m^{∼−1}, as in CRE (2.24) (p.259 l.17–21). So only φ_m varies at x. Bałaban allows any such φ_m. The collar Λ_m ∖ Λ_m^{∼−1} is one layer of the cubes of which Λ_m is a union (CRE p.245 l.40–43), so its width is ≥ a_m, and φ_m is chosen, as ζ₀ and ζ₁ are, as a fixed smooth function with |∇φ_m| ≤ C/a_m, the same in both runs. F_K does not depend on the choice. By (2.24), −A(g_k^{−2}(·), U) − Σ_{j≤k}β_j(g_{j−1})A(φ_j, U) = −g_0^{−2}A(U) for every U, so φ_j only moves terms between the Wilson term of (2.23) and the counterterms of (2.25) (CRE p.253 l.25–37, p.258 l.49–51, p.259 l.13–27).
      - {#4.172} *The chain.* The domains of (1.50)–(1.55) are taken within Z, the union of the class of components (LFR I p.177 l.33, (1.1)); this is Bałaban's convention (R-Z), which three printed statements force. There (Ω″_{h+1})^c, (Ω″^∼_{h+1})^c, and (Ω″^{∼2}_{h+1})^c stand for their intersections with Z, so U_2 and θ live in Z, and (1.53) puts U_1 on Ω″^∼_{h+1} ∪ Z^c and U_2 on (Ω″^∼_{h+1})^c ∩ Z. The same holds for the domains of the join in (1.52): Ω″^∼_{h+1} stands for Ω″^∼_{h+1} ∪ Z^c in 𝐁₁ and its complement for (Ω″^∼_{h+1})^c ∩ Z in 𝐁₂. It is Bałaban's convention for the section: "For simplicity we denote intersections of the regions Z_j with Z by Z_j also … We write the intersections explicitly only if it may lead to a misunderstanding" (LFR I p.177 l.33–35), and the operation 𝕋_k(Z_k ∩ Z^c), which the section does not change, is omitted from the formulas ((1.1), l.41–42). Three printed statements force it. By LFR I (1.12) (p.179 l.35) the literal (Ω″_{h+1})^c is Z″_{h+1} ∪ (Ω^c_{h+1} ∩ Z^c), and its enlargements' complements reach Z^c where Ω^c_{h+1} ∩ Z^c is deeper than one or two of their layers. So (1) and (3) fail in the literal reading whenever (Ω″^{∼2}_{h+1})^c ∩ Z^c ≠ ∅, and (2) whenever (Ω″^∼_{h+1})^c ∩ Z^c ≠ ∅. Such terms occur: the section does not restrict 𝕋_k(Z_k ∩ Z^c), and the components outside Z may be old and large.
        {#4.172-1} (1) U^0_k "considered on Z^c depends weakly on the field V″⌈(Ω″^{∼2}_{h+1})^c" (p.370 l.14–15), while on Z^c ⊂ Λ^c the field V″ is itself an argument of (1.50). (2) U_{1,2} "restricted to Z^c is equal to U_1" (p.371 l.26–27), while (1.53) puts U_2 on (Ω″^∼_{h+1})^c. (3) Λ ⊃ Z″_k ⊃ ⋯ ⊃ Z″_{h+1} ⊃ (Ω″^{∼2}_{h+1})^c (LFR I p.195 l.42), while Λ = (Ω^{∼4}_{k₀+1})^c ∩ Z ⊂ Z (LFR I (1.73), p.192 l.43), and already Z″_{h+1} ⊂ Z by (1.11). The convention leaves 𝐁″_k, U^0_k, U″_k, U_{k,Λ}, and U_k unchanged everywhere, since in (1.50) the literal overlap of Λ^c and (Ω″^{∼2}_{h+1})^c carries the same V″, so the data is the same with and without the convention. It changes the auxiliary objects 𝐁₁, 𝐁₂, U_1, U_2, U_{1,2}, and θ of (1.52)–(1.55) in Z^c. Off Z″_{h+1}, which contains Λ^c, U_1 carries the data V″⌈Λ^c of U^0_k and 𝐁₁ coincides with 𝐁″_k, since the boundary layer of the join (2.14) [III] (CRE p.257 l.15) lies where θ = 1, in Z″_{h+1} ⊂ Λ (p.371 l.2–4). It is a function of g_k|B| and Bałaban's constants, so at equal B and g_k the two runs use the same circle. The derivative at t_□ = 0 that (1.23) represents does not depend on the radius, so where the runs' g_k differ the smaller radius serves both, with the larger 1/|t_□| in (1.24).

              {#4.289.3} The statement is joint analyticity: a term is analytic, with Bałaban's bound of the term, along every family (𝐔(z), 𝐉₀ + δ(z)) that depends analytically on complex parameters z and lies in 𝒟^c, so the configuration and the perturbation may move together and δ(z) need not be linear in z. At the first step there are no old terms, and the step's own constructions read the current only through the functionals of *Where Bałaban puts 𝐉.*, so the property holds there. Under (3.13) the perturbation passes linearly, as (L^{j−1}η)³δ, while Δ_𝐔A stays in the pointwise part of the argument. No transport between lattices enters: all terms of a run, old and new, are functions on the run's one fine lattice, which RG I reads at the scale j as T_ξ, ξ = L^{−j}, "the continuous space T scaled properly" (RG I p.257 l.2–3), the term of the scale j reads the current (1.8) of its configuration on that lattice (p.261 l.37), and (3.12) identifies the current of U_{k+1} on the old term's lattice with (L^{j−1}η)³J_{k+1} (p.272 l.26–30), an identity of currents of one configuration on one lattice, so the factor (L^{j−1}η)³ is the conversion of the current's units between the two scales. So the old terms see the perturbation itself, at the same points and in the same divergence form, in their units, against the thresholds of their own layer ℓ_T, since CRE's class bounds are per layer ((2.34)–(2.39)) and its thresholds α_{0,n}(L^nξ)^{−3} (CRE (2.36)) are the bounds of the current in the term's units, which the same conversion relates.

The terms are analytic on 𝒟^c since they are given by Bałaban's constructions, fixed points, Neumann series, and convergent expansions, whose estimates hold uniformly there, so they are locally uniform limits of analytic functions. So they hold on 𝒟^c, at fixed and at moving configurations of the class alike, since the class conditions on the configuration and on the current are separate (RG I p.262), and the proof uses of δ nothing but the bounds of its functionals.

A bound derived on a class holds on its norm class, and the real backgrounds of the support lie in the norm classes (*The room at real points.*), so every use at real configurations is unchanged. The sub-bullets derive the coarse alignment at the points of the norm class and the joint line of (ii) there, through the complex lift.

    - {#4.473} *Bałaban's Statements at the Reduced Thresholds (Derived, Unreviewed).* Bałaban's statements hold at the thresholds α_{i,j}/μ for the ten values μ ∈ {½, 1, 4B₃, 8B₃, 32B₃²L³, 8B₃C_{Q*}, 256B₃²L³, 64B₃C_{Q*}, 2^{13}B₃²L³, μ_mem} that the notes use, {#D.μ_mem} μ_mem := 8B₃/C_mem ≤ 2 the value at which *The conditions.* in §4(d) places the members' complex parts at the radii r (the values 256B₃²L³ and 64B₃C_{Q*} place the members in the class at real points for *The age factor.*, #4.454, and 2^{13}B₃²L³ places U_{k,Λ} and U_1 there; the age factor needs no room, R-Δ being run at the radii (9/8)r at the values 8μ/9, and the membership at complex points is derived in #4.454 from the Cauchy note's #C5.22–#C5.34), once C₀ and C₁ are at least λ_Q = max{1, 4B₃, 8B₃, 2^{13}B₃²L³, 64B₃C_{Q*}, C_mem} times his lower bounds, and so at every μ ≤ λ_Q, as *The room at real points.* takes them. At μ = ½, used for the margin of the X_s representation (`WILSON_IT1_WALK_FACTOR_DIFFERENCE_2026_10_28.md`, §12, *The domain.*), the lower bounds hold a fortiori and the upper bounds hold for γ small, and the same holds at μ_mem where it is below 1, μ_mem being a constant of d and L. The construction does not involve C₀ and C₁, and each of his restrictions on them is of one of three kinds, each of which holds at C₀/μ and C₁/μ. This rests on every use of C₀, C₁, and the thresholds in CRE, LFR I, LFR II, RG I, and RG II.
      - {#4.474} *The construction.* In CRE, C₀ and C₁ occur, directly or through the thresholds, only in (2.28) (p.259 l.40–50), in the spaces of p.261 (l.5–37, l.60), in (3.43) (p.276 l.24–31), and in the remark of p.262 l.43–46. In LFR I the thresholds occur only in the spaces (1.64)–(1.69) (p.190 l.13–p.191 l.21, p.195 l.22–24) and in the remarks of p.191 l.34–43 and p.192 l.16–22. The C₀ of LFR I (1.70) (p.192 l.11) is the constant of a bound, which at the full thresholds restricts to the smaller spaces, so it needs no identification. The α of LFR I pp.186–187 and pp.198–200 is an absolute constant, and the α₀ of p.200 l.35 is the exponent log L₀²/log L. In LFR II the thresholds occur only in the extensions of p.358 l.27–29, p.366 l.25–28, and p.367 l.46–48, in the spaces of (1.65) (p.375 l.17–35), and in the bounds (1.47) (p.368 l.23–27) and p.379 l.31. The α of LFR II p.377 l.11–14 and pp.388–391 is the constant of a bound. The cutoffs are ε_j = g_jA₀(log g_j^{−2})^{p₀} (CRE (2.4)), δ_k = g_k(A₁/A₀)p₀(g_k) (CRE p.265 l.39) in (3.16), and ϑ_k (LFR I p.193 l.21–23). The number of usual steps is N = R_j (LFR II p.384 l.17, LFR I p.177 l.25–33, N > N₀ by p.179 l.10), with R_j the power of L of CRE (2.5). None of these involves C₀ or C₁. So the effective actions, the expansions, and the R-operation are the same for all values of C₀ and C₁.
        {#4.474-1} The extensions are given by explicit substitution formulas, which do not involve C₀ or C₁ either: RG I (3.13) replaces J_{k+1} by 𝐉 and U_{k+1} by 𝐔 in (3.11)–(3.12) (p.272), (3.15) defines 𝐇_j and 𝐇_k by VAR (179)–(180) with 𝐔 and 𝐉 in their operators (p.273), and LFR II constructs its extensions "by replacing" the real arguments by the complex ones (p.358, p.366), with 𝐀₀ = 𝐇_{k,Λ}((1/i)log M(U₀(𝐔))) by VAR Sect. G (p.367). So the extensions at smaller thresholds are the restrictions of those at larger ones. The real configurations alone would fix an extension only on the graph 𝐉 = J(𝐔), since 𝐉 is an independent variable; the formulas fix it everywhere.

  - {#4.557} *Lemma (Two Constants).* Let 1 < 𝔯 < 𝔯₁, let 𝔣 be analytic on |z| < 𝔯₁ with |𝔣| ≤ 𝔐 there, and let |𝔣| ≤ 𝔪 on the real segment (−𝔯, 𝔯), with 0 < 𝔪 ≤ 𝔐. Then |𝔣(z)| ≤ 𝔪^{𝔢(z)}𝔐^{1−𝔢(z)} for |z| < 𝔯, with {#D.𝔢(z)} 𝔢(z) := 1 − (2/π)|arg((𝔯 + z)/(𝔯 − z))|. For {#D.𝔯.2} 𝔯 := 24 and {#D.𝔯₁} 𝔯₁ := 25, |𝔣(z)| ≤ 𝔪^{15/16}𝔐^{1/16} for |z| ≤ 1.
  - {#4.558} *Proof.* On the upper half-disc {#D.D₊} D₊ := {|z| < 𝔯, Im z > 0}, {#D.𝔴} 𝔴 := (𝔯 + z)/(𝔯 − z) maps D₊ onto the open first quadrant, the segment onto the positive real axis, and the semicircle onto the positive imaginary axis. So {#D.𝔥} 𝔥 := 1 + (2i/π)Log 𝔴 is analytic on D₊, and Re 𝔥 = 𝔢 is 1 on the segment and 0 on the semicircle. Let {#D.𝔉} 𝔉 := 𝔣𝔪^{−𝔥}𝔐^{𝔥−1}. Then |𝔉| = |𝔣|𝔪^{−𝔢}𝔐^{𝔢−1} is bounded on D₊, continuous on its closure except at ±𝔯, and ≤ 1 on its boundary there. For η > 0 let {#D.𝔉_η} 𝔉_η := 𝔉·((𝔯² − z²)/(4𝔯²))^η, with the principal power, since Re(𝔯² − z²) > 0 on D₊. Then |𝔉_η| ≤ 1 on the boundary and 𝔉_η → 0 at ±𝔯, so |𝔉_η| ≤ 1 on D₊ by the maximum modulus principle, and η → 0 gives |𝔣| ≤ 𝔪^𝔢𝔐^{1−𝔢} on D₊. On the lower half-disc the same follows for z ↦ conj(𝔣(z̄)), since 𝔢(z̄) = 𝔢(z), and on the segment it is the hypothesis. For |z| ≤ 1, |arg(𝔯 ± z)| ≤ arcsin(1/𝔯), so 𝔢(z) ≥ 1 − (4/π)arcsin(1/𝔯), which exceeds 15/16 at 𝔯 = 24, since (4/π)arcsin(1/24) < 0.054. Since 𝔪 ≤ 𝔐, 𝔪^𝔢𝔐^{1−𝔢} = 𝔐(𝔪/𝔐)^𝔢 ≤ 𝔪^{15/16}𝔐^{1/16}. For 𝔪 > 𝔐 the bound 𝔪^{15/16}𝔐^{1/16} ≥ 𝔐 holds trivially, so the Lemma applies with any real-segment bound 𝔪.
  - {#4.559} *The lines.* Let (𝐔, 𝐉) be in the class, with 𝐔 = e^{iξA′}U as in CRE (2.39), U G-valued, A′ = A′_R + iA′_I, and 𝐉 = 𝐉_R + i𝐉_I, the four fields real. Let {#D.𝐔(z)} 𝐔(z) := e^{iξ(A′_R + zA′_I)}U and {#D.𝐉(z)} 𝐉(z) := 𝐉_R + z𝐉_I. Then (𝐔(i), 𝐉(i)) = (𝐔, 𝐉), and the line is real for real z. Since ∇_U is a real operator, |A′_R| and |A′_I| are ≤ |A′|, and |∇_UA′_R| and |∇_UA′_I| are ≤ |∇_UA′|. Both runs are evaluated at the common data {#D.D(z)} D(z) := M^·(𝐔(z)) at the shared scales, since Bałaban's extension replaces the variables V_k in U_0 by the averages M^k(𝐔) (LFR II p.358 l.27–29). - {#4.570} *The lift difference as a Taylor coefficient.* A bound of E without the Cauchy note's (10.6c), as the first Taylor coefficient of the alignment field along the data tg_kB, does not work, since the real bound of that field holds in the alignment's gauge, its first coefficient is computed in the Landau gauges of VAR Sect. G, and the first-order gauge mismatch between the two is what (10.6c) controls.

{#4.571} (e) *The Carried Boundary Terms (Derived; the R-Operation's Own Terms Derived, Not Reviewed).* In (e), k is the fluctuation step, and {#D.k_s.2} k_s := K − j(C) is the stopping scale of the Cauchy note's §8.2, the k of §1, which sets the thresholds k_s/8 and k_s/4.
- {#4.572} *The objects.* A boundary term 𝐁^{(i)} of CRE (2.40)–(2.42) is localised in X ∈ 𝐃_i with X ∩ Ω_i ≠ ∅ and X ∩ Z_i^∼ ≠ ∅, and is bounded by B₀exp(−κd_i(X)) on its class (p.261 l.47–66). After the step that creates it, it is a fixed function, evaluated at the later backgrounds: the form 𝐁^{(i)}(U_k, …) of (2.40), with 𝐁_k(U_{k+1}) remaining in the action (3.25). The class norm of its two-run difference is b_i, the smallest number with |𝐁^{B,(i)}(X) − 𝐁^{A,(i)}(X)| ≤ b_iB₀exp(−κd_i(X)) on the class: the norm of the Cauchy note's §8.2 with B₀ in place of E₀. The class is the intersection of the two runs' classes Ũ^c_i(X, α̃₀, α̃₁), on which both runs' terms are analytic and bounded. The thresholds (2.28) carry each run's own g_i, and g^A_i and g^B_i differ relatively by ≤ Cg_i²|δ_i|, so the intersection contains either run's class with α̃₀ and α̃₁ scaled by 1 − C′g_i²|δ_i|, C′ a constant of q₀ and q₁. Here Z_i = Λ_i^c (p.255 l.25), and Γ_m = Ω_m^{(m)} ∖ Ω_{m+1}^{(m)} is the layer of the scale m (p.255 l.15–16). By (2.47) (p.263 l.50–p.264 l.8), the part 𝐁^{(i,m)} of the generation i on the layer Γ_m, m < i, carries the factor 2^{−(i−m)}, from exp(−d_i(X)). So the generations i ≥ m sum to ≤ 2B₁ per point of Γ_m, and their differences to ≤ 2B₁max_{i≥m}b_i. The generations i < m on Γ_m are not in (2.47); they carry the inward weight of "The weights of the ages" below.
- {#4.573} *Where they enter.* At a fluctuation step k, 𝐁_k enters CRE (3.26) only through its first expression: as the integrand 𝐁_k(U_k(…)) − 𝐁_k(U_{k+1}) of the t-integral, and, multiplied by t, in the measure (3.27) of that integral (p.271 l.7–8, l.22). The output of that expression goes into 𝐁^{(k+1)} only (p.271 l.29–31, p.279 l.16). The s-integral and the logarithm in (3.26) are taken at t = 0 (p.271 l.14–15), so the 𝐁-terms do not enter the step's 𝐄- and 𝐑-outputs; 𝐁_k(U_{k+1}) remains in the action as a frozen function. Two more expressions of the t-integrand go into the boundary terms only (p.277 l.10–17): the coupling term A(g_k^{−2}(·) − g_k^{−2}, ·), localised in Z_k, and V^{(k)}(S_{k+1}), the expressions above expanded in the perturbative terms of (1.22), each with a localisation in S_{k+1}. At an R-operation, the old terms whose domains meet a component Z belong to the first part of (1.49), which is integrated with Z (LFR II p.369 l.28–30). The terms disjoint from Z are expanded around the new background U_k. There 𝐓(X, U_k) stays as a frozen function (taken at U_k, p.373 l.5–6), and the brackets 𝐓(X, exp iη𝐇″_k(g_kB)U^0_k) − 𝐓(X, U^0_k) of (1.59)–(1.60), with their analogues along the chain of (d), give "a term which is small, and satisfies the exponential bound (2.42) [III] in d_k(Y₀)".
  {#4.573-1} Bałaban takes these "together with other terms of the first part of the effective action" (p.372 l.27–33), so they too are integrated with Z. So the R-operation carries the frozen boundary terms disjoint from the components with the factor 1. The boundary terms that it creates itself are those of the preliminary integrations of LFR I §1, localised in X ∈ 𝔻_m, for some m ≥ j + 1, with X ⊂ Ω_{m+1}^c, X ∩ Ω_m ≠ ∅, and X ∩ (Z_{j+1} ∖ Z″_{j+1}) ≠ ∅ (LFR I (1.63), p.189 l.40–47), and bounded by C₀exp(−(1 + 3β)κd_m(X)) on the spaces Ũ_k^{(n)c} (LFR I (1.70), pp.190–191). They are 𝔹_k^{(n)} = Σ_{i≤n}ℂ_k^{(i)}, with ℂ_k^{(n+1)} the logarithm of the integral (1.60) plus the coupling term A(1/(g_k^{(n+1)})² − 1/(g_k^{(n)})², U_k^{(n+1)}) (LFR I (1.61)–(1.62), pp.188–189). Z_{j+1} is identified with Z_{j+1} ∩ Z (LFR I p.177 l.33–35), so these terms meet the components renormalised at the step. Where the integrations of a component end at some n, Bałaban leaves them "as a part of all boundary terms" (LFR I p.191 l.44–47), and from then on they are carried like the others. So their two-run difference at creation is a source of the recursion below. It is derived in *The Creation Difference of 𝔹_k^{(n)}* below (not reviewed). The old 𝐁-terms enter the quotients of the Cauchy note's §8.6 through V(Y) of (d).
- {#4.574} *Deep terms.* A term is deep at a step i > k_s/8 if its domain contains a point of a layer ≤ k_s/8 at that step.
  - {#4.575} A boundary term of the generation i that is still carried at a later step contains a point of a layer ≤ i. Its domain X meets Z_i^∼, one layer of MR_i-cubes around Z_i (p.245 l.40–43), so X has a point y in an MR_i-cube touching Z_i. By (2.9), MR_ia_i ≤ (1 + L^{−1})MR_{i+1}a_{i+1} ≤ 2MR_{i+1}a_{i+1}, so y lies within three layers of LMR_{i+1}-cubes around Z′_i, the union of the LMR_{i+1}-cubes meeting Z_i (p.264 l.52–55). By (3.2)–(3.5), Ω_{i+1}^c ⊇ (B^{i+1}(P^1_{i+1})^c)^{∼3} ⊇ Z′_i^{∼8} (p.265 l.2, l.17–22, l.43), so y ∉ Ω_{i+1}. The layer of a point changes only when a component containing the point is renormalised, since an R-operation acts inside the renormalised components: its domain Λ = (Ω_{k₀+1}^{∼4})^c ∩ Z and the sets Z″_k ⊂ Λ lie in Z (LFR I p.192 l.43, p.195 l.42); then X meets that component, so the term belongs to the first part of (1.49) and is integrated with it (LFR II p.369 l.28–30). So y stays at a layer ≤ i while the term is carried.
  - {#4.576} The output domains of a step contain the domains of their inputs: at a fluctuation step the polymers of the cluster expansion are unions of the inputs' domains with further cubes (RG II p.12 l.9–11, l.23, (2.9), (2.13); CRE p.278 l.16–31), and at an R-operation the same holds for the expansions of LFR II p.387 l.40–42, p.388 l.2, l.13–14. So a term built from a deep input is deep, a non-deep term is built from non-deep inputs only, and by the first item a non-deep boundary term at a step > k_s/8 has a generation > k_s/8, as have its boundary inputs.
  - {#4.577} The norms D, S, and b of the Cauchy note's §8 at the steps > k_s/8 are taken over the non-deep terms. A deep term at a step j > k_s/8 has a point y at a layer ≤ k_s/8, and y ∈ Λ_j^c, since Λ_j ⊂ Ω_j ⊂ Ω_{k_s/8+1}. Let Z′ be the component of Λ_j^c containing y (LFR I p.177 l.16–17); its history reaches a layer ≤ k_s/8.
    - {#4.578} Let the term, of the generation i and with the domain X, meet a component Z ≠ Z′ renormalised at the step j > k_s/4. X is connected (RG I p.257 l.7–9), so it passes from y through Λ_j ⊂ Ω_j to Z, and crosses every layer Γ_l, k_s/8 < l < j. Bałaban's bound of exp(−d_i(X)) for a generation-i term with a point in Γ_n, ≤ 2^{−(i−1−n)} (p.264 l.1–3), gives exp(−d_i(X)) ≤ 2^{−(i−1−k_s/8)} for i > k_s/8 + 1. The layers i ≤ l < j cost ≥ R(j − i) π_i-cubes, and the layer j − 1 alone ≥ RL^{j−1−i}, by (a) of "The weights of the ages", so exp(−½δκd_i(X)) ≤ exp(−½δκRL^{j−1−i}), and with ½δκR ≥ σ ≥ (d + 1)log L + 1 this pays the L^{d(j−i)} points of the scale i in a point of the scale j up to a factor L^de^{−(j−1−i)}. Since j − k_s/8 > k_s/8, one of the two factors is ≤ L^de²2^{−k_s/16} at every generation. So the deep terms meeting Z are ≤ C_Dk̄Ē₀2^{−k_s/16} per point of Z at the scale j, with {#D.k̄} k̄ := max(k_s, j) ≥ j bounding the number of generations i ≤ j, {#D.Ē₀} Ē₀ := max(E₀, B₀, R₁) bounding the frozen 𝐄-, 𝐑-, and 𝐁-terms as in the Cauchy note's §8.6, and C_D a constant of C_X, L, and d, the rest of the exponent, exp(−(κ − 1 − δκ)d_i(X)), controlling the sum over X as exp(−(κ − 1)d_j(X)) does in Bałaban's (2.48) (p.263 l.50–52), with C_X the Cauchy note's domain count at a point (§8.5), the sum at the rate (β/16)κ, which bounds the sum at the rate κ − 1 − δκ, since (β/16)κ ≤ ½(κ − 1) ≤ κ − 1 − δκ for β ≤ ¼, δ ≤ ¼, and κ ≥ 2; their two-run difference is ≤ twice this, by the triangle inequality. They enter ν_j of the Cauchy note's §8.6.
    - {#4.579} Otherwise the term meets no component renormalised at the step j other than Z′. If Z′ is renormalised, the term belongs to its first part and is bounded in the Cauchy note's §8.6, "Fine scales and old histories". If Z′ is of the second class, the term enters 𝐓′_k(Z′), an ingredient of Z′'s large-field operation, and stays deep with Z′ (LFR II p.378 l.8, l.20–22). If Z′ is not among the components renormalised at the step j (LFR I p.177 l.33), the term is carried with Z′ and stays deep. If Z′ is alive at the stopping scale, the pair is old and is bounded by the triangle inequality in the Cauchy note's §6.2. A deep term that meets a component renormalised at a step j with k_s/8 < j ≤ k_s/4 is bounded by the triangle inequality in the Cauchy note's §8.6, "Fine scales and old histories", which covers every component renormalised at a step ≤ k_s/4.
  - {#4.580} *Deep V(Y) in a Young Polymer (Derived; the Exceptional Constituents and the Completions Unreviewed).* Let a component be renormalised at the step j > k_s/4, Bałaban's k in LFR II (1.61)–(1.68), and let V(Y) be a factor of LFR II (1.91) in a polymer X′ whose components of Bałaban's Z, those that X′ contains, are all young. By LFR II p.377 l.5–8, Y ∩ Z^∼ is a union of components of Z^∼, and these lie in X′, so every point of Y ∩ Z lies at a layer > k_s/8. Let Y be deep, with a point y at a layer ≤ k_s/8. Then y ∉ Z, and y ∈ Λ_j^c, since Λ_j ⊂ Ω_j ⊂ Ω_{k_s/8+1}. The component W of Λ_j^c containing y is not one of the components that make up Z (LFR I p.177 l.33), so W ∩ Z = ∅. In this item the old terms' generation is i, Bałaban's j in (1.66).
    - {#4.581} *The Constituents.* V(Y) re-sums, at fixed Y = Y₄, the terms of the expansions (1.61)–(1.64) of the terms of p.373 l.10–13: the terms of the first part of (1.49) other than its first two, and the terms with the localisation domains Y₀ of (1.59)–(1.60), which contain a component of Λ^∼ (p.372 l.17–18). Each of them has a localisation domain X that meets Z (p.373 l.13–14). Y₄ = Y₁ ∪ Y′₂ ∪ Y′₃ ∪ Y′₄, with Y₁ the smallest 𝐃_k-domain containing X and the components of Z that meet X (p.373 l.15–16), and Y₀ in (1.66) is the smallest 𝐃_k-domain containing X (p.376 l.9). Each constituent has the factor (1.66) (p.376 l.19), and Y₄ ∖ Z = (Y₀ ∖ Z) ∪ ⋃_{i=2}^4(Y′_i ∖ Z) (p.376 l.23). So every constituent of a deep V(Y) has y in Y₀ ∖ Z or in some Y′_i ∖ Z. The V(Y) of (1.70) and (1.91) is this re-summation minus the completions of p.377 l.22–26, which *The Completions.* below bounds.
    - {#4.582} *The Crossing.* Let a constituent have some Y′_i nonempty, i₀ the first such index. Each Y′_i connects Y′_i ∖ Z with Λ (p.376 l.24–25), and Λ = (Ω^{∼4}_{k₀+1})^c ∩ Z ⊂ Z (LFR I p.192 l.43). If y ∈ Y′_i, a path in Y′_i joins y to Λ. If y ∈ Y₀, X has a point y′ within one M-cube of the scale of y's layer, so at a layer ≤ k_s/8 + 1, since the layers are wider than RM in their own units (PRT2 (2.2), p.224 l.10–13). A path in X, which is connected (RG I p.257 l.7–9), joins y′ to a point of X, a contour realising the scaled distance d((Y₁⁰)^c ∩ Y₁ ∩ Y′_{i₀}, X) of the third term of (1.66) (PRT2 (2.46), p.231 l.9–13, cited at LFR II p.376 l.13–16) joins that point to Y′_{i₀}, and a path in Y′_{i₀} joins its end to Λ. A layer is crossed by at most three consecutive pieces, in X, along the contour, and in Y′_{i₀}. The tree lengths and volumes are counted in the scale of each layer. CRE states this for the operation ∼ (p.263 l.6–8) and for volumes (l.21–22); for tree lengths Bałaban's bound of exp(−d_i(X)) by 2^{−(i−1−n)} (p.264 l.1–3) forces it, since that bound fails under single-scale counting. A fluctuation step k adds Ω_{k+1} inside the current top layer Ω_k and keeps Ω_1, …, Ω_k (CRE (3.5), p.265 l.42–44). An R-operation on a component Z replaces Ω_l by Ω″_l = (Z″_l^c ∩ Z) ∪ (Ω_l ∩ Z^c) ⊇ Ω_l, since Z″_l ⊂ Z_l, and keeps Ω_l for l ≤ h (LFR I (1.10)–(1.12), p.179 l.12–38); LFR II works with the same Ω″_l (p.362 l.10). So a piece of extent t in the units of its layer at the step j has an extent ≥ t in the units of the step i, for the old terms integrated with Z and for the completions of *The Completions.* alike. So pieces of extents t₁, t₂, and t₃ in the layer's units, with t₁ + t₂ + t₃ > RM, cost ≥ t₁/M − 1 of d_i(X), ≥ t₂ of the scaled distance, and ≥ t₃/M M-cubes of Y′_{i₀}. - {#4.590} *The step map.* At the fluctuation step k the boundary terms are among the activities of the expansion of the Cauchy note's (8.1), and its marking "R-mark" applies: the two-run difference of an output is a sum of terms, each linear in one marked activity, with the other activities at run B or at run A. So the two-run difference of 𝐁^{(k+1)} has three parts. (i) The terms with the frozen 𝐁-difference of one input marked. (ii) The terms with the step's own two-run difference marked, applied to run B's boundary terms: the measure difference of (8.1), which contains 𝐁_k through (3.27), and the variation of the old terms at the two runs' backgrounds. (iii) The 𝐁-parts of the output differences generated by the other marked activities. The t-integral is a product of the integrand 𝐁_k(U_k(…)) − 𝐁_k(U_{k+1}) and the measure (3.27), which contains t𝐁_k. Its two-run difference telescopes into the integrand's difference against run A's measure plus run B's integrand against the measures' difference, and the measures' difference is, by the interpolation of the Cauchy note's (8.1), a sum of terms each linear in one marked activity, t times a frozen 𝐁-difference among them. So R-mark applies with two insertions, one in the integrand and one in the measure, and every term is linear in one marked activity.

So (i) is ≤ ε_k^{*B}w_{k+1−i}L^{d(k+1−i)}b_i from the input generation i > k_s/8, with {#D.ε_k^B} ε_k^{*B} := 2C_ptC_XC_KPC_εε_k (C_pt, C_X, and C_KP of the Cauchy note's §8.5, whose statement covers the insertions from the boundary terms), which tends to 0 with g_k, w_r the weight of the age r below, and L^{d(k+1−i)} the number of points of the scale i in a point of the scale k + 1.

- {#4.623} *The Creation Difference of 𝔹_k^{(n)} (Derived, Not Reviewed).* In this item k_R denotes Bałaban's k of LFR I §1, the step of the R-operation on a component Z, and ν denotes his n, the number of preliminary integrations done, so that the (ν + 1)st integration, (1.60), is at the scale j and ν = j − h (p.190 l.36, p.191 l.33). The birth scale of the history is n, as in (b).
  - {#4.624} *Which components.* A component renormalised at a step k_R ≤ k_s/4 is bounded by the triangle inequality in the Cauchy note's §8.6, "Fine scales and old histories", together with all of its terms, the 𝔹-terms included. So let k_R > k_s/4. Then h ≥ k_R/2 − 1 (§1), and every integration scale j ≥ h (the integrations run over h, …, k − 1, (1.71)) and every index m ≥ j + 1 of (1.63) exceed k_s/8 once k_R > k_s/4 + 4; the threshold of the triangle-inequality case is raised from k_s/4 to k_s/4 + 4, which changes only its constants by a factor L^{O(1)}. The 𝔹-terms whose domains contain a point of a layer ≤ k_s/8 are deep, and they are bounded by "Deep terms" with the generation i read as the index m of (1.63). Their bound C₀exp(−(1 + 3β)κd_m(X)) is stronger than the inductive one used there. If the deep point lies in another component Z′, the crossing bound of that item applies; if it lies in Z, the history of Z reaches a layer ≤ k_s/8 and Z is old. Below, all norms are over the non-deep terms.
  - {#4.625} *The norm.* Let c_ν be the smallest number with |ℂ^{B,(ν)}_k(X) − ℂ^{A,(ν)}_k(X)| ≤ c_νC₀exp(−(1 + 3β)κd_m(X)) on the intersection of the two runs' spaces Ũ_k^{(ν)c}(X, α̃₀, α̃₁), the bound of (1.70) (p.192). As in *The objects.*, the intersection contains either run's space with α̃₀ and α̃₁ scaled by 1 − C′g_j²|δ_j|. The domains X of (1.63) are physical sets of the layers of the matched pair, the same in both runs, as are the sets Z_{j+1} ∩ Ω_{j+1} and Ω_{j+1}^c ∖ Z″_{j+1} of the integration variables (§1).
  - {#4.626} *The identity.* (1.60) is a fluctuation integral "of the same type as the integral studied in Sect. 3 [III]" (p.189 l.36–38). The variables A_j and B_j are block variables at the shared scale j, the same in both runs. So the interpolation of the Cauchy note's (8.1) applies verbatim, with 𝐏_t built from the exponent of (1.60) and the Gaussian forms of A_j and B_j interpolated as Δ_t there, at run A's cutoffs. The logarithm of the integral, the constant E^{(j)}_0, and the coupling term of (1.62) together make up ℂ^{(ν+1)}_k, so ℂ^{B,(ν+1)}_k − ℂ^{A,(ν+1)}_k is the right side of (8.1), the cutoff shells, and the coupling term's difference. The measure ⟨·⟩_t is of Bałaban's kind, since 𝐏_t is a convex combination of two admissible exponents. §8.5 (R-mark) then gives localised terms in the domains of (1.63), each linear in one marked activity, bounded by C_ptC_XC_KP[ι_G + a_jι] times exp(−κ′d_m(X)) ≤ exp(−(1 + 3β)κd_m(X)), κ′ = (1 + 7β/2)κ. Bałaban's resummation into the smallest 𝔻_m-domain (p.189 l.43–46) is a fixed rule of the domains, the same in both runs.
  - {#4.627} *The marked activities.* They are the parts of 𝐏^B − 𝐏^A, with these bounds per point:
    - {#4.628} the fluctuation parts of the frozen 𝐄-, 𝐑-, and 𝐁-differences, at U_k^{(ν)}(exp i[g_jCB_j − hD̃(g_jCB_j)]V^{(j)}) minus U_k^{(ν+1)}. These are the norms d, d^R, and b of the Cauchy note's §8.2 and of the recursion below, ≤ C𝒟^B_{k_R} with the factor O(δ′_j) of the fluctuation (p.191 l.46–p.192 l.6);
    - {#4.629} the fluctuation parts of the earlier differences ℂ^{B,(i)}_k − ℂ^{A,(i)}_k, i ≤ ν. By (1.70) and the inclusion of the shifted configuration in Ũ_k^{(ν)c} ⊂ Ũ_k^{(i)c} (p.191 l.33–42), each is analytic there with the bound c_iC₀exp(−(1 + 3β)κd_m(X)). As in (i) of "The step map", its fluctuation part carries O(δ′_j). At a point at most N₀ of these terms share a localisation region (the common domain Ω_{k₀+1}^c ∖ Ω″_{k_R}, p.191 l.48–49), and the others are on disjoint regions Z_{h+i} ∖ Z″_{h+i}. So their sum per point is ≤ C_cN₀δ′_jC₀max_{i≤ν}c_i, with C_c the constant of Bałaban's count. With his N₀δ′_j < 4N₀²δ′_{k_R} (p.192 l.1–4) this is ≤ 4C_cN₀²δ′_{k_R}C₀max_{i≤ν}c_i;
    - {#4.630} the perturbative part 𝐏^{(j)}(g_j, A_j, B_j) and the fine actions at the fluctuated configurations. Their difference at equal coupling is the classical depth of U_k^{(ν)} at the fluctuated data, ≤ C_hθ̃^n per point by (b) at the history's birth scale. Their coupling part is ≤ C_gg_j²|δ_j|, as in the Cauchy note's §8.2(b);
    - {#4.631} the coupling terms A(1/(g_k^{(ν)}(·))² − 1/g_j², ·) of (1.60) and A(1/(g_k^{(ν+1)}(·))² − 1/(g_k^{(ν)}(·))², U_k^{(ν+1)}) of (1.62). The functions g_k^{(ν)}(·) are built from the β_l of the history, so the two runs' functions differ by ≤ C_β(k_R − m + 1)max_{m≤l≤k_R}d_l at a point of the layer m, with the growth that Bałaban's bound of the terms already absorbs, as in "The coupling term" of "The step map". So this part is ≤ (C_β/b′)max_{k_s/8<l≤k_R}d_l times Bałaban's bound, and the rest is a variation at the two runs' configurations;
    - {#4.632} V^{(j)} = exp(iℍ_Z^{(j)})V_Z^{(j)} (1.58). ℍ_Z^{(j)} is an analytic function of U_k^{(ν+1)} on Z, ≤ O(1)e^{−R_j}ε_j on (Ω_{j+1}^c ∖ Z″_j)^{(j)} (p.188 l.31–34). Its run difference at the two runs' configurations is a variation, ≤ O(1)e^{−R_j} times the depth by Cauchy's estimate on its domain;

- {#4.651} *The weights of the ages.* An input of the generation i > k_s/8 enters the step k + 1 in two ways: through a domain X that reaches the region Ω_{k+1} of the fluctuation, and through the dependence of the fluctuation-dependent configuration on the fluctuation outside X. By the first item of "Deep terms", X has a point y at a layer ≤ i, so in both ways the layers Γ_{i+1}, …, Γ_k lie between y and Ω_{k+1}, and the age r = k + 1 − i pays a factor for each of these r − 1 layers.
  - {#4.652} (a) Through X. The layer Γ_l separates Ω_l^c from Ω_{l+1} by ≥ 8LMR_{l+1} ≥ 6MR_l in the units of the scale l, by (3.5) (Ω_l^c ⊂ Λ_l^c ⊂ Z′_l) and (2.9), at the layers built by fluctuation steps, and by > RM in its own units at every layer, those changed by R-operations included (PRT2 (2.2), p.224 l.10–13). That is ≥ RL^{l−i} ≥ R π_i-cubes for l ≥ i, with R that of (b); and d_i(X) is the tree length in π_i-cubes (RG I p.257 l.14–16). Bałaban obtains the factor exp(−δκ(L^jη)^{−1}) of a step from (1.18), with δ "a small, positive number", and "the remaining factor exp(−(1−δ)κd_j(X))" is used for the new terms (RG I p.272 l.2–4). His δ is taken as ½δ there, and the other ½δκ, spent on the r − 1 layers, gives e^{−½δκR(r−1)}; (1 − δ)κ remains for the new terms, as in the print.

By the count of (b), PRT2 (2.58) at α = ¼, this rest gives e^{−(1/16)δ₀RM} per layer crossed, under (2.59) at α = ¼, and Bałaban's factors are untouched. Where X covers some of the layers and the decay of 𝐇_k bridges the others, each layer is paid by one of the two at the smaller rate, except the one layer they share, whose factor e^{σ} is absorbed in C_W.

- {#4.658} *The recursion and its solution.* With {#D.η_k} η_k := ε_k^{*B} and b taken over the non-deep terms,
