- {#4.661} *Into the quotients.* Take a component Z renormalised at the step j > k_s/4, with history from the birth scale n > k_s/8, and the non-deep terms of its integrand; the deep ones are those of "Deep terms".
  - {#4.662} On a layer Γ_m of the history the generations i ≥ m contribute ≤ 2B₁max_{i≥m}b_i by (2.47), and the generations k_s/8 < i < m contribute ≤ C_XB₀C_wmax_ib_i by the inward weight, C_X counting the domains at a point. With b_i ≤ 2s^B_i ≤ 2s^B_j, the frozen 𝐁-differences are ≤ 2(2B₁ + C_XB₀C_w)C_B(𝒟^∗_j + C_hθ̃^{k_s/8}) per point of a layer, with no age factor.
  - {#4.663} The history has Σ_mp_m(Z) ≤ (1 + L^d)P_j(Z) points (the Cauchy note's §8.6). So the frozen 𝐁-differences enter φ + ψ there as C^B_n(𝒟^∗_j + C_hθ̃^{k_s/8})P_j(Z), with {#D.C^B_n} C^B_n := 2(1 + L^d)(2B₁ + C_XB₀C_w)C_B. With P_je^{−C_PP_j} ≤ 1, |q^B − q^A| gains 2(e + 1)C^B_n(𝒟^∗_j + C_hθ̃^{k_s/8})q̄.
  - {#4.664} The variation of V(Y) at the points of Y outside the history is ≤ C_hθ̃^{k_s/8} per point, by the profile of (b), since a non-deep Y has no points at the layers ≤ k_s/8; at complex points this rests on the room at complex points of (d)(ii), derived, not reviewed. A factor V(Y) of LFR II (1.91) in a polymer X′ whose components of Bałaban's Z are all young can be deep, through points of Y outside Z; its constituents are bounded in "Deep terms", *Deep V(Y) in a Young Polymer*, with the run difference ≤ r_D + r_E + r_C times the factor's bound.
- {#4.665} *What changes in the Cauchy note.*
  - {#4.666} In §8.2(a), the frozen 𝐁-differences become marked activities, feeding only 𝐁^{(k+1)}.
  - {#4.667} In §8, the norms D, S, and b at the steps > k_s/8 are taken over the non-deep terms.
  - {#4.668} In §8.6, the boundary terms leave (γ) of the Cauchy note's (LF) line, with the bound above: the carried ones, and the R-operation's own terms 𝔹_k^{(n)} through *The Creation Difference of 𝔹_k^{(n)}* (not reviewed). The bullet *No deep V(Y) in a young polymer.* is replaced by the bound of "Deep terms", *Deep V(Y) in a Young Polymer*, which adds 2(r_D + r_E + r_C) = 4e²(C_V + C_E + C_C)2^{−k_s/16} to the bracket. ν_j gains the terms in θ̃^{k_s/8} and k̄Ē₀2^{−k_s/16} times R₁′(100MR_j)^dg_j^{κ₀}, and 4e²(C_V + C_E + C_C)L⁴R₁′2^{−k_s/16}(100MR_j)^dg_j^{κ₀} from the deep V(Y), and (8.4) gains C^B_R(100MR_j)^d𝒟^∗_jg_j^{κ₀}, with {#D.C^B_R} C^B_R := 2(e + 1)C^B_nL⁴R₁′.
  - {#4.669} In §8.7, each part of 𝒟^B_i is ≤ a constant times m_{i−1} in the weighted norm m_i = iθ̃^i + w_K, {#D.w_K} w_K := (K + 1)(θ̃^{k_s/8} + 2^{−k_s/16}) + μ_K, the coupling part g²|δ| by g_i²(K − i) ≤ b^{−1} as there. Every index l ≥ k_s/8 − 1 has lθ̃^l ≤ C_μ(k_s + 1)θ̃^{k_s/8} ≤ C_μw_K, with {#D.C_μ} C_μ := θ̃^{−1}max(1, 1/(e log(1/θ̃))), so max_{k_s/8−1≤l≤j}m_l ≤ (1 + C_μ)m_j. So 𝒟^∗_j is ≤ a constant times m_j there.
  - {#4.670} (T1) includes 2η_kW ≤ 1 and (T-F) of "The step map".

{#4.671} The Cauchy note derives (b)–(d) for single-scale data at the stopping scale; (b)–(d) above are the multiscale versions. (e) has no single-scale counterpart there.

## 5. The Large-Field Dressings of the Loop (Derived; the R-Operations With the Loop Not Reviewed) {#S5}

{#5.1} Here 𝒲^A[τ] and 𝒲^B[τ⁺] are the normalised dressed loops of the Cauchy note's #C1.2 on a matched pair τ⁺, τ of its §6.2, each with its own κ divided out. They have the form of the map's l.261: e^{𝓔_k} times the leading word f_k plus the words tr(Y_{W₁}U_{(1)} ⋯ Y_{W_m}U_{(m)}) with the weights Q_k(𝔅). They are functions of the integration variables of 𝐓, which are the same in both runs (the Cauchy note's #C6.2.1; map l.263, l.326) and are written V below. {#D.a_j.2} a_j := εL^j, j(x), C₀, and the profile {#D.ρ̄(x).2} ρ̄(x) := 2C_G(ε₀)c″_K(ε/a_{j(x)})^{1−ε₀}ε₁ are those of §4(b), and {#D.m_W} m_W := ⌊k/8⌋. |·| and ‖·‖ are the norms of the Cauchy note, and {#D.‖dπ‖} ‖dπ‖ := sup_{|Y|=1}‖dπ(Y)‖_op for the representation π of the loop.

{#5.2} (a) *What the Main Proof Uses (Derived).*
- {#5.3} (LF-W) enters the main proof only at the Cauchy note's #C6.2.22, in the second term of ∫|𝒲^Bρ^B − 𝒲^Aρ^A| dV ≤ B_W∫|ρ^B − ρ^A| dV + ∫|𝒲^B − 𝒲^A|ρ^A dV, for the young matched pairs, k − j₀ < ⌊k/2⌋. The unmatched set (§6.1) and the old pairs use only |𝒲| ≤ B_W pointwise in V (the Cauchy note's #C6.1.3-1 and #C6.2.2), and the all-small-field pair has no large-field dressing. The young pairs need the second term, summed over them, to be ≤ B_Ws^{W,tot}_Kδ_LFZ^A_{ℓ₀} plus the dev part inside s′_K (#5.62), with s^{W,tot}_K summable in K. The young pairs, after run B's own-support shells are removed (the Cauchy note's §6.2), then change F by ≤ B_Wδ_LF(3s_K + s^{W,tot}_K): 2B_Wδ_LFs_K from the densities and the normalisation, B_Wδ_LFs_K from the dev part, and B_Wδ_LFs^{W,tot}_K from the dressings.
- {#5.4} *The Pairs With m_W ≤ k − j₀ < ⌊k/2⌋.* By the argument of the Cauchy note's #C6.2.2 with m_W in place of m, the oldest component X of such a pair meets the large-field region at every scale from j₀ to k, so P(X) ≥ m_W + 1. The bounds |𝒲^B|, |𝒲^A| ≤ B_W hold pointwise in V (#3.40). Also ρ^A ≥ 0 on the real integration region (LFR I p.176 l.20) and Z^A_τ ≤ M^A_τ. With these and (11.3) with the weight {#D.ω(X)} ω(X) := e^{C_PP(X)},

{#5.5} (5.1) Σ_{(M), m_W ≤ k−j₀ < ⌊k/2⌋}∫|𝒲^B[τ⁺] − 𝒲^A[τ]|ρ^A[τ] dV ≤ 2B_We^{−C_P(m_W+1)}δ_LFZ^A_{ℓ₀}.

- {#5.6} *The Pairs With k − j₀ < m_W.* Their components are born at scales ≥ j₀ > k − m_W, and the ingredients at the scales i < j₀ are the all-small-field pair's (the Cauchy note's #C6.2.3). Since Ω_i = T for i < j₀ (§1), the nonempty layers Ω_i ∖ Ω_{i+1} of every step have i ≥ j₀ − 1 ≥ k − m_W ≥ 7k/8. For these pairs (b)–(e) derive, at every V of the real integration region of τ,

{#5.7} (W) |𝒲^B[τ⁺] − 𝒲^A[τ]| ≤ [e^{D^{dev}}(exp(Σ_{X⊂Z(τ)}C_Ms^W_KP(X) + s^{W,0}_K) − 1) + (e^{D^{dev}} − 1)]·𝒲̄[τ].

  {#5.8} Here 𝒲̄[τ] ≤ B_W is the paid majorant of run A's loop on τ: the sum over the dressing's terms of the products of its factors' bounds, with the attached part paid from the reserve as in the continuum note's (4.5) and the D2.6 closure 7.2. D^{dev} is the weighted difference mass of the dev insertions, which l.140 bounds by the recursion of the Cauchy note's §8.3 inside s′_K, and (d) supplies its depth term at the large-field backgrounds. s^W_K and s^{W,0}_K are defined in (f). (W) is the form (LF-1) of the Cauchy note's #CP.2 for the loop, and (5.2) is its integrated form.

{#5.9} (b) *The Run-Dependent Factors and the Assembly (Derived).*
- {#5.10} On a young pair with k − j₀ < m_W, four kinds of factors of 𝒲 depend on the run.
  - {#5.11} The transports of f_k and the U_{(i)}, read on the run's background (map l.265).
  - {#5.12} The insertions Y_W of the species dev, att(j, Z), att(j, coll), and wrap(j) (map l.276). There is no lw, since lw is made at step 1 only and j₀ > k − m_W ≥ 2.
  - {#5.13} The cluster weights φ_k(Γ) of Q_k and the local terms of 𝓔_k. These are numbers given the labels in each run (map l.324), so they do not depend on V.
  - {#5.14} The parts produced by the R-operations of τ's components (the D2.7 closure 15.3–15.6).
- {#5.15} E_const,k is the same number on every labelled term of a run (map l.268, l.312). It is a factor of the run's whole numerator, the same on τ and on ℓ₀, so it is not a large-field dressing and is not compared here.
- {#5.16} *The Assembly.* Let a product have factors with |x^A_i| ≤ x̄_i and |x^B_i − x^A_i| ≤ Δ_ix̄_i. The telescoping identity gives |Π_ix^B_i − Π_ix^A_i| ≤ (Π_i(1 + Δ_i) − 1)Π_ix̄_i ≤ (e^{Σ_iΔ_i} − 1)Π_ix̄_i. The products Π_W(1 + e^{θ(W)}ȳ_W) majorise the sums over 𝔅, since |Q_k(𝔅)| ≤ Π_{W∈𝔅}e^{θ(W)} (map l.310) and the dressing is multilinear in the species. Here ȳ_W is the bound of run A's insertion and d_W the bound of the two runs' difference. Then Π_W(1 + e^{θ(W)}(ȳ_W + d_W)) − Π_W(1 + e^{θ(W)}ȳ_W) ≤ (exp(Σ_We^{θ(W)}d_W) − 1)Π_W(1 + e^{θ(W)}ȳ_W), and |e^{𝓔^B} − e^{𝓔^A}| ≤ (e^{|𝓔^B − 𝓔^A|} − 1)|e^{𝓔^A}|. So (W) follows once the factors' relative differences sum to ≤ Σ_XC_Ms^W_KP(X) + s^{W,0}_K + D^{dev}, by (e^{a+b} − 1) ≤ e^b(e^a − 1) + (e^b − 1).

{#5.17} (c) *The Transports (Derived).*
- {#5.18} *The Alignment of the Backgrounds.* The transports are read on the term's background. This background is a VAR minimiser with the term's multiscale determining set, and its data are the term's integration variables, the same in both runs (map l.265; by the D2.7 closure 15.5 the words are functions of U^{old} through the multiscale minimiser CRE (2.12)). At equal data the profile of §4(b) gives U^A = e^{iεA′*}MU^B in the gauge of the Cauchy note's #C9.4.1, with A′* = A₁* − HD(A₁*). Then VAR (55) and (57) (p.286 l.24 and l.42, with |·|_{(−1)} the supremum over the layers) and the gradient bound of HD used at the Cauchy note's #C9.6.1 give

{#5.19} (P′) a_{j(x)}|A′*(x)| + a_{j(x)}²|∇A′*(x)| ≤ ρ̄(x) + 8B₀C₂ρ̄_n² ≤ 2ρ̄(x),  {#D.ρ̄_n} ρ̄_n := sup_xρ̄(x).

  {#5.20} The second inequality holds under 16B₀C₂C_G(ε₀)c″_Kε₁ ≤ 1, since ρ̄_n²/ρ̄(x) ≤ 2C_G(ε₀)c″_Kε₁L^{−(1−ε₀)(2n−j(x))} and the finest layer n ≥ k − m_W has 2n ≥ k ≥ j(x).
- {#5.21} *The Coarse Links.* For a bond c of T_ε, CMP 98 (15) gives MU^B(c) = e^{iY_c}W(c). Here W(c) is the transport of U^B along the L fine bonds of c, {#D.Y_c} Y_c := L^{−d}Σ_x(1/i)log h_{c,x}, and {#D.h_c,x} h_{c,x} := W(γ_{c,x})W(c)^{−1} (the Cauchy note's #C10.3.21). In the axial gauge of the Cauchy note's #C10.4.9, each fine bond within 4dε of the block's centre is within 4dε(ε/L)|F| of 1, and h_{c,x} is a closed path of at most (3d + 1)L fine bonds there. So |h_{c,x} − 1| ≤ 4d(3d + 1)ε²|F|. For run B's background, |F| ≤ C₀ε₁/a_{j′}² (§4(b), *Regularity*), where a_{j′} ≥ a_{j(c)}/L is the finest layer within 4dε of c. With |log h| ≤ 2|h − 1| for |h − 1| ≤ ½, this gives

{#5.22} (Y) |Y_c| ≤ C_Y(ε/a_{j(c)})²ε₁,  {#D.C_Y} C_Y := 8d(3d + 1)L²C₀,  under 4d(3d + 1)L²C₀ε₁ ≤ ½.

- {#5.23} *The Leading Word and the Arcs.* Hol_C(U^B) = Π_cW(c), the ordered product over the bonds c of C in T_ε. Hol_C(U^A) = Π_ce^{iεA′*(c)}e^{iY_c}W(c) up to a gauge transformation, which leaves the closed trace unchanged. Since π(W(c)) is unitary and ‖π(e^{iX}) − 1‖_op ≤ ‖dπ‖|X|, (P′) and (Y) give

{#5.24} (T) |f^B_k − f^A_k| ≤ Σ_{c⊂C}δ_c,  {#D.δ_c} δ_c := ‖dπ‖(ε|A′*(c)| + |Y_c|) ≤ ‖dπ‖(4C_G(ε₀)c″_K + C_Y)(ε/a_{j(c)})^{2−ε₀}ε₁.

  {#5.25} The transports U_{(i)} between the slots of a word obey the same bound with the insertions' norms as the factor, since the insertions transform covariantly at their slots (map l.266). So in every term of the dressing the transports differ relatively by ≤ Σ_{c⊂C}δ_c.
- {#5.26} *The Count.* A layer-j block of side a_j holds the initial points of at most 4a_j/ε bonds of the square C, at most a_j/ε on each side. There are at most L^d layer-j blocks per scale-(j + 1) point of Z_{j+1} ∩ X (the Cauchy note's §8.6, p_m(Z) ≤ L^d|Z_{m+1} ∩ Z|_{m+1}), and L^{−(1−ε₀)} ≤ θ̃. Put {#D.C^tr_W} C^{tr}_W := 4‖dπ‖(4C_G(ε₀)c″_K + C_Y).
  - {#5.27} The bonds of C in the layers j < k contribute ≤ L^dC^{tr}_Wε₁θ̃^j per point of Z_{j+1} ∩ X, so ≤ L^dC^{tr}_Wε₁θ̃^{k−m_W}P(X) per component.
  - {#5.28} The at most 4ℓ_Ca_k/ε bonds of C in the stopping layer contribute ≤ {#D.s^W,tr_K} s^{W,tr}_K := ℓ_CC^{tr}_Wε₁L^{−(1−ε₀)k}, where ℓ_C is the side of C in stopping-scale bonds (the continuum note's l.24).

{#5.29} (d) *The Insertions, the Weights Q_k, and the Local Terms (Derived).*
- {#5.30} *The Variation.* Each insertion of run A is analytic in (𝐔, 𝐉) on the sub-domain 𝒟^{sub} of the SW closure §3(b1) about (U^A, J(U^A)), and it obeys its bound there (D(k)(iii); the SW closure §3(b2); for the attached species, the D2.6 closure 5.1). Put {#D.Ũ.4} Ũ := MU^B, {#D.J′.2} J′ := 𝐐(Ũ)*λ^B, and {#D.δ𝐉.2} δ𝐉 := J(U^A) − J′. Then {#D.(𝐔(t),𝐉(t))} (𝐔(t), 𝐉(t)) := (e^{i(t−1)εA′*}U^A, J(U^A) + (t − 1)δ𝐉) is the alignment path of §4(d) (*The Intermediate Current and the Estimate*). It joins (Ũ, J′) at t = 0 to (U^A, J(U^A)) at t = 1. At equal data its current bound reads a_{j(x)}³|δ𝐉(x)| ≤ x̄_J(2ρ̄_n + (ε/a_n)ε₁), with the alignment field bounded by 2ρ̄_n by (P′).
  - {#5.31} At a step i ≥ j₀ − 1, at a point of a layer l ≤ i, 𝒟^{sub} allows the phase (1 − β)α_{1,i}ε/a_i per fine bond, the gradient a_i²|∇A′| < (1 − β)α_{1,i}, and |𝐉 − J_i| < (1 − β)α_{0,i}a_i^{−3}. These are the top-layer radii with the layer's factor ≥ 1 − β.
  - {#5.32} On these layers i − l ≤ m_W, l ≥ k − m_W, and ρ̄ ≤ 2C_G(ε₀)c″_KL^{−(1−ε₀)(k−m_W)}ε₁. The phase gives the factor L^{i−l}, the gradient L^{2(i−l)}, and the current L^{3(i−l)}. So the path stays in 𝒟^{sub} for |t − 1| ≤ R_i, with

{#5.33} (R) 1/R_i ≤ c_W(ε₁/((1 − β)min(α_{0,i}, α_{1,i})))L^{3m_W−(1−ε₀)(k−m_W)},  {#D.c_W} c_W := x̄_J(4C_G(ε₀)c″_K + 1) + 4C_G(ε₀)c″_K.

  - {#5.34} By CRE (2.28) and (2.4), with q₀ = q₁ > p₀ (the SW closure §2) and C₀, C₁ ≥ A₀, α_{0,i}, α_{1,i} ≥ ε_i. As in §4(d)(ii), ε₁/ε_i ≤ C_{αε}R_k(m_W + 1)^{1/2} with {#D.C_αε} C_{αε} := C(M)2^{p₀}(1 + β₀). Also 3m_W − (1 − ε₀)(k − m_W) ≤ −(4 − 7ε₀)k/8.
  - {#5.35} For R_i ≥ 2, Cauchy's estimate on |t − 1| ≤ R_i shows that every insertion of run A changes along the path by ≤ {#D.v_i} v_i := 2/R_i times its bound, with

{#5.36} (V) v_i ≤ {#D.r̄_K} r̄_K := 2c_WC_{αε}(1 − β)^{−1}R_k(m_W + 1)^{1/2}L^{−(4−7ε₀)k/8}.

  - {#5.37} This holds under ε₀ < 4/7 and the conditions of §4(d)'s alignment. No function of run B is evaluated on run A's lattice. Run B's insertion at (U^B, J(U^B)) is compared with run A's at (Ũ, J′), the lifts of the same multiplier λ^B (as §4(d) and the Cauchy note's §10.4 use them), and run A's change along the path is added.
- {#5.38} *The Generated Part.* At aligned arguments the two runs' insertions differ by what the two step maps generate from their ingredients. The loop's words are marked activities of the fluctuation measure, species-blind (the Cauchy note's #C8.3.3), and the attached members are fixed factors of the same measure ((T0) of the D2.6 closure). So (8.2)–(8.3) bound the generated difference at the step i + 1, per unit of an insertion's weighted mass, by g_{i+1} ≤ (1 + C_g)𝒟^B_{i+1}. Here C_g is that of the Cauchy note's §8.2(b) and ε^* ≤ 1, with the depth term of 𝒟^B at the small-field points and (V) at the history's backgrounds. By §4(e), 𝒟^B_{i+1} ≤ C_𝒟Bm_i, with {#D.m_i} m_i := iθ̃^i + w_K and {#D.w_K.2} w_K := (K + 1)(θ̃^{k_s/8} + 2^{−k_s/16}) + μ_K of the Cauchy note's §8.6, and C_𝒟B the constant of §4(e) (not the C_m of the Cauchy note's §8.7). Since iθ̃^i ≤ kθ̃^{k−m_W−1} for k − m_W − 1 ≤ i ≤ k, g_{i+1} ≤ {#D.ḡ_K} ḡ_K := (1 + C_g)C_𝒟B[(k + 1)θ̃^{k−m_W−1} + w_K] for these i.
- {#5.39} *The Masses.* Let {#D.Ȳ_X} Ȳ_X := Σ_ZE_{j(Z)}(Z), the sum over the components Z created in X's history, at their creation steps j(Z), of the lifetime totals E_j(Z) of the D2.6 closure 7.2. These totals contain Z's carried attached species with the carry factor 2, the species att(n, Z_n) of the later steps, the collar parts assigned to Z (map l.303), and the exposed segments that pay e^{E^∂}. Then E_j(Z) ≤ ε_A(j)(d′_j(Z) + 1) (closure 7.2), d′_j(Z) + 1 ≤ 2|Z|_j, and the components created at one scale are disjoint. So Ȳ_X ≤ 2ε̄_AP(X), with {#D.ε̄_A} ε̄_A := sup_{j>k−m_W}ε_A(j). The wrap species have no component, and their weighted mass b_wrap is uniform in K, since it is part of the bound B_W of the continuum note's (8.1).
- {#5.40} *The Carry.* Let D_i be the weighted difference mass, at aligned arguments, of the attached and wrap species present at the step i, and M_i their weighted mass, with w(W) of the D2.6 closure §5.0. The carry lemma (closure 5.1–5.3) applies to the differences as to the insertions. Evaluation at the new background does not grow sup bounds, and the touched parts become descendants with the factor 1 + δ_i. This factor is doubled for a descendant of several parents, since the difference of a product replaces one parent at a time. So D_{i+1} ≤ (1 + 2δ_i)(D_i + v_iM_i) + g_{i+1}M_{i+1}, the last step's v_kM_k being the change along the path at the stopping scale. There are no attached species before j₀, at most m_W + 1 steps run from j₀ − 1 to k, Π_i(1 + 2δ_i) ≤ e^{2log 2} = 4, and M_i ≤ Σ_XȲ_X + b_wrap. Hence

{#5.41} (D) D_k ≤ c̄^W_K(Σ_XȲ_X + b_wrap),  {#D.c̄^W_K} c̄^W_K := 4(m_W + 1)(r̄_K + ḡ_K).

- {#5.42} *The Weights Q_k and the Local Terms.* φ_k(Γ) and the attached local terms of 𝓔_k are numbers given the labels (map l.324), so they do not change along the path. They are cluster terms of each run's expansions at the reference point (map l.322; the D2.6 closure 7.4(a)). Their activities differ by ≤ c̄^W_K relative, by the same recursion at the reference point, so the marked-cluster bound (G′) of the Cauchy note's §8.5 gives Σ_{Γ hits W}|φ^B_k(Γ) − φ^A_k(Γ)| ≤ 2C_ptC_XC_KPc̄^W_Kθ(W), with C_pt, C_X, and C_KP of §8.5, the factor 2 being ι_G + a_kι ≤ 2ι (ι_G ≤ ι, a_k ≤ 1). The attached local terms satisfy the same bound relative to their part of E_j(Z). Use θ(W) ≤ νσ(W)/16 (map l.310), 2C_ptC_XC_KPc̄^W_Kν/16 ≤ ν_r/2, and σe^{−ν_rσ/2} ≤ 2/(eν_r). Then the Q-part of an attached or wrap member W is e^{θ(W)}(e^{2C_ptC_XC_KPc̄^W_Kθ(W)} − 1)ȳ_W ≤ C_Q^Wc̄^W_Kw(W), with {#D.C_Q^W} C_Q^W := C_ptC_XC_KPν/(4eν_r). For the dev members the Q-part is in D^{dev}.
- {#5.43} *The Dev Insertions.* The same variation acts on the dev insertions at the steps ≥ j₀ − 1, and it is ≤ r̄_K per unit of their class norm. For ε₀ < 2/5, r̄_K ≤ C′_eθ̃^k with {#D.C′_e} C′_e := sup_Kr̄_Kθ̃^{−k} < ∞, since θ̃ ≥ L^{−(1−ε₀)/4} and R_k is a power of log g_k^{−2} (CRE (2.5)). So it is a depth term of the Cauchy note's kind, e_i ≤ C_eθ̃^i with C_e enlarged by C′_e. D^{dev} is then bounded by the recursion of the Cauchy note's §8.3 (#C8.3.3-4) inside s′_K, as #C6.2.22-1 states.

{#5.44} (e) *The R-Operations With the Loop (Reduced to the Points (3), (6), (7), and (10) of (LF-A); Derived, Not Reviewed).*
- {#5.45} *The Objects.* At a step at which a component of τ is renormalised, the loop-linked part of LFR II (1.72)'s bracket is the ratio of gases Ξ^C/Ξ of the D2.7 closure 15.3. Its activities are Bałaban's (1.91), with the loop's slots. Its flat part P_{k−1}(C)μ^R_k + 4ζ^R_k is subtracted into κ_k (15.4), which each run divides out (the Cauchy note's #C1.2). The remainder e^{E°^R_k − Ψ(S)} and the deviation insertions D_g of 15.6 are cluster terms of the same gas. Every word is a function of U^{old} (15.5), so its two-run difference is that of (c)–(d). In a pair with k − j₀ < m_W every R-operation is at a step > k − m_W, so the fine scales and old histories of the Cauchy note's §8.6 do not occur.
- {#5.46} *The Comparison.* The activities are built from the renormalised components' operations 𝐓′, the factors V(Y) of (1.91), and the slot words.
  - {#5.47} The interpolation of the Cauchy note's §8.6 (*From the Quotients to the R-Terms*), {#D.𝐓′_t} 𝐓′_t := 𝐓′^A + t(𝐓′^B − 𝐓′^A) and V_t(Y), is applied with the slot words interpolated alongside, {#D.w_t} w_t := w^A + t(w^B − w^A). Every interpolated factor obeys the bound that both runs' factors obey, since those bounds are bounds of moduli on the class and so convex. The gas converges for every t by (1.92)–(1.97).
  - {#5.48} The derivative in t replaces one activity by its two-run difference. For 𝐓′ and V this difference is ≤ b̄_K times the activity's bound per point, with {#D.b̄_K} b̄_K := sup_{k−m_W<j≤k}{2(e + 1)[C_n𝒟_{[j]} + C^B_n𝒟^∗_j + C^θ_nθ̃^{k_s/8} + 2L^dC_Dk̄Ē₀2^{−k_s/16}] + 4C_hθ̃^{k_s/8}}, with k_s, k̄, and Ē₀ as there. For a slot word it is the relative difference of (c)–(d), already counted in (W).
  - {#5.49} By (G′) of §8.5, the exponent E°^R_k − Ψ(S) and the D_g change by ≤ 2C_ptC_XC_KPb̄_K per point of the renormalised component, beyond the words' part, the factor 2 being ι_G + a_kι ≤ 2ι. The count of the activities in a cluster is absorbed by the weight of (1.93), as §8.6 absorbs q (q ≤ e^q). Per point of the component's history this is the part {#D.s^W,R_K} s^{W,R}_K := 2C_ptC_XC_KPL^db̄_K/C_M of s^W_K.
- {#5.50} *What It Rests On.* 𝒟_{[j]} contains h_n, the (LF-2) bounds of the fine-lattice objects of §8.6: U₀, H_{1,j}, Δ₁(ζ₀), Im∂U₀, and the argument of V. These objects are (LF-A), whose π-part vanishes at single-scale data by the Cauchy note's β_π ≡ 0 and is derived, not reviewed, at the interfaces as the point (6) of (LF-A). So the R-part of (W) reduces to the points (3), (6), (7), and (10) of (LF-A), derived and not reviewed, as they stand in the Open Gaps and needs nothing else, and the loop adds no object to (LF-A). The exterior part W_ext of 𝐂_k enters the loop's R-operations only as a part of these objects, and it is derived in §4(d), *The exterior part W_ext.*
