## The Weighted Bound at Λ^c (for #0.1; derived, not reviewed) {#SA}
- {#A.1} *Setting.* Inside a cube Q_s with s ≤ L/8 each direction μ meets at most one hyperplane {x_μ = h_μ} of the cells of Λ (side ≥ L), h_μ a half-integer. A cube is *good* if s ∈ [ρ, 3ρ] and the faces of Q_s and of Q_{9s/16} lie at distance ≥ ρ/(40d) from these hyperplanes. Per direction the excluded s have measure ≤ (1 + 16/9)ρ/(20d), so ≤ 5ρ/36 < 2ρ in all. Then the hyperplanes and the faces of Q_{9s/16} cut Q_s and {#D.A′_s} A′_s := Q_s ∖ Q_{9s/16} into C(d) boxes of a product grid with all sides between ρ/(40d) and 6ρ (*fat boxes*), each in Λ or in Λ^c; A′_s ⊂ A_s = Q_s ∖ Q_{s/2} (#0.1.21). The mass graph joins the sites of each bond with both endpoints in Λ^c (the bonds outside Λ of PRT2 Lemma 2.4, p.245); its components are the residual group's domains of constancy. Let s ≤ s₃ (#0.1.20), Q_s = Q_s(x₀). Two cells of Λ^c that meet Q_s differ on hyperplanes that all cut Q_s, a product of intervals, so they meet in Q_s, in codimension k, k the number of these hyperplanes. For k = 1 they share a face. For k ≥ 2 the contact lies within C(d)s of x₀, and since t₃(x₀) ≥ C(d)s₃ excludes a contact of distinct local components there (#A.10), near every point of the contact the cells of Λ^c around it form one local component. So the cells of Λ^c meeting Q_s lie in one local component at Q_s, and every contact of codimension ≥ 2 among them is locally joined. Inside Q_s the cells are the orthant boxes about the point (h_μ) of the hyperplanes that meet Q_s, each a product of intervals that reach ∂Q_s. The part of such a box in A′_s is connected: its pieces {±x_μ > 9s/16} are fat boxes, and any two of different directions meet. Two boxes that share a face are joined across it in A′_s, near ∂Q_s. So {#D.Z_D} Z_D := the set of the sites of Λ^c in D is empty or connected through face-sharing fat boxes, for D = Q_s and D = A′_s, and it meets A′_s if it meets Q_s. In VAR's problem read Λ₀ and its data bonds for Λ^c and the mass bonds (#A.10).
- {#A.2} *Primitives.* On a box P with sides between ℓ and 4ℓ, the complete axial contraction from a base point b (a_1 = 0, and a_μ the sum of F_{νμ}, ν < μ, along e_ν from the faces {x_ν = b_ν} in turn, as in #0.1.26), averaged over b ∈ P, gives a₀ with ∂₁a₀ = F on P and ‖a₀‖_P ≤ C(d)ℓ‖F‖_P. Indeed, by Cauchy–Schwarz along the paths, the contraction from b has square norm ≤ C(d)Σ_{ν<μ}ℓ^{ν+1}‖F_{νμ}‖² over the section {x_1 = b_1, …, x_{ν−1} = b_{ν−1}} of P, whose mean over b is ≤ C(d)ℓ²‖F‖²_P. P is simply connected, so u − a₀ = ∂₁ψ_P on P, and ‖u − ∂₁ψ_P‖_P ≤ C(d)ℓ‖F‖_P. For D = Q_s, ψ := ψ_{Q_s}. For D = A′_s, let {#D.S_a} S_a := {x ∈ Q_s : ±x_μ > s/2}, a = μ±, be the 2d slabs of A_s, with sides s/2 and 2s, and ψ_a := ψ_{S_a}. Slabs of one direction are disjoint, and two or three of different directions meet in a box with sides ≥ s/2. On S_a ∩ S_b, ∂₁(ψ_a − ψ_b) = (u − ∂₁ψ_b) − (u − ∂₁ψ_a), so by Poincaré ψ_a − ψ_b = δ_{ab} + r_{ab}, with δ_{ab} its mean and ‖r_{ab}‖_{S_a∩S_b} ≤ C(d)s²‖F‖_{A_s}. On a triple overlap abs(δ_{ab} + δ_{bc} + δ_{ca}) ≤ C(d)ε_A, {#D.ε_A} ε_A := s^{2−d/2}‖F‖_{A_s}. Put c_{1+} := 0, c_a := δ_{a,1+} for the slabs a of directions ≠ 1, and c_{1−} := δ_{1−,2+} + δ_{2+,1+}. Then abs(c_a − c_b − δ_{ab}) ≤ C(d)ε_A for every two slabs that meet, by ≤ 4 triangle relations through a third direction (d ≥ 3). For (a, b) of directions ≠ 1 the triangle is (a, 1+, b).
  {#A.2-1} For (1−, b) with b of direction ≠ 1, 2, the triangles are (2+, 1+, b) and (1−, 2+, b). For (1−, 2−), each of δ_{1−,2+}, δ_{2+,1+}, and δ_{1+,2−} is split through 3+, and then (1−, 3+, 2−) is used. Let ϑ̂_a equal 1 where ±x_μ ≥ 9s/16 and 0 where ±x_μ ≤ 17s/32, with abs(∇ϑ̂_a) ≤ C(d)/s. Every site of A′_s has abs(x)_∞ ≥ 9s/16, so Σ_bϑ̂_b ≥ 1 there, and ϑ_a := ϑ̂_a/Σ_bϑ̂_b vanishes off S_a and within distance s/32 of its inner face, so a bond on which ϑ_a or ∂₁ϑ_a is nonzero lies in S_a. Then ψ := Σ_aϑ_a(ψ_a − c_a) on A′_s has u − ∂₁ψ = Σ_aϑ_a(u − ∂₁ψ_a) − Σ_a(ψ_a − c_a − ψ_b + c_b)∂₁ϑ_a, up to the shift of the lattice product rule, for any b with x ∈ S_b. So ‖u − ∂₁ψ‖_{A′_s} ≤ C(d)s‖F‖_{A_s}, and in both cases ‖u − ∂₁ψ‖_D ≤ C(d)s‖F‖_{D̂}.
- {#A.3} *Poincaré on Λ^c.* If Z_D ≠ ∅, then ‖f − c‖_{Z_D} ≤ C(d)ρ‖∂f‖_{Z_D} for every function f on Z_D, c its mean over Z_D and ‖∂f‖_{Z_D} the norm over the bonds with both endpoints in Z_D, which are mass bonds. Z_D is a connected union of ≤ C(d) fat boxes of a product grid (#A.1), and two neighbours share a full face, so together they form a box with sides between ρ/(40d) and 12ρ. Poincaré on each box and on each such pair bounds the differences of the box means along a chain by C(d)ρ^{1−d/2}‖∂f‖_{Z_D}. The same chain over all the fat boxes of D gives ‖f − c‖_D ≤ C(d)s‖∂f‖_D for the mean c over D, and ‖f‖_D ≤ C(d)s‖∂f‖_D if f vanishes on a fat box of D, since its volume is ≥ c(d) times that of D.
- {#A.4} *Reflection Extension.* For every function f on Z_D, D = Q_s or A′_s good, there is f̃ on D with f̃ = f on Z_D and ‖∂f̃‖²_D ≤ C(d)(‖∂f‖²_{Z_D} + ρ^{−2}‖f‖²_{Z_D}). Let H_j := {x_j = h_j}, j ≤ k, be the hyperplanes that meet Q_s, {#D.d_j(x)} d_j(x) := abs(x_j − h_j) ≥ ½, τ_j the reflection x_j ↦ 2h_j − x_j, τ_J := Π_{j∈J}τ_j, and {#D.ρ₁} ρ₁ := ρ/(80d). If d_j(x) ≤ ρ₁ for j ∈ J and x ∈ D, then τ_Jx ∈ D, and so is the segment from x to τ_jx, since τ_j changes only x_j, keeps d_j, and goodness keeps the faces of Q_s and Q_{9s/16} at distance ≥ ρ/(40d) = 2ρ₁ from H_j. For a site x of Λ in D let 𝒥(x) be the set of the J with τ_Jx ∈ Z_D and d_j(x) ≤ ρ₁ for j ∈ J, c_J(x) := max_{j∈J}d_j(x), and m(x) := min_{J∈𝒥(x)}c_J(x) (∞ if 𝒥(x) = ∅). Let ζ₀ be a fixed smooth function equal to 1 on [0, 1] and 0 on [2, ∞), {#D.ϖ_J} ϖ_J := ζ₀(c_J/m)/Σ_{J′∈𝒥(x)}ζ₀(c_{J′}/m), whose denominator is ≥ 1, and ϑ := ζ₀(8m/ρ₁). Put f̃(x) := ϑ(x)Σ_{J∈𝒥(x)}ϖ_J(x)f(τ_Jx) at the sites of Λ in D, and f̃ := f on Z_D. Where ϑ ≠ 0, m < ρ₁/4, and every J with ϖ_J ≠ 0 has c_J < ρ₁/2, below the threshold ρ₁ of 𝒥 by more than 3, as ρ₁ ≥ 8 for ρ ≥ ρ₀. *The chain.* Let J, J′ ∈ 𝒥(x) with c_J, c_{J′} ≤ 2m(x) + 3 ≤ 8m(x), o the cell of x, and Δ := J △ J′. The cells τ_Jo and τ_{J′}o of Λ^c share a face if abs(Δ) = 1.
  {#A.4-1} If abs(Δ) ≥ 2 they meet in the contact ∩_{j∈Δ}H_j, which is locally joined (#A.1), so the cells of Λ^c among the τ_{J△E}o, E ⊂ Δ, the cells around a point of that contact, contain a chain from τ_Jo to τ_{J′}o, each cell sharing a face with the next. The points τ_{J△E}x of the chain are joined by straight segments along the e_j, j ∈ Δ, of length 2d_j(x) ≤ 16m(x), each lying in two cells of Λ^c of the chain and in D, so consisting of bonds of Z_D. On a segment along e_j, Cauchy–Schwarz with the weight (abs(b_j − h_j) + ½)^{1/2} bounds the square of the sum of ∂f by C(d)d_j(x)^{1/2}Σ_b(abs(b_j − h_j) + ½)^{1/2}abs(∂f(b))². A bond b of Z_D lies on such a segment only for x on ≤ C(d) lines along e_j, at the points with d_j(x) ≥ abs(b_j − h_j), where m(x) ≥ d_j(x)/8. So Σ_xm(x)^{−2}abs(f(τ_Jx) − f(τ_{J′}x))² ≤ C(d)Σ_babs(∂f(b))²(abs(b_j − h_j) + ½)^{1/2}Σ_{n≥abs(b_j−h_j)}n^{−3/2} ≤ C(d)‖∂f‖²_{Z_D}, the n running over the half-integers. *The bonds.* (i) On the bonds of Z_D, ∂f̃ = ∂f. (ii) A bond from a site x of Λ to y ∈ Z_D crosses some H_i, with y = τ_ix and d_i(x) = ½. So m(x) = ½, ϑ(x) = 1, and ϖ_J(x) ≠ 0 only if c_J(x) ≤ 1, that is d_j(x) = ½ for j ∈ J. Then f̃(x) − f(y) = Σ_Jϖ_J(x)(f(τ_Jx) − f(τ_ix)), each difference being a sum of ≤ C(d) values of ∂f on bonds of Z_D within distance C(d) of x, by the chain.
  {#A.4-2} (iii) For a bond of Λ crossing H_i, from x to x′ = τ_ix, the map J ↦ J △ {i} takes 𝒥(x) onto 𝒥(x′), with c_{J△{i}}(x′) = c_J(x), since d_i = ½ ≤ every d_j and ∅, {i} ∉ 𝒥, and with τ_{J△{i}}x′ = τ_Jx. So f̃(x′) = f̃(x). (iv) For a bond of Λ from x to x′ not crossing a hyperplane, 𝒥 and the c_J agree up to the J with c_J ≥ ρ₁ − 1, which carry no weight where ϑ ≠ 0, and abs(c_J(x′) − c_J(x)) ≤ 1, and abs(m(x′) − m(x)) ≤ 1 when m(x) or m(x′) is < ρ₁/4 + 1, the only case needed, since otherwise ϑ = 0 at both ends. With J₀ ∈ 𝒥(x) attaining m(x), f̃(x′) − f̃(x) = ϑ(x′)Σ_Jϖ_J(x′)(f(τ_Jx′) − f(τ_Jx)) + Σ_J(ϑϖ_J(x′) − ϑϖ_J(x))(f(τ_Jx) − f(τ_{J₀}x)) + (ϑ(x′) − ϑ(x))f(τ_{J₀}x). The first sum reads ∂f on the reflected bonds, which are bonds of Z_D, each the image of ≤ 2^k bonds. In the second, abs(ϑϖ_J(x′) − ϑϖ_J(x)) ≤ C(d)/m(x), since c_J ≤ 2m on the support and m(x′) ≥ m(x)/4, and the chain bounds it. The third is ≤ C(d)ρ^{−1}abs(f(τ_{J₀}x)), which adds C(d)ρ^{−2}‖f‖²_{Z_D}. If ϑ(x′) ≠ 0, then m(x) ≤ m(x′) + 1 < ρ₁/4 + 1, so 𝒥(x) ≠ ∅ and J₀ exists.
- {#A.5} *Lemma P.* Let D = Q_s or A′_s be good, s ≤ s₃, and ψ as in #A.2. If Z_D = ∅, φ := ψ. Otherwise let c be the mean of ψ over Z_D, f := ψ − c on Z_D, and φ := ψ − f̃ (#A.4). Then φ = c on Z_D, and ‖u − ∂₁φ‖_D ≤ ‖u − ∂₁ψ‖_D + ‖∂f̃‖_D. By #A.2, ‖u − ∂₁ψ‖_D ≤ C(d)s‖F‖_{D̂}. The bonds of Z_D are mass bonds, so ‖∂f‖_{Z_D} ≤ ‖u‖_{m∩D} + C(d)s‖F‖_{D̂}. #A.3 and #A.4 give ‖∂f̃‖_D ≤ C(d)(‖∂f‖_{Z_D} + ρ^{−1}‖f‖_{Z_D}) ≤ C(d)‖∂f‖_{Z_D}. Hence ‖u − ∂₁φ‖²_D ≤ C(d)(s²‖F‖²_{D̂} + ‖u‖²_{m∩D̂}) ≤ C(d)ρ²E(D̂), with a = 1 and ρ ≥ 1. In VAR's problem Z_D consists of the sites of Λ₀ in D, one local component below s₃ (#0.1.29, #A.10), and the residual vanishes on the data bonds (#0.1.29), so the second term is absent.
- {#A.6} *Hole-Filling.* The Caccioppoli bound (#0.1.21), Lemma P on A′_s and Q_s, the blend χφ_A + (1 − χ)φ_Q, and the sources of #0.1.24 give E(Q_{s/2}) ≤ θ_hE(Q_s) + C(d)(s/L)²Ē, θ_h = (C₁ + ¼)/(C₁ + 1) ∈ [5/8, 1) (#0.1.23). ∇η acts on R_η ⊂ Q_s ∖ Q_{47s/64} and ∇χ on Q_{5s/8} ∖ Q_{9s/16}, so w = u − ∂φ_A on R_η and only E(A_s) enters the main term. The Q_s gauge enters only the sources and the tails, through ‖w‖_{Q_s} ≤ C(d)ρE(Q_s)^{1/2}. In the N_b problem the sites of Λ^c in Q_s and in A′_s are connected (#A.1), so the two gauges equal one constant on Λ^c, and no capacity of the components enters.
- {#A.7} *Iteration.* If ϕ is nondecreasing with ϕ(ρ/2) ≤ θ_hϕ(3ρ) + Bρ^β for ρ₀ ≤ ρ ≤ R, here R := s₃/3 (#0.1.20), and β > {#D.α} α := log(1/θ_h)/log 6, induction on 6^{−k}R gives ϕ(r) ≤ C(d, β − α)[(r/R)^αϕ(R) + Br^αR^{β−α}], the geometric sum Σ_m(θ_h6^β)^m being dominated by its last term. Monotonicity covers ρ₀ ≤ r < 3ρ₀ and R < r ≤ s₃. Here ϕ(r) = E(Q_r), β = 2, B = C(d)L^{−2}Ē (#0.1.23), and α ≤ log(8/5)/log 6 < 1, so C(d, 2 − α) ≤ C(d), Br^αR^{2−α} ≤ C(d)(r/R)^α(R/L)²Ē, and ϕ(R) ≤ Ē. This gives E(Q_r) ≤ C(d)(r/s₃)^αĒ for ρ₀ ≤ r ≤ s₃.
- {#A.8} *Hard Constraints.* For s ≤ L/8, Q_s meets at most 2^d coarse blocks. VAR's linearised average is Q̃ = Q − D̄K: in RG I (0.4) (p.253) the contours Γ ∈ 𝐆(c₋, x) and Γ′ ∈ 𝐆(c₊, x′) depend only on the block point and the site, so the linear part is the average Q of the line integrals A([x, x′]) over x ∈ B(c₋), with weights of order L^{−d} on the bonds of the lines (PBG's Q_j up to its factor 1/(L^jη) of (3.14), QD = D̄Q′), minus D̄ of KA(y), the average of A over the contours from y to the sites of B(y) (table #T10.23, Q − Q̃ ∈ ran D̄); the composites over the scales keep this form. ∂A_N = ∂U′_ax, the two differing by a gradient (heading), and in the linearised problem U′_ax minimises ‖∂A‖² on VAR's constraint set (VAR minimises (5)), so ⟨∂A_N, ∂t⟩ = ⟨μ, Q̃t⟩ for every t that vanishes on the data bonds of Λ₀, μ the multipliers of the coarse constraints. Testing with t = ∂λ, λ constant on the components of Λ₀ and arbitrary elsewhere, gives D̄*μ = 0 at the block points of the layers j ≥ 1, and at the points of Λ₀ only its sums over each component. Kt = 0 at the points y of Λ₀, since B(y) = {y} and the contour from y to y is empty, so ⟨μ, D̄Kt⟩ = ⟨D̄*μ, Kt⟩ = 0 and ⟨μ, Q̃t⟩ = ⟨μ, Qt⟩: the contour parts drop out. Hence ⟨∂A_N, ∂t⟩ = 0 for every t with Qt = 0 that vanishes on the data bonds. The test field is {#D.t.4} t := η²f − Σ_c(Q(η²f))(c)β_c, η the cutoff of #0.1.21 (1 on Q_{s/2}, supported in Q_s), not the lattice spacing, which is 1 in these units, {#D.f.3} f := A_N − ∂φ − A_ref (A_ref an interpolant carrying the data on the support of η), β_c the bumps of #0.1.33.1, with Qβ_c = δ_c, of size 1/L on the block and ‖∂β_c‖² ≤ C(d)L^{d−4}. Then abs(Q(η²f)(c)) ≤ C(d)L^{1−d}ρ^{d/2}‖f‖_{Q_s} and ‖f‖²_{Q_s} ≤ C(d)ρ²E by Lemma P, so the correction's energy is ≤ C(d)(ρ/L)^{d+2}E and its cross term with ∂A_N is ≤ εE + C(d)ε^{−1}(ρ/L)^{d+2}Ē: a source with exponent d + 2 > α.
- {#A.9} *Bałaban's Representative.* RG I's data (0.4) (#A.11.1.4.4.1), like VAR's (3), are invariant under VAR (4) = REG (1.14), u = 1 at the points of 𝔅_k (p.278; REG p.78), and the axial representative U′_ax (REG (1.19)) satisfies them. Bałaban's u_R = U′_ax^{u^{−1}} with \overline{R₀u}^j = 1 (REG (1.29); VAR (152)), whose linear part is Q′_jζ = 0 (PBG p.394 l.1–2), so u_R = U′_ax + ∂ζ^R with Q′ζ^R = 0, and u_R is not in VAR's data set (REG p.81 l.23–25). The bounds below are derived for this first-order ω at a background, whose transports enter the differences and the contours; *The exact transformation.* (#A.9.3) bounds the exact G^c-valued transformation from them. A_N = U′_ax + ∂ζ^N has ζ^N = 0 on Λ₀ and Q′ζ^N = −KU′_ax (#0.1 heading). So ω = ζ^R − ζ^N vanishes on Λ₀, where Q′ = P, and at a block point y of the layer j, Q′ω(y) = KU′_ax(y), the average with weights L^{−jd} over x ∈ B^j(y) of the sums of U′_ax along the contours Γ^{(j)}_{y,x} (#A.8), each at most the length ≤ dL^j of Γ^{(j)}_{y,x} in η-bonds times sup_{block}abs(U′_ax). This holds at real backgrounds, where R(U) is unitary, and with a factor 1 + C(L, M)ε₁ at the complex ones, whose transports along such paths have ‖R(U)‖ ≤ e^{2dL^j sup abs(Im ηA)}.
  {#A.9-1} At a site x of the block, ω(x) differs from its transport to y by at most 2dL^j sup_{block}abs(∂ω) plus the holonomy defect of loops of length ≤ 4dL^j, which bound ≤ C(d)L^{2j} plaquettes of Ω_j, each with abs(U(∂p) − 1) < ε₀L^{−2j} by VAR (2) (p.278), so the defect is ≤ C(d)ε₀ sup_{block}abs(ω), and sup_{block}abs(ω) ≤ 2(abs(Q′ω(y)) + 2dL^j sup_{block}abs(∂ω)) for C(d)ε₀ ≤ ½. Hence abs(ηω(x)) ≤ C(d)L^jη sup_{block}(abs(U′_ax) + abs(A_N) + abs(u_R)), L^jη times a field being its size in the units of the layer j. All three are linear in the data to first order, and their complex parts are ≤ C(L, M) times the complex part of the data, volume-uniformly: u_R = 𝓗(B) in the representation exp iη𝓗(B)U_k, and VAR (190) (p.308) bounds δ𝓗(x)/δB(y′) by O(1)(L^jη)^{−1}(L^{j′}η)^{−d}e^{−δ₀d(y,y′)/8} on the complex domain, so integrating from Re B to B and summing over y′ gives abs(Im 𝓗(x)) ≤ C(d, L, M)(L^jη)^{−1}sup abs(Im B); A_N = u_R − ∂ω, so its complex part follows from those of u_R and ω, and that of ω is bounded directly at first order, without a local bound on A_N.

  {#A.9.1} A_N is least on A_N + ∂N(Q′) (#0.1 heading), so ω minimises ‖u_R − ∂ω‖ under Q′ω = KU′_ax and ω = 0 on Λ₀. Let b_y be a bump in the block of y, zero on Λ₀, with Q′b_y = δ_y, abs(b_y) ≤ C(d), and abs(∂b_y) ≤ C(d)ℓ_y^{−1}, ℓ_y the block's side. Put {#D.ω_g} ω_g := Σ_yKU′_ax(y)b_y and {#D.ω₀} ω₀ := ω − ω_g ∈ N(Q′). Then ⟨∂ω₀ − f, ∂ζ⟩ = 0 for ζ ∈ N(Q′), with {#D.f.4} f := u_R − ∂ω_g and abs(f) ≤ abs(u_R) + C(d)sup_{block}abs(U′_ax), since abs(KU′_ax(y)) ≤ dℓ_y sup_{block}abs(U′_ax). For ζ vanishing on Λ₀, ⟨∂ω₀ − f, ∂ζ⟩ = Σ_yν(y)Q′ζ(y), and testing with b_y gives abs(ν(y)) ≤ C(d)ℓ_y^{d/2−1}‖∂ω₀ − f‖_{y⁺}. Let ρ be the distance in the local units, a bond in a block of side ℓ having length ℓ^{−1} and a bond between blocks of sides ℓ < ℓ′ the length ℓ^{−1} of its finer endpoint, ℓ := ℓ_y on the block of y, and w := e^{±δρ}, so abs(∂w) ≤ C(d)δℓ^{−1}w and abs(w² − w(y)²) ≤ C(d)δw(y)² on the block of y and its neighbours, for δ ≤ 1. Test with {#D.ζ.3} ζ := w²ω₀ − Σ_yQ′(w²ω₀)(y)b_y, which vanishes on Λ₀ and has Q′ζ = 0, so ζ ∈ N(Q′). Since Q′ω₀ = 0, Q′(w²ω₀)(y) = Q′((w² − w(y)²)ω₀)(y), of size ≤ C(d)δw(y)²ℓ_y^{−d/2}‖ω₀‖_y, and ‖∂b_y‖ ≤ C(d)ℓ_y^{d/2−1}. With ⟨∂ω₀, ∂(w²ω₀)⟩ ≥ ‖w∂ω₀‖² − C(d)δ‖w∂ω₀‖‖wℓ^{−1}ω₀‖, by the product rule ∂(w²ω₀)(b) = w²(b₊)∂ω₀(b) + ω₀(b₋)∂(w²)(b) with the bonds between layers oriented so that b₋ is the finer endpoint, the identity ⟨∂ω₀ − f, ∂ζ⟩ = 0 gives ‖w∂ω₀‖² ≤ (‖w∂ω₀‖ + C(d)δ‖wℓ^{−1}ω₀‖)‖wf‖ + C(d)δ‖wℓ^{−1}ω₀‖(‖w∂ω₀‖ + ‖wf‖). The per-block Poincaré bound of #0.1.30, for ω₀ with Q′ω₀ = 0 on every block and ω₀ = 0 on Λ₀ (its covariant form, with a factor 1 + C(L, M)ε₁ at the complex backgrounds, *At the complex backgrounds.* below), gives ‖wℓ^{−1}ω₀‖ ≤ C(d)‖w∂ω₀‖, so for δ ≤ c(d), ‖e^{±δρ}ℓ^{−1}ω₀‖ + ‖e^{±δρ}∂ω₀‖ ≤ C(d)‖e^{±δρ}f‖.

  {#A.9.2} At a site x of the block of y, let B be the ball of radius {#D.r.4} r := ℓ_y/(4L) about x with the sites of Λ₀ removed, and G_B its Green's function, ≤ C(d)abs(· − ·)^{2−d}. Then ω₀ = h + G_B∂*f + G_BQ′*ν with h harmonic in B and 0 on Λ₀. Extended by 0, abs(h) is subharmonic, so abs(h(x)) ≤ C(d)r^{−d/2}‖h‖_B. Caccioppoli for G_B(x, ·) on dyadic annuli gives Σabs(∂G_B(x, ·)) ≤ C(d)r, so abs(G_B∂*f(x)) ≤ C(d)r sup_Babs(f). The weights of Q′* are ≤ ℓ′^{−d} on the blocks of side ℓ′ ≥ ℓ_y/L that meet B, so abs(G_BQ′*ν(x)) ≤ C(d)r²(L/ℓ_y)^{1+d/2}‖∂ω₀ − f‖_{B⁺}. Hence sup_{block}abs(ω₀) ≤ C(d, L)Σ_{y″}e^{−δρ(y, y″)}ℓ_y(ℓ_{y″}/ℓ_y)^{d/2}sup_{y″}abs(f), the ratio ℓ_{y″}/ℓ_y ≤ L^{abs(j″ − j)} being paid by e^{−δρ} across the layers for δRM ≥ (d + 2)log L. In the units of the layer j, the fields of a finer layer j″ < j are L^{j−j″} times larger, and the same decay pays this. So abs(Im ηω) ≤ C(L, M)sup(L^{j″}η abs(Im u_R) + L^{j″}η abs(Im U′_ax)), the supremum over all layers, each field in the units of its own layer; U′_ax because by (1.19) its value on a bond of the block is fixed by the data and by the plaquettes of F = ∂U′_ax along the contours Γ_{x_{n+1},x_n}, each of at most dL bonds of the scale n, inside the block, so in the units of the layer j its complex part is at most C(d)L² times the complex parts of the data and of those plaquettes, the scales n < j adding a geometric series. PBG Theorem 3.1 ((3.42), p.397) enters only through the operator G′ of R, with constants of d and L.

  {#A.9.3} *The exact transformation.* The relations u_R = U′_ax + ∂ζ^R, A_N = U′_ax + ∂ζ^N, and u_R = A_N + ∂ω are additive, while the covariant members are conjugated by a group-valued transformation, so the representative at which the chain runs is fixed at group level as follows. Let B_t := Re B + it Im B, t ∈ [0, 1]. At t = 0 the data are real, and g₀ := e^{iηω^{re}}, ω^{re} the ω above at the data Re B, is G-valued, so Ad(g₀) is an isometry and CRE (2.34)–(2.37) are invariant under it. Let g_t solve g_t^{−1}∂_tg_t = iηω′_t, with ω′_t the first-order ω above at the background u_R(B_t)^{g_t^{−1}} for the data ∂_tB_t = i Im B: ω′_t vanishes on Λ₀, its block conditions are those above with U′_ax replaced by ∂_tU′_ax, and it is stationary for ‖∂_tu_R − ∂ω′_t‖² in the transports of that background. The square is the bilinear extension to 𝔤^c of the Ad-invariant inner product, which Ad(G^c) preserves, and the transports and the covariant means are gauge-covariant (PBG (3.32), p.395, with its consequence (3.33), p.396, for G′ and R, and its analytic continuation, PBG Theorem 3.4, p.400), so ω′_t = Ad(g_t^{−1})ω̃′_t pointwise, with {#D.ω̃′_t} ω̃′_t := the first-order ω at the background u_R(B_t) itself, for the inputs ∂_tu_R and ∂_tU′_ax.
  {#A.9.3-1} Here the inputs of ω′_t are these read in the frame of u_R(B_t)^{g_t^{−1}}, i.e. conjugated by Ad(g_t^{−1}) as the data transform (REG p.78 l.15), which is the frame in which d/dt(u_R^{g_t^{−1}}) is computed. The representative is u_R^{g^{−1}}, {#D.g.5} g := g_t at t = 1. In the transports of B_t its derivative in t is ∂_tu_R − ∂ω′_t, the heading's A_N for the data i Im B, so A_N is its first-order part, and g = 1 on Λ₀. The rest is of second order: for data Re B + is Im B, s complex, the construction along t ↦ Re B + its Im B is analytic in s, and for abs(s) ≤ c(L, M)/ε₁ the data stay in the domain where the bounds of this item hold, with the representative within C(L, M) of its value at s = 0 in the units of each layer; so by Cauchy's bound on that disc, the representative at s = 1 differs from its value at s = 0 plus its first-order part by ≤ C(L, M)ε₁², and the callers carry this as the second-order terms of #0.1.11.

  {#A.9.4} *At the complex backgrounds.* u_R(B_t) = exp(iη𝓗(B_t))U_k = e^{iηA′}U_re with U_re := exp(iη Re 𝓗(B_t))U_k G-valued. By the first two entries of VAR (190), which hold on the complex domain (VAR p.309 l.2–3), summed over y′ as above, and the Baker–Campbell–Hausdorff formula, abs(ηA′) ≤ αℓ^{−1} and abs(η∇_{U_re}A′) ≤ αℓ^{−2} on the blocks of side ℓ, in the units η = 1, with {#D.α.9} α := C(d, L, M)ε₁: the form (3.37) of PBG (p.396). Write ∂_U = ∂_{U_re} + E₁, (E₁ζ)(b) = e(b)ζ(b₊), and Q′_U = Q′_{U_re} + E₂. Then abs(e) ≤ C(d)αℓ^{−1}, abs(∇e) ≤ C(d)αℓ^{−2}, and abs(E₂ζ(y)) ≤ C(d)αℓ_y^{−d/2}‖ζ‖_y, the contours having length ≤ C(d)ℓ_y. Three steps above change, each by a relative C(d)α. (i) The per-block Poincaré bound at U_re (#0.1.30) holds at U after absorbing E₁ and E₂, for α ≤ c(d), and b_y is replaced by b_y(Q′_Ub_y(y))^{−1}, so that Q′_Ub_y = δ_y. (ii) In the weighted bound the test field is ζ := w²ω̄₀ − Σ_yQ′_U(w²ω̄₀)(y)b_y, with ω̄₀ the conjugate of ω₀ in 𝔤^c = 𝔤 ⊗ ℂ. With σ the conjugation of G^c fixing G, Q′_Uω̄₀ is the conjugate of Q′_{U^σ}ω₀, which differs from Q′_Uω₀ = 0 by ≤ C(d)αℓ_y^{−d/2}‖ω₀‖_y. The bilinear pairing of ∂_Uω₀ with ∂_U(w²ω̄₀) is the Hermitian ⟨∂_Uω₀, ∂_U(w²ω₀)⟩ up to C(d)α‖w∂_Uω₀‖‖wℓ^{−1}ω₀‖, so the weighted inequality holds with δ + C(d)α in place of δ. (iii) In the Green's-function step G_B is that of the real covariant Laplacian ∂_{U_re}^*∂_{U_re}.
  {#A.9.4-1} The remainder ∂_U^T∂_U − ∂_{U_re}^*∂_{U_re} = ∂_{U_re}^*E₁ + E₁^T∂_{U_re} + E₁^TE₁ is, by the covariant product rule (as a·∇ζ = ∇·(aζ) − (∇·a)ζ), ∂_{U_re}^*(e₁ζ) + e₂ζ with abs(e₁) ≤ C(d)αℓ^{−1} and abs(e₂) ≤ C(d)αℓ^{−2}, and E₂ adds Q′-terms of relative size C(d)α. They enter ω₀ as G_B∂*(e₁ω₀) and G_B(e₂ω₀), which are ≤ C(d)α(r/ℓ + r²/ℓ²)sup_Babs(ω₀) and are absorbed in the weighted supremum. The source changes by ∂_U^Tf − ∂_{U_re}^*f = E₁^Tf, and G_B(E₁^Tf) ≤ C(d)αr²ℓ^{−1}sup_Babs(f) ≤ C(d)αr sup_Babs(f), of the form of the term G_B∂*f. So for ε₁ ≤ c(d, L, M) the bounds above hold at u_R(B_t), with other constants of d, L, and M.

  {#A.9.5} Write g_t = g₀e^{iηω_t} with ω_t = 0 at t = 0, and {#D.ω.5} ω := ω_t at t = 1; the solution exists on [0, 1] by the bound below and continuity. The bounds above at u_R(B_t) give abs(ηω̃′_t) ≤ C(L, M)sup(L^{j″}η abs(∂_tu_R) + L^{j″}η abs(∂_tU′_ax)), and ∂_tu_R = (δ𝓗/δB)(B_t)[i Im B] and ∂_tU′_ax are bounded as the complex parts above, so abs(ηω̃′_t) ≤ C(L, M)ε₁ and abs(ηω′_t) ≤ ‖Ad(g_t^{−1})‖C(L, M)ε₁ ≤ e^{2abs(ηω_t)}C(L, M)ε₁. With {#D.φ.5} φ(z) := (1 − e^{−z})/z, g_t^{−1}∂_tg_t = φ(ad iηω_t)(iη∂_tω_t), and 1/φ(z) = z/(1 − e^{−z}) = 1 + z/2 + z²/12 − z⁴/720 + …, whose coefficients sum in absolute value to < 2, so abs(η∂_tω_t) ≤ 2abs(ηω′_t) while ‖ad(iηω_t)‖ ≤ 2abs(ηω_t) ≤ 1. Let T be the largest t ≤ 1 such that the solution exists on [0, t] with abs(ηω_s) ≤ ½ at every point for s ≤ t. On [0, T], abs(η∂_tω_t) ≤ 2eC(L, M)ε₁, so abs(ηω_t) ≤ 2eC(L, M)ε₁t < ½ for ε₁ ≤ c(L, M), and since the system is finite with an analytic right side, T = 1. So abs(ηω) ≤ C(L, M)ε₁ ≤ ½. So abs(Im ηω) ≤ abs(ηω) ≤ C(L, M)ε₁ at every point, and ‖Ad(g)‖ = ‖Ad(e^{iηω})‖ ≤ e^{‖ad(iηω)‖} ≤ e^{2abs(ηω)} ≤ 1 + C(L, M)ε₁.

  {#A.9.6} *At the interfaces.* Where the chain runs at A_♮ = A_N + ∂ω_♮ for the complex part of the data (#0.1.11, #0.1.30, #A.11.50), the representative is u_R^{g_♮^{−1}} with {#D.g_♮} g_♮ := ge^{−iηω_♮^{im}}, where {#D.ω_♮^{im}} ω_♮^{im} := ω_♮ for the data i Im B, built in the transports of the real representative u_R(Re B)^{g₀^{−1}}, as the first-order part A_N is. The maps of #A.11.50 are real-linear and preserve 𝔤 there, so abs(ηω_♮^{im}) = abs(ηω_♮(Im B)) ≤ C(L, M)ε₁, by the sup-to-sup bounds of #A.11.50 at the real background. ω_♮^{im} ∈ N(Q′) is block-anchored and vanishes on Λ₀, where Q′ = P, so g_♮ = 1 on Λ₀, and ‖Ad(g_♮)‖ ≤ ‖Ad(g)‖e^{2abs(ηω_♮^{im})} ≤ 1 + C(L, M)ε₁. For the data Re B + is Im B, g_♮(s) := g(s)e^{−isηω_♮^{im}}, g(s) the g above at these data, is analytic in s and equals g₀ at s = 0, and g_♮^{−1}∂_sg_♮ = iη(ω′_0 − ω_♮^{im}) at s = 0. So the first-order part of u_R^{g_♮^{−1}} is A_N + ∂ω_♮^{im}, the A_♮ for the data i Im B. At s = 0 it is u_R(Re B)^{g₀^{−1}}, as in #A.9.3, since g_♮ removes only ω_♮^{im}. For abs(s) ≤ c(L, M)/ε₁, abs(sηω_♮^{im}) ≤ ½, so Cauchy's bound on that disc gives its second-order terms ≤ C(L, M)ε₁², as above.

  {#A.9.7} In the maximum principle for λ in (KW) the boundary is Λ₀, where λ = c_i up to the increments B − v_{x̄} − w_{x̄} on the data bonds, and the layer sites of Λ are interior sites with Δλ = −σ.
- {#A.10} {#KW} *The Gradient Part (KW).* (derived, not reviewed) The steps of #0.1 are written for Bałaban's problem, with {#D.A.2} A := A_N, the *boundary sites* those of the data bonds of Λ₀, on which A = B, and the *free sites* the other sites of Λ; for the N_b problem read u, the mass bonds, and the sites of the mass graph. {#D.θ} θ := C_H^{reg}θ_B ≥ θ_B is the bulk size: ‖A‖_{Q_{2L}(x₀)} ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^pL^{d/2}θ for every x₀ of the region of (K0)(f), and in their units at the interfaces of (K0)(g), by (K0) (for every x₀ by the weighted L² decay of #0.1 in the N_b problem). In the N_b problem E(Q_L(x₀)) ≤ Ē = C(d)(1 + log L)^{2p}L^{d−2}θ² (#0.1.20) by Caccioppoli at the scale L. In VAR's problem the energy of A_N near a face of Λ₀ is of order L^{d−1}θ_B² per block, and Ē is the bulk bound ‖da‖²_{Q_L(x₀)} ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^{2p}L^{d−2}θ² of the residual a = A_N − E (K0)(f); the curvature enters the rest only through F₁ ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^pθ, the part ∂₁*Δ^{−1}(χdE) of v_{x̄}, *VAR's interior bound.* (#0.1, *The gauge-invariant part.*), and the source ℓ_E of the hole-filling (#0.1.30). Exponents are written for d = 4, as in the bound on v of #0.1. Δ is the lattice Laplacian, 2d times the generator 𝓛 of the simple random walk (Lawler–Limic p.17: 𝓛f(y) = −f(y) + Σ_xp(x)f(x + y)), so Δ = −∂*∂ on functions. A *local component* at a cube Q′ is a component of the graph of the data bonds (mass bonds) in Q′. By *Setting.*, inside Q_{L/8} two cells of Λ₀ (of Λ^c) that share a face lie in one local component, and two that meet only in codimension ≥ 2 do so only through a chain of face-sharing cells, and sites of two distinct local components at distance ≤ ρ lie within C(d)ρ of a contact between them. t₃ is the distance to these contacts, whether or not the two cells are joined elsewhere, since the jump of λ across such a contact is not controlled by the connection elsewhere.
  - {#A.11} {#K0} {#A.11.1} (K0) Weighted decay for VAR's problem (derived, not reviewed; at the flat base U = 1, and at a real base with the additive constant δ_U ≤ 1 of #A.11.1.1–#A.11.1.6). #0.1 derives the L-uniform decay for the N_b problem only; for VAR's problem it is derived as follows. ℓ(x) denotes the side of the block of the layer containing x (1 on Λ₀, L^j on Λ_j), and "local units" are those of ℓ.

    {#A.11.1.1} *At a real base.* (derived, not reviewed) In #A.9–#A.11.1, M is PBG's block size and R₁M₁ is VAR's product, both M′ = M′(d, L) on the chain's sequences (#4.22, #4.23, #4.26, #4.27; table #T2.7, #T2.10). So every C(L, M) there is a constant of d and L. PBG's constants are uniform in M ≥ M₁ (p.397 l.38), so the covariant maps' (P2) constant K below depends on M′ only through the factor e^{¼δ₀C(d)LM′} of #A.11.1.3 (#A.11.1.4.3.2), their (P3) constant K₃ being a C(L, M′), and a = c(L, M′)a₁ with PBG's a₁ of Theorem 3.4, a constant of d and L (table #T1.4). The large-field M (#4.22.2) enters only through ε₁. The steps of (K0) and (KW) are taken at the flat base U = 1. Their pointwise conclusions hold at a real base U (defined below), point by point, with an additive constant δ_U ≤ 1. No global regular gauge of U is used, since none need exist: in an axial-type gauge the field grows with the distance (VAR (145)). *Real regular* means G-valued and satisfying PBG (3.35)–(3.36) (p.396) on PBG's class cubes, the unions of M′-blocks of table #T11.25, with M′α₀ ≤ a₀, a₀ the threshold of PBG Theorem 3.1 (p.397 l.38), and with α₀ below the threshold of Theorem 3.12 ("for α₀ sufficiently small", p.423 l.34), which #A.11.1.3–#A.11.1.4 use, an upper bound on ε₁ (#A.11.1.6); the covariant maps' constants below are uniform in such α₀.
    {#A.11.1.1-1} At the minimisers this is VAR Theorem 1 (9)–(10) (p.279) on VAR's class cubes, which is how VAR applies PBG at its base (p.280 l.51–53; H₁ with PBG's B₀ at (103), p.293). These conditions ask for a gauge on each cube, so they are gauge invariant. U₀ = U_k(V₀) and the minimisers U_k(V′V₀) at real data are real regular (VAR Theorem 1; (172)–(173), p.305, with B₃(1 + 4C₁)ε₁ at l.41), and so are their G-valued transforms, such as u_R(Re B)^{g₀^{−1}} (#A.9.3, #A.9.6). These are the {#D.real_base} *real bases* := the minimisers at real data on the chain's sequence and their G-valued transforms. Their data satisfy VAR (7) with the parameter C_Vε₁, {#D.C_V} C_V := 1 + C(d)LC₁: V₀ at ε₁; for V′V₀, abs(V′ − 1) < C₁ε₁ by (172), a plaquette inside a layer has four bonds, and on a plaquette crossing ∂Λ_j VAR (7) reads V̄ on the bonds outside Λ_j (p.278 l.40–45), an average along ≤ C(d)L finer bonds. VAR assumes C₁ to be an absolute constant (p.305 l.44), B₅ = 6B₁B₃C₁ being one with it, and C₁ = L³ at p.280 l.20, so it is taken as a constant of d and L, and so is C_V. VAR Theorem 1 at the parameter C_Vε₁, which is ≤ VAR's a₁ for ε₁ small, gives them (9)–(10) on each of VAR's class cubes with C_Vε₁ in place of ε₁, and #A.11.1.2 uses this; PBG's form alone would give α_□ only of order a₀.
    {#A.11.1.1-2} A *covariant map* (so named to distinguish it from the covariant members of #0.1.13) is a family of real-linear maps 𝒯(U) from the data to fields, defined at the real regular U and at the configurations e^{iηA′} of (3.37)–(3.38) about the base 1 with α₁ ≤ a, with constants a = c(L, M), K = C(L, M) in (P2), K₃ = C(L, M) in (P3), and c = c(L) such that, in local units and with θ_B the supremum of the data (#0.1.27), the following hold. (P1) 𝒯(U^g)B^g = (𝒯(U)B)^g for every G-valued gauge g, B^g being the data transformed at the block points (REG p.78 l.15). (P2) If two real regular U, U′ agree on a union □′ of blocks, then abs((𝒯(U) − 𝒯(U′))B(x)) ≤ Ke^{−c·d(x, □′^c)}θ_B at every point x, with d(x, □′^c) := 0 for x ∉ □′. Here d is PBG's weighted distance (p.397 l.29, cited there as (2.36) of PBG's [4], which is PRT2 (PBG p.433 l.53); PRT2's (2.36) is Σh_□² = 1, and the distance is PRT2 (2.46), p.231), in which a path in B^i(Λ_i) has (L^iη)^{−1} times its length. (P3) For A′ with values in 𝔤 and e^{iηA′} in (3.37)–(3.38) about 1 with α₁ = α, the map s ↦ 𝒯(e^{iηsA′})B(x) is analytic on abs(s) ≤ a/α and bounded by K₃θ_B there.

    {#A.11.1.2} *The comparison.* Let 𝒯 be a covariant map, U a real base (#A.11.1.1), y a point of the layer j, and W′ ≥ 1 a weight, with the flat constant K_♭ := sup_{B′}‖𝒯(1)B′‖_{W′}/θ_{B′}. Then abs(𝒯(U)B(y)) ≤ W′(y)K_♭θ_B + δθ_B, with δ := Ke^{−cM_□/(4L)} + 4K₃α_□/a and α_□ := C(d)L⁴C_VB₃M_□ε₁, a C(L)B₃M_□ε₁ with C_V of #A.11.1.1, so ‖𝒯(U)B‖_{W′} ≤ (K_♭ + δ)θ_B. Here M_□ is a multiple of R₁M₁ (VAR's M in Theorem 1), with M_□ ≥ C(d)LR₁M₁. Take the class cube □ of VAR (p.279 l.2–4) about y. If y lies at distance ≥ (M_□ + C(d)R₁M₁)L^jη from Ω_j^c, □ has the index j and the size 2M_□L^jη. Otherwise it has the index j − 1 and the size 2M′_□L^{j−1}η, with M′_□ the least multiple of R₁M₁ that is ≥ L(M_□ + C(d)R₁M₁). In both cases □ is a union of big blocks whose centre lies in a big block of y, C(d)R₁M₁ covering this shift and the margin 2R₁M₁ of □̃. Every layer of the chain's sequences (CRE's 𝐁, 𝐁″_k, and the joins) below the top one is at least R′M′ ≥ ½LM₁ wide in its units (#4.24, #4.27); the top layer of 𝐁₂ can be thin (#4.14). Write RM for this least width (PRT2 (2.2)). The widths used below are those of the layers j + 1 (first case, to miss Ω_{j+2}), j (second case, to miss Ω_{j+1}), and j − 1 (second case); when the layer j or j + 1 is the top one, the set to be missed is empty, so the top width is not used; by the choice of M₁/M′ in #A.11.1.6, RM ≥ C(d)L(M_□ + R₁M₁).
    {#A.11.1.2-1} In the first case □̃ contains y ∉ Ω_{j+1} and lies in Ω_j ∖ Ω_{j+2}. In the second it contains a point of Ω_j^c, lies in Ω_{j−1}, and misses Ω_{j+1}, which is at distance ≥ (RM − M_□ − C(d)R₁M₁)L^jη from y. The second case needs the index j − 1, so at j = 0 only the first case is used, and it suffices. On the data bonds of Λ₀ the maps to which this comparison is applied return the datum independently of U: Q(U) is the identity there, so H₁(U)B = B; ω_H and ω_♮ lie in N(Q′) and vanish on Λ₀, where Q′ = P, so A_N(U)B = A_♮ = B; and f_ξ = 0, so 𝒫_Uξ = 0 there (#A.11.1.4–#A.11.1.5). So 𝒯(U)B = 𝒯(1)B there, and the claim holds with the δ term unused. The other bonds of Λ₀ touch Ω₁, at distance ≥ RMη ≥ (M_□ + C(d)R₁M₁)η from Ω₀^c, where the first case applies. This covers the sequences whose Ω₀ is not the whole lattice, such as 𝐁₂, supported in (Ω″^∼_{h+1})^c (LFR II p.370 l.23; #4.261). So □ is in VAR's class, with the index j_□ ∈ {j − 1, j} and the size parameter M_c ∈ {M_□, M′_□}, M_c ≤ C(d)LM_□, and M_c ≤ M(C_Vε₁) = R₁M₁a₁/(C_Vε₁) for ε₁ small. VAR Theorem 1 gives a G-valued gauge u, extended G-valued to all points, with U^{u^{−1}} = e^{iηA₀} on □ and the bounds (9)–(10) at C_Vε₁ (#A.11.1.1). Let χ be 1 on the middle half □_{1/2}, a union of big blocks, and 0 off □, with abs(∇^kχ) ≤ C(d)(M_cL^{j_□}η)^{−k} for k ≤ 2.
    {#A.11.1.2-2} Then U_□ := e^{iηχA₀} on □, and 1 elsewhere, is real regular with α₀ = α_□/M′, the gauge 1 serving on every class cube, each of size ≥ 10M′, and M′α₀ = α_□ ≤ a₀ for ε₁ small; it lies in (3.37)–(3.38) about 1 with α₁ = α_□: by (9)–(10) and the product rule, abs(χA₀), abs(∇(χA₀)), and abs(∂*∂(χA₀)) are ≤ C(d)C_VB₃M_cε₁(L^{j_□}η)^{−k}, k = 1, 2, 3, and the points of □ in the layer j_□ + 1 carry the factor L^k. By (P1), Ad(u(y)) being an isometry, abs(𝒯(U)B(y)) = abs(𝒯(U^{u^{−1}})B_u(y)), with B_u := B^{u^{−1}} and θ_{B_u} = θ_B. U^{u^{−1}} and U_□ agree on □_{1/2}. A path from y out of □_{1/2} has length ≥ M_□L^jη/2 − C(d)R₁M₁L^jη in B^{j_□}(Λ_{j_□}) ∪ B^{j_□+1}(Λ_{j_□+1}), so d(y, □_{1/2}^c) ≥ M_□/(4L), and (P2) gives abs((𝒯(U^{u^{−1}}) − 𝒯(U_□))B_u(y)) ≤ Ke^{−cM_□/(4L)}θ_B. Along s ↦ e^{iηsχA₀}, (P3) and Cauchy's bound on the disc abs(s) ≤ a/α_□, of radius ≥ 2, give abs((𝒯(U_□) − 𝒯(1))B_u(y)) ≤ 2K₃θ_B/(a/α_□ − 1) ≤ 4K₃α_□θ_B/a. Finally abs(𝒯(1)B_u(y)) ≤ W′(y)K_♭θ_B, and dividing by W′(y) ≥ 1 gives the claim.

    {#A.11.1.3} *H and H₁ are covariant maps.* (P1) holds by PBG (3.32)–(3.34) (pp.395–396) for G′, R, Q, Δ_a, and the G of (3.34), which is G₀ of Sect. D. J = D*η^{−2} Im ∂U (p.419 l.11) and C^{(2)}_j are covariant, hence so are Δ′_π (3.120), G (3.130), (QGQ*)^{−1}, and H (3.126) (p.420), and Δ_π^{(2)}, G₁, and H₁ by (3.128)–(3.129) (p.421) and (3.134)–(3.138) (pp.422–423). (P2): by Theorem 3.12 (p.423), Theorem 3.10's expansion (3.107)–(3.108) holds for H and H₁ at real U satisfying (3.35)–(3.36) with α₀ small. Each walk term depends on U only on X̃₀⁵ ∪ … ∪ X̃_n⁵ (p.416 l.7–8) and is bounded as in (3.108), with the factors of (3.133). If U and U′ agree on □′, the terms of the walks with every X̃ᵢ⁵ ⊂ □′ coincide. Any other walk has a domain Xᵢ with X̃ᵢ⁵ ∩ □′^c ≠ ∅, so d(ω, x, y′) ≥ d(x, Xᵢ) ≥ d(x, □′^c) − C(d)LM, by (3.93) (p.410) and the triangle inequality, X̃ᵢ⁵ lying within d-distance C(d)LM of Xᵢ, since it can reach the layer j − 1 (#4.25), where PRT2 (2.46) weights a path by (L^{j−1}η)^{−1}. Half of the factor e^{−½δ₀d(ω,x,y′)} gives e^{−¼δ₀(d(x,□′^c) − C(d)LM)}. The other half pays the sum over y′ by PRT2's count (2.57)–(2.59), as at #0.1.12, and the walk sum converges by the factors O(M^{−1/2})^{abs(ω)} as in PBG. So (P2) holds with c = δ₀/4 and K = C(L)e^{¼δ₀C(d)LM′}, M = M′ (#A.11.1.1), δ₀ being the common rate of these operators (p.423 l.39–40).
    {#A.11.1.3-1} (P3): Theorem 3.4 (p.400) gives G′, (Q′G′²Q′*)^{−1}, R, and G₀ analytic on (3.37) for α₁ ≤ a₁, with the bounds of Theorems 3.1–3.3; the G of Theorem 3.4 is the G₀ = (Δ + DRD* + Q*aQ)^{−1} of Sect. D (p.421 l.33). Along s ↦ U(s) := e^{iηsA′}, abs(s) ≤ s₁ := a₁/α, J(U(s)), the continuation of D*η^{−2} Im ∂U with U(∂p)^{−1} in place of U(∂p)*, and Δ′_π(U(s)) of (3.120) (built from G′, R, D, and J) are analytic and bounded by C(L, M) in the norms of (3.131) (p.422). Both vanish at s = 0, where J = 0 and Δ_π = Δ (p.419; #A.11.25). By the Schwarz lemma, applied to each kernel entry, they are ≤ C(L, M)abs(s)/s₁ on abs(s) ≤ s₁. So, for abs(s) ≤ s₂ := c(L, M)s₁, the series (3.130) for G converges as on p.422 l.12–13. (QGQ*(U(s)))^{−1} is the Neumann series about U = 1, with (3.132) at U = 1 and the difference QGQ*(U(s)) − QGQ*(1) ≤ C(L, M)abs(s)/s₂ by Cauchy's bound, convergent for abs(s) ≤ c(L, M)s₂. H follows by (3.126); Δ^{(2)} and Δ_π^{(2)} by (3.134)–(3.136), with abs(H*J) ≤ C(L, M)abs(s)/s₁; G₁ by (3.138) (p.423); (QG₁Q*)^{−1} as for G; and H₁ by (3.129). Each is analytic and bounded by C(L, M) on abs(s) ≤ s₂ (shrinking s₂ by a factor c(L, M) at each step), so (P3) holds with a = c(L, M)a₁.

    {#A.11.1.4} *A_N is a covariant map.* At a real regular U let {#D.A_N(U)} A_N(U)B := H₁(U)B − D_Uω_H(U)B, with ω_H(U)B the element of N(Q′(U)) least for ‖H₁(U)B − D_Uω‖. The part ⟨A, Δ_πA⟩ − 2⟨HC_π^{(2)}(A), J⟩ of (3.128) is invariant under the gauges of N(Q′(U)), A − DG′RD*A being so (p.419 l.26–28). Every A is carried by such a gauge to A − DG′RD*A, which has RD*(A − DG′RD*A) = 0 ((3.119), p.419), and Q(D_Uλ) = D̄Q′λ = 0 for λ ∈ N(Q′(U)) (PBG (3.115), p.418). So, as in #A.11.25, the minimisers of that part under QA = B form the class H₁(U)B + D_UN(Q′(U)), H₁(U)B being the minimiser with RD*A = 0 ((3.127)–(3.129), p.421). A_N(U)B is the ℓ²-least element of this class. #A.9's A_N at the base U is A_N(U)B + 𝒫_Uξ_ω + Π_Ue_a, with the terms of #A.11.1.4.1, which vanish at U = 1 and are bounded in #A.11.1.4.1.1–#A.11.1.4.3.3. At U = 1, where J = 0 and Δ′_π = Δ_π^{(2)} = 0, so H₁(1) = H₀, it is the split's A_N = H₀B − ∂ω_H (#A.11.25). (P1) holds since the ℓ² norm is Ad-invariant and D_U and Q′(U) are covariant. Sup bound: ω_H(U) satisfies ⟨D_Uω_H − f, D_Uζ⟩ = 0 for ζ ∈ N(Q′(U)), f := H₁(U)B, the problem of #A.9.1 with ω_g = 0 at a real background, with the covariant per-block Poincaré bound of #0.1.30, whose plaquette condition VAR (2) holds for U and for U_□ (abs(U_□(∂p) − 1) ≤ C(d)α_□L^{−2j}). So #A.9.1–#A.9.2 bound abs(ηω_H) by C(L, M)θ_B.
    {#A.11.1.4-1} Since Q′ω_H = 0, Δ′_aω_H = D_U^*D_Uω_H, so ω_H = G′(U)(D_U^*f + Q′(U)^*ν), and D_Uω_H is bounded pointwise by PBG (3.42)–(3.44) (pp.397–398) for ∇_UG′∇_U^*, with the Hölder norm of f from (3.133) for H₁ (Theorem 3.12) and abs(ν(y)) ≤ C(d)ℓ_y^{d/2−1}‖D_Uω_H − f‖_{y⁺} (#A.9.1). (P2): let U, U′ agree on □′, ω := ω_H(U)B, ω′ := ω_H(U′)B, y ∈ □′, and S := d(y, □′^c). ω′ is not compared with ω off □′: there U and U′ may differ by O(1) on each bond, so D_U − D_{U′} would be a source of the size abs(ω′)/η, L^j times a field of the layer j. For S ≤ C(L), (P2) is the sup bound at U and at U′, so let S ≥ C(L). Let φ be a cutoff equal to 1 at d-distance ≤ S/2 from y and 0 at d-distance ≥ 3S/4, with abs(∂φ) ≤ C(d)ℓ^{−1}/S, and ω̂ := φω′ − Σ_{y′}Q′(U)(φω′)(y′)b^U_{y′}, with b^U_{y′} the bumps of #A.9.4 (i) at U. The sum runs over the blocks where φ is not constant, on which Q′(U)(φω′)(y′) = Q′(U)((φ − φ(y′))ω′)(y′) ≤ C(L)S^{−1}abs(ω′), a block having d-diameter ≤ C(d)L, since U = U′ on supp φ and Q′(U′)ω′ = 0. So ω̂ ∈ N(Q′(U)). For ζ ∈ N(Q′(U)), ζ′ := φζ − Σ_{y′}Q′(U′)(φζ)(y′)b^{U′}_{y′} lies in N(Q′(U′)), with the same bound, and ⟨D_{U′}ω′ − H₁(U′)B, D_{U′}ζ′⟩ = 0. Since D_U = D_{U′} on supp φ, ω − ω̂ ∈ N(Q′(U)) satisfies ⟨D_U(ω − ω̂) − φg, D_Uζ⟩ = ⟨h₁, D_Uζ⟩ + ⟨h₂, ζ⟩ for ζ ∈ N(Q′(U)).
    {#A.11.1.4-2} Here g := H₁(U)B − H₁(U′)B is ≤ Ke^{−cS/4}θ_B on supp φ by (P2) for H₁. h₁ collects (1 − φ)H₁(U)B, the terms of ∂φ times ω′, and the bump terms, and h₂ the terms of ∂φ times D_{U′}ω′ − H₁(U′)B and the bump terms. They are covariant fields, so their pointwise norms do not depend on the gauge, and they are supported at d-distance ≥ S/2 from y, with abs(h₁) ≤ C(L, M)θ_B and abs(h₂) ≤ C(L, M)ℓ^{−1}θ_B by the sup bounds at U and U′. The weighted test of #A.9.1, with w := e^{−δρ(·, y)}, δ := c(d)min(1, δ₀) so that the decay of G′(U) at the rate δ₀ in (3.42)–(3.44) dominates the weight in the pointwise step below, δRM ≥ (d + 2)log L by #A.11.1.6, and c(d)d − C(d) ≤ ρ ≤ C(d)(d + 1), both weighting a path by the inverse sides of its blocks, the first for the decay of the weight and the second for that of G′(U), and the per-block Poincaré bound turning ⟨h₂, w²(ω − ω̂)⟩ into ‖wℓh₂‖‖wD_U(ω − ω̂)‖, gives ‖wD_U(ω − ω̂)‖ ≤ C(d)(‖wφg‖ + ‖wh₁‖ + ‖wℓh₂‖) ≤ C(L, M)e^{−c′S}θ_B, with c′ := min(c(d)δ, c)/8, the block sides and the count being paid by the other half of the weight as in (s2). ω̂ = ω′ at d-distance ≤ S/2 from y.
    {#A.11.1.4-3} The pointwise bound at y follows from D_U^*D_U(ω − ω̂) = D_U^*(φg + h₁) + h₂ + Q′(U)^*ν̃, with ν̃ bounded by the weighted energy as in #A.9.1, through G′(U) and the decay of (3.42)–(3.44) at U. The Hölder inputs come from (3.133) and Theorem 3.10's corresponding inequalities for the norms of (3.42)–(3.47), so (P2) for H₁ holds in these norms by the same walk bounds. (P3): at U(s) = e^{iηsA′}, #A.9.4 applies with U_re = 1 and C(d)abs(s)α ≤ c(d) in place of its α. The stationarity system is finite, analytic in s through D_{U(s)}, Q′(U(s)), and H₁(U(s))B (#A.11.1.3), and uniquely solvable by the weighted bound, so ω_H(U(s))B is analytic in s, and D_{U(s)}ω_H is bounded through G′(U(s)) (Theorem 3.4) as above.

    {#A.11.1.4.1} *#A.9's A_N at a real base.* (derived, not reviewed) Let U be the base of #0.1.11, the minimiser at the real data, or a G-valued transform of it, and let a be the first-order part of u_R relative to U. u_R satisfies the Landau condition (21) relative to VAR's base U₀ = U_k(V₀) (#A.11.1.4.4.4.2), and a = H₁(U)Q(U)a + e_a + D_Uν_a, with e_a ≤ C(L, M′)ε₁θ_{B₁} in the norms of (3.133), e_a = 0 at U = 1, and ν_a ∈ N(Q′(U)) (#A.11.1.4.4.4–#A.11.1.4.4.4.2). #A.9 writes its A_N as a − D_Uω exactly, with ω vanishing on Λ₀ and {#D.ξ_ω} ξ_ω := Q′(U)ω the contour term KU′_ax of #A.9, and A_N is ℓ²-least in A_N + D_UN(Q′(U)) (#A.11.2 heading). Let {#D.Π_U} Π_U := the ℓ²-orthogonal projection onto the complement of D_UN(Q′(U)), so that Π_U takes each field to the ℓ²-least element of its class and A_N(U) = Π_UH₁(U) (#A.11.1.4), and put B := Q(U)A_N, the data of #A.9's A_N (#A.11.2 (a)). Then, Π_U annihilating D_Uν_a, A_N = Π_U(a − D_Uω) = Π_U(H₁(U)Q(U)(A_N + D_Uω) + e_a − D_Uω) = A_N(U)B + 𝒫_Uξ_ω + Π_Ue_a, with {#D.𝒫_U} 𝒫_Uξ := Π_U(H₁(U)Q(U)D_Uλ_ξ − D_Uλ_ξ) and {#D.λ_ξ} λ_ξ := Σ_yξ(y)b^U_y, the bumps of #A.9.4 (i) at U. Indeed ν_ω := ω − λ_{ξ_ω} has Q′(U)ν_ω = 0 and vanishes on Λ₀, so Q(U)D_Uν_ω = 0 (PBG (3.115)) and Π_UD_Uν_ω = 0.
      {#A.11.1.4.1.1} *The pairing term.* (derived, not reviewed) Π_Ue_a = e_a − D_Uω_e, with ω_e ∈ N(Q′(U)) least for ‖e_a − D_Uω‖, the problem of #A.11.1.4 with the source e_a in place of H₁(U)B. Its sup bound uses of the source only its sup and Hölder norms, so abs(Π_Ue_a) ≤ C(L, M′)ε₁θ_{B₁} ≤ C(L, M′)ε₁(θ_B + 2θ_{ξ_ω}) ≤ C(L, M′)ε₁θ_B, by #A.11.1.4.4.4.1 and #A.11.1.4.3.3. It vanishes at U = 1, and δ_U covers it (#A.11.1.5.3).
      {#A.11.1.4.2} 𝒫_U is a covariant map on the 𝔤-valued functions ξ at the block points of the layers ≥ 1 (ξ_ω = Q′(U)ω vanishes on Λ₀, where Q′ = P and ω = 0), which transform by ξ^g(y) = Ad(g(y))ξ(y), with θ_ξ := sup abs(ηξ) in local units. (P1) holds since Π_U, H₁(U), Q(U), D_U, and the bumps are covariant. For (P2) and (P3), 𝒫_Uξ is the problem of #A.11.1.4 with the source {#D.f_ξ} f_ξ(U) := H₁(U)Q(U)D_Uλ_ξ − D_Uλ_ξ in place of H₁(U)B, and that proof uses of the source only its covariance, its sup and Hölder bounds, its (P2), and its analyticity in s. f_ξ has sup and Hölder bounds C(L)θ_ξ, by (3.133) for H₁ (Theorem 3.12) and the bounds of the bumps.
        {#A.11.1.4.2.1} *(P2), (P3), and U = 1.* If U and U′ agree on □′, f_ξ(U) − f_ξ(U′) is the sum of three terms. The first, (H₁(U) − H₁(U′))Q(U)D_Uλ_ξ, is ≤ Ke^{−c·d(x,□′^c)}θ_ξ by (P2) for H₁. The second is H₁(U′) applied to Q(U)D_Uλ^U_ξ − Q(U′)D_{U′}λ^{U′}_ξ = (D̄_U − D̄_{U′})ξ: Q′(U)λ^U_ξ = ξ for every U, so Q(U)D_Uλ^U_ξ = D̄_Uξ by PBG (3.115), with D̄_U := D_{Ū^j} the covariant difference in the transports of U's averages (p.418), which depend on U. (D̄_U − D̄_{U′})ξ vanishes on the coarse bonds whose blocks lie in □′, where Ū_c = Ū′_c, and on the others, which lie at d-distance ≤ C(d)L from □′^c, it is ≤ 2abs(ξ(c₊)), the transports being unitary at real U. By (3.133) for H₁(U′), with the layer factor paid under δ₁RM ≥ 8 log L and the sum over y′ by PRT2 (2.58)–(2.59), as in #A.11.26, the second term is ≤ C(L)e^{−(δ₁/8)d(x,□′^c)}θ_ξ, and the same holds in the Hölder norms that #A.11.1.4 uses, by the derivative and Hölder entries of (3.133). The third, D_{U′}λ^{U′}_ξ − D_Uλ^U_ξ, vanishes unless x lies in, or next to, a block that meets □′^c, since b^U_y depends on U only on the block of y; there d(x, □′^c) ≤ C(d)L, and the sup bound serves. So f_ξ satisfies (P2) with the rate min(c, δ₁/8) and C(L)K. For (P3), H₁(U(s)), Q(U(s)), D_{U(s)}, and b^{U(s)}_y are analytic in s (#A.11.1.3, #A.9.4 (i)), so f_ξ(U(s)) is analytic, and the rest is as in #A.11.1.4. At U = 1, 𝒫_1 = 0. H₀Q∂λ_ξ minimises ‖da‖² on 𝒞 with the data of ∂λ_ξ (#A.11.25), and so does ∂λ_ξ, since ‖d∂λ_ξ‖ = 0. The minimisers differ by ∂N(Q′) (#A.11.2 (a)), so Π_1 annihilates H₀Q∂λ_ξ − ∂λ_ξ. By #A.11.1.2 with K_♭ = 0, abs(𝒫_Uξ(y)) ≤ δθ_ξ.
      {#A.11.1.4.3} *The data suprema.* (derived, not reviewed) In #A.11.1.4.1–#A.11.1.4.2, as in the chain, θ_B is the supremum of the data B = Q(U)A_N of #A.11.2 (a), RG I's data up to the crossing shift −S_bU′_ax at every interface at U = 1 (#0.1.4 at j = 1, #0.1.12), and further up to −E(U)U′_ax at a real base (#A.11.1.4.3.4), and K_♭ is measured against it. Let {#D.B₁} B₁ := Q(U)a, the input of H₁(U) in #A.11.1.4.1. B₁ = Q(U)(A_N + D_Uω) = B + D̄ξ_ω (#A.11.1.4.1, PBG (3.115)), so θ_{B₁} ≤ θ_B + 2θ_{ξ_ω}, and the bound of θ_{ξ_ω} below uses B₁ only through this. By #A.11.1.4.4.2, θ_{ξ_ω} ≤ C_ξ sup abs(F), with {#D.C_ξ} C_ξ := C(d)L² times the geometric series over the finer scales, a constant of d and L, and F the first-order plaquette variables of U′_ax at the scales of #A.11.1.4.4.2 in local units, averages of its fine ones at the flat base, D̄K being curl-free. U′_ax and u_R differ by a G-valued gauge (#A.9), so their plaquette variables are conjugate, and at first order those of u_R are η²(D_Ua)(p), up to terms ≤ C(L, M′)B₃ε₁(θ_B + θ_{ξ_ω}) from the base's plaquettes, abs(a) being ≤ C(L)θ_{B₁}: the linearisations of Ad(u)P and of e^{iηa}U about a base in VAR's space (2) with ε₀ = O(1)B₃ε₁ (p.304 l.52), and of the averages over the scales, carry commutators with U(∂p) − 1. #A.11.1.4.3.3 bounds D_Ua and closes the bound. These are bounds of real-linear maps at the real base.
        {#A.11.1.4.3.1} *The constants of the two maps.* Hence #A.9's A_N at U obeys the bounds of A_N(U) with δ replaced by (1 + C(L) + C(L, M′)ε₁)δ, δ being here the larger of the δ of #A.11.1.2 for A_N(U) and that for 𝒫_U, each with its own (P2) constants: #A.11.1.4's argument turns a source of rate c_s and constant K_s into the rate min(c(d)min(1, δ₀), c_s)/8 (#A.11.1.4's c′) and a constant C(L, M′)K_s, so A_N(U) has the rate min(c(d)min(1, δ₀), c)/8 and 𝒫_U, whose source f_ξ has the rate min(c, δ₁/8) and the constant C(L)K (#A.11.1.4.2.1), has the rate min(c(d)min(1, δ₀), c, δ₁/8)/8 and a constant C(L, M′)C(L)K, all rates constants of d and L; δ_U bounds both (#A.11.1.5.3).
        {#A.11.1.4.3.2} *The M′-dependence.* (derived, not reviewed) At a real base, and at the real regular pairs (U^{u^{−1}}, U_□) to which #A.11.1.2 applies (P2), the factor C(L, M′) of #A.11.1.4.3.1 is, in (P2), a C(L), a constant of d and L independent of M′. #A.11.1.4's (P2) argument uses four inputs. First, the sup bounds at U and U′, which are #A.9.1–#A.9.2 with ω_g = 0: the per-block Poincaré bound of #0.1.30 has constants of d only at a real background, its factor 1 + C(L, M)ε₁ arising at the complex ones (#A.9.4), and #A.9.2's bound of sup_{block}abs(ω₀) has the constant C(d, L), the sum over y″ being paid under δRM ≥ (d + 2)log L; the C(L, M) of #A.9.2's last bound multiplies the complex parts Im u_R and Im U′_ax, which vanish at a real base. Second, the source's sup and Hölder bounds, C(L)θ_B for H₁(U)B by (3.133) (Theorem 3.12) and C(L)θ_ξ for f_ξ (#A.11.1.4.2). Third, the pointwise step through G′(U), by PBG (3.42)–(3.44), whose constants are of d and L, uniform in M ≥ M₁ (p.397 l.38). Fourth, the threshold S ≥ C(L), the bump bounds, and the weighted count, each a C(L). So the C(L, M) of #A.11.1.4's bounds of h₁, h₂, and the weighted energy are C(L) at a real base, and the (P2) constants are C(L)K for A_N(U) and for 𝒫_U, K = C(L)e^{¼δ₀C(d)LM′} being that of H₁ (#A.11.1.3), as #A.11.1.1 states. The (P3) constants K₃ are C(L, M′) (#A.11.1.3, #A.11.1.4). #A.11.1.2 uses them only in its term 4K₃α_□/a, its term Ke^{−cM_□/(4L)} using the (P2) constant, so the K of #A.11.1.6's order is the (P2) constant, and the (P3) constant is paid by ε₁ through α_□, a C(L)B₃M_□ε₁ (#A.11.1.2), ε₁ being chosen last. Hence the constant of δ_U's first term is ≤ C(L)e^{¼δ₀C(d)LM′}, the factor 1 + C(L) + C(L, M′)ε₁ of #A.11.1.4.3.1 being ≤ 2 + C(L) for ε₁ ≤ 1/C(L, M′).
        {#A.11.1.4.3.3} *The curvature.* (derived, not reviewed) By #A.11.1.4.1, a = H₁(U)B₁ + e_a + D_Uν_a = H₁(U)B + H₁(U)D̄_Uξ_ω + e_a + D_Uν_a, and D̄_Uξ = Q(U)D_Uλ_ξ by PBG (3.115), so H₁(U)D̄_Uξ = f_ξ(U) + D_Uλ_ξ (#A.11.1.4.2). Hence D_Ua = D_UH₁(U)B + D_Uf_ξ(U) + D_UD_Uλ_ξ + D_Ue_a + D_UD_Uν_a, with D_U the covariant curl on fields, and the last two terms are ≤ C(L, M′)ε₁(θ_B + 2θ_{ξ_ω}) by #A.11.1.4.4.4.1–#A.11.1.4.4.4.2 and θ_{B₁} ≤ θ_B + 2θ_{ξ_ω}. By (3.133) for H₁ and ∇H₁ (Theorem 3.12, p.423), whose O(1) are PBG's constants of d and L, uniform in M ≥ M₁ (Theorem 3.1, p.397 l.38), with its layer factor L^{abs(j_x − j′)} paid under δ₁RM ≥ 8 log L and the sum over y′ by PRT2 (2.58)–(2.59), as in #A.11.26, the first term is ≤ C(L)θ_B in local units. The third is the commutator of λ_ξ with the base's plaquettes, ≤ C(L)B₃ε₁θ_{ξ_ω}. For the second, let {#D.𝒞_U} 𝒞_Uξ := D_Uf_ξ(U) in local units, a family of real-linear maps on the ξ of #A.11.1.4.2. (P1) holds since f_ξ and the curl are covariant. (P2) holds with the rate and constant of f_ξ (#A.11.1.4.2.1), whose bound holds in the derivative and Hölder norms of (3.133), D_U and D_{U′} agreeing on the plaquettes in □′. (P3) holds since f_ξ(U(s)) is analytic and bounded with its derivatives, by #A.11.1.3's (P3) for H₁ in the norms of (3.133) and by #A.9.4 (i) for the bumps. At U = 1, f_ξ(1) ∈ ∂N(Q′) (#A.11.1.4.2.1), so 𝒞_1 = 0. By #A.11.1.2 with K_♭ = 0, abs(𝒞_Uξ) ≤ δ_𝒞θ_ξ, with {#D.δ_𝒞} δ_𝒞 := the δ of #A.11.1.2 for 𝒞_U. So θ_{ξ_ω} ≤ C_ξ(C(L)θ_B + (δ_𝒞 + C(L, M′)ε₁)θ_{ξ_ω}) + C_ξC(L, M′)ε₁θ_B, and under C_ξ(δ_𝒞 + C(L, M′)ε₁) ≤ ½ (#A.11.1.6.1), θ_{ξ_ω} ≤ (C(L) + C(L, M′)ε₁)θ_B, with C(L) = 2C_ξC(L) a constant of d and L only, independent of M′. At U = 1 the second and third terms and the base's terms vanish, and θ_{ξ_ω} ≤ C_ξC(L)θ_B directly. Neither #A.9's C(L, M) nor VAR (190) enters, and B₁ enters only through θ_{B₁} ≤ θ_B + 2θ_{ξ_ω} with the factor ε₁, so the bound is not circular.
        {#A.11.1.4.3.4} *RG I's data at a real base.* (derived, not reviewed) At first order RG I's datum of the configuration is {#D.B′_U} B′_U := Q̃(U)U′_ax (#A.11.1.4.4.4). Q(U)U′_ax = B₁, since u_R − U′_ax = D_Uζ^R with Q′(U)ζ^R = 0 at first order (#A.9; PBG p.394 l.1–2) and Q(U)D_Uζ^R = 0 by (3.115). K(U)U′_ax = ξ_ω at the block points of the layers ≥ 1 (#A.11.1.4.1), ξ_ω(y) being the composite over y's own block up to y's level (#A.11.1.4.4.2). On a crossing bond b from Λ_{j−1} to Λ_j, j ≥ 1, the average carries a further factor at every interface (REG p.81 l.36–44): the mean over x ∈ B(b₋), the L-block of the scale-(j−1) lattice, of the line integrals of the level-(j−1) averages along the contours from b₋ to x, the 𝐆-means in RG I's pairing. Its first-order part is {#D.S_b} S_bU′_ax := that mean for the first-order field, and ξ_ω(b₋) does not contain it. At j = 1 it is #0.1.4's KU′_ax(b₋), with ξ_ω(b₋) = 0. So B′_U = B + S_bU′_ax + E(U)U′_ax on the crossing bonds, #0.1.4's and #0.1.12's shifted datum, with S_bU′_ax transported, and B′_U = B + E(U)U′_ax on the others.
          {#A.11.1.4.3.4.1} *The one-sided bound.* (derived, not reviewed) abs(E(U)U′_ax) ≤ C(L)α₀ sup abs(U′_ax) in local units (#A.11.1.4.4.4). On every bond U′_ax is its datum plus at most C(d)L² of its first-order plaquette variables (#A.11.1.4.4.1, #A.9.2), up to relative corrections C(L)α₀ from the linearisations of (0.4) and (1.19) at U, and, on the fine bonds of a crossing bond's path, minus the crossing term, whose contours (1.19) does not fix (#A.11.1.4.4.3), ≤ C(d)Lθ_{B′_U}, which costs another C(L) below. The plaquette variables of u_R are η²(D_Ua)(p) up to the commutators of a with the base's plaquettes, so they are ≤ C(L)N(a). At first order U′_ax = u_R − D_Uζ^R, so the plaquette variables of U′_ax differ from those of u_R by the commutator of ζ^R with the base's plaquettes, ≤ C(L)B₃ε₁abs(ηζ^R). By #A.9's scalar problem, abs(ηζ^R) ≤ C(L)(sup abs(u_R) + sup abs(U′_ax)), with sup abs(u_R) ≤ N(a). N(a) ≤ C(L)θ_{B′_U} by (190) (#A.11.1.4.4.4.2.2.1). So sup abs(U′_ax) ≤ C(L)θ_{B′_U} + C(L)B₃ε₁ sup abs(U′_ax), and sup abs(U′_ax) ≤ 2C(L)θ_{B′_U} for C(L)B₃ε₁ ≤ ½. S_bU′_ax is a mean of the line integrals of ≤ dL level-(j−1) averages on bonds inside Λ_{j−1}, which are data of the layer j − 1 on bonds that do not cross, where B′_U = B + E(U)U′_ax. So, in the units of #0.1.12, abs(S_bU′_ax) ≤ C(d)L(θ_B + C(L)α₀θ_{B′_U}), as #0.1.4 has at j = 1. So θ_{B′_U} ≤ (1 + C(d)L)θ_B + C(L)α₀θ_{B′_U}, and θ_{B′_U} ≤ 2(1 + C(d)L)θ_B for C(L)α₀ ≤ ½. This uses neither #A.11.1.4.3.3 nor ν_a, and it gives N(a) in #A.11.1.4.4.4.2.2. At U = 1, E(U) = 0, and B′_U = B off the crossing bonds.
          {#A.11.1.4.3.4.2} *The conversion per level.* (derived, not reviewed) The chain's response is bounded against A_N's data B, and the next level reads RG I's data. At a real base the two differ by the flat chain's crossing shift S_bU′_ax at every interface (#0.1.4, #0.1.12, #A.11.1.4.3.4) and by E(U)U′_ax, with abs(E(U)U′_ax) ≤ C(L)α₀ sup abs(U′_ax) ≤ C(L)α₀θ_{B′_U} by #A.11.1.4.3.4.1. At a real base S_b reads B + E(U)U′_ax on the layer j − 1, so it is the flat shift of B up to S(E(U)U′_ax) ≤ C(d)LC(L)α₀θ_{B′_U}. So the conversion is the flat one with the factor 1 + C(L)α₀, not a factor 2. C_H being a constant of d and L, the term (C_H + δ_U)C(L)α₀ ≤ C(L)B₃C_Vε₁, δ_U ≤ 1, is covered by δ_U's second term C(L, M)M_□²ε₁, whose constant is taken so (#A.11.1.5.3), and the factor per level of #0.1.10 and #0.1.42 keeps the form (C_H + δ_U).
      {#A.11.1.4.4} *The contour term at first order.* (derived, not reviewed) At first order about the base, ξ_ω = KU′_ax is a sum of loop terms of the plaquette variables of U′_ax (#A.11.1.4.4.2), and #A.11.1.4.3–#A.11.1.4.3.3 bound it. 𝒫_Uξ_ω is the term bounded by δθ_ξ (#A.11.1.4.2.1). REG (1.19) (p.79) sets, at every level n and for every x_n ∈ B(x_{n+1}), the transported product of the level-n average Ũ′^n along Γ_{x_{n+1},x_n} to 1, a condition at every site of each block.
        {#A.11.1.4.4.1} *The pairing.* The chain takes RG I's averages (0.4) (p.253) with the axial gauge Ax_k "as in Sect. G [15]" (p.265 l.37), [15] being VAR, [14] REG, and [12] the averages of CMP 98 (p.299). That gauge is REG (1.19) on the single contours Γ_{x_{n+1},x_n}, which VAR fixes, "(see the definition (1.19) in [6])" (VAR p.280 l.44–45). RG I makes its step in this pairing: "As in Sect. G [15] we write U_k(V′V^{(k)}) = U′_k(V′)U_{k+1}, and we transform at first U′_k(V′) into the axial gauge Ax_k(T^{(k)}, U_{k+1}). … Its properties are described in Sect. G [15]" (p.265 l.37–40). LFR II applies Sect. G with RG I's averages on the layered determining sets (p.357 l.19, p.367 l.30, l.47–48). From these, the minimisers at RG I's data, their regularity, VAR Theorem 1's gauges on class cubes, and their analytic extension in the data are Bałaban's, accepted. RG I prints Sect. G's Landau form in its pairing about the non-flat base U_{k+1}, U_k(exp iB′V^{(k)}) carried to exp(iη𝐇_k(B′))U_{k+1}, "where we have used the results of Sect. G [15]" ((3.3), p.270 l.32), and RG II writes 𝐇_k(B′) = H₀B′ + 𝐀₀ − HD(H₀B′ + 𝐀₀) "By the results of Sect. G [15]" ((1.2), p.2 l.25–29); replacing the propagators of (1.3)–(1.4) by localised ones, RG II keeps for operators "having the same regularity properties and satisfying the same bounds" the solutions "having all the properties proved in [15]" (p.3 l.2–4).
        {#A.11.1.4.4.1-1} The bounds of the propagators in RG I's pairing are not printed separately; they are part of Bałaban's "By the results of Sect. G [15]" of (1.2), accepted. CRE carries RG I Sect. 3 to the layered covers, "we obtain all the formulas and bounds of Sects. 3, 4 [I] with η replaced by L^{−n}" (p.276 l.2–16), and constructs the random-walk localisation on them, applying "Theorems 3.7–3.10 [13] in their full generality" (p.276 l.18–20). So Proposition 9's Landau form exp(iη𝓗(B)) with B = (1/i)log V′, V′ RG I's data ratio, its analyticity, the conditions (19) and (21), and the bounds (190), as #A.9 and #0.1 use them, are Bałaban's in this pairing, accepted. The constraint (20) with the REG (1.31) field is not used: in this pairing Q(U)a = B₁ = B + D̄ξ_ω (#A.11.1.4.3), and #A.11.1.4.4.4 derives the first-order identity that replaces it. #A.9's data are RG I's (0.4), Ū(c) = exp[i·(the mean of (1/i)log of the holonomies of the loops Γ ∪ [x, x′] ∪ (−Γ′) ∪ (−c), based at c₋)]𝐔(c) (p.253 l.5–6). Since log is covariant under conjugation, Ū(c) ↦ u(c₋)Ū(c)u(c₊)^{−1}, so the data are invariant under the gauges with u = 1 at the block points. In this pairing #A.8's K, and the K of #A.9, are the 𝐆-means of (0.4), so #A.9's contours Γ^{(j)}_{y,x} are those of the families 𝐆(y, x), each of length ≤ dL^j in η-bonds. The contours Γ_{x_{n+1},x_n} of #A.11.1.4.4 are REG's single contours.
        {#A.11.1.4.4.1-2} In #A.9.2 the value of U′_ax on a bond b = ⟨x, x′⟩ of a block with the block point y is fixed through the loop Γ_{y,x} ∪ b ∪ (−Γ_{y,x′}), of at most 2dL + 1 bonds of the scale n. Take a coarse bond c with blocks B(c₋) and B(c₊), and the bond b of the contour [x, x′] (p.252 l.32) that joins them. At first order, by (0.4), the datum at c is the integral of the field along c plus the mean over x and over 𝐆 × 𝐆 of its integrals around the loops Γ ∪ [x, x′] ∪ (−Γ′) ∪ (−c). Each of these loops spans ≤ C(d)L² plaquettes. The field on b is its integral along c plus its integral around the loop Γ_{c₋,z} ∪ b ∪ (−Γ_{c₊,z′}) ∪ (−c), b = ⟨z, z′⟩, since (1.19) sets its integrals along the two single contours to 0. That loop also spans ≤ C(d)L² plaquettes. So the field on b is the datum plus at most C(d)L² first-order plaquette variables, and #A.9.2's bound C(d)L² holds on every bond, with another C(d).
        {#A.11.1.4.4.2} *The composites.* By (0.8), (1/i)log 𝐔(y, x) is at first order the mean over 𝐆(y, x) of the line integrals, which is the summand of the contour term K of #A.8 at the site x. The composites over the scales are taken level by level: with Q̃ = Q − D̄K at each level (#A.8) and Q_{n+1}D̄ = D̄Q′ (PBG (3.114)–(3.115)), Q̃_{n+1}Q̃^{(n)} = Q_{n+1}Q^{(n)} − D̄(Q′K^{(n)} + K_{n+1}Q̃^{(n)}), so the composite contour term at a block point of the level n + 1 is K_{n+1} on the level-n averages plus Q′ of the level-n composite, the average over the block of its values at the level-n block points. At first order (1.19) sets to 0 the line integral, along the single contour Γ_{y,x}, of the first-order field of U′_ax's level-n average. So each level's summand at a site x is the mean over Γ ∈ 𝐆(y, x) of the integrals of that field around the loops Γ ∪ (−Γ_{y,x}). Each loop has ≤ 2d(L − 1) bonds of the scale n inside the block and spans ≤ C(d)L² plaquettes of that scale. So the summand is ≤ C(d)L² times the first-order plaquette variables of U′_ax at the scale n. The composite adds these over the levels, the finer scales adding a geometric series, as in #A.11.1.4.3. On Λ₀, ξ_ω = 0 since ω = 0 there (#0.1.4).
        {#A.11.1.4.4.3} *The crossing bonds.* On a crossing bond, B is shifted by −S_bU′_ax (#A.11.1.4.3.4), −KU′_ax(b₋) at j = 1 (#0.1.4): (0.4) carries the 𝐆-mean of the line integrals along the contours in the block B(b₋) of the finer layer. The conditions (1.19) at the block points of b's layer do not fix these contours. This is the shift of the datum in #0.1.4 (there at j = 1), of size ≤ C(d)Lθ_B. At first order B₁ − B = D̄ξ_ω on every bond (#A.11.1.4.1), so on a crossing bond B₁ is B, with its 𝐆-mean, shifted by D̄ξ_ω, and #A.11.1.4.3 does not use a crossing form of B₁. Likewise δRM ≥ (d + 2)log L, with δ = c(d)min(1, δ₀) and δ₀ = δ₀(d, L) (#A.11.1.4), holds for M₁/M′ ≥ C(L), since M′ ≥ 1, and so do δ₁RM ≥ 8 log L (#A.11.1.4.3, as in #A.11.26), (δ₀/8)RM ≥ 8 log L (#A.11.1.4.4.4.2.2.1), and PRT2's (2.59) at the rates of #A.11.1.3 and #A.11.1.4.2.1, δ₁ and those rates being constants of d and L. The bound M₁/M′ ≥ C(L) does not depend on M′, so the ratio may be chosen before M′.

    {#A.11.2} {#K0.a} (a) The normalisation and the variational form. In the normalisation of RG I (0.4), whose weights are L^{−d} (p.253), Q(∂ζ) = D̄Q′ζ follows from (0.4) directly. The line integral of ∂ζ along [x, x′] is ζ(x′) − ζ(x), and its average over x ∈ B(c₋) is Q′ζ(c₊) − Q′ζ(c₋), with the transports of PBG (3.19) at a non-flat base. PBG (3.114)–(3.115) (p.418) write the same identity with scaled derivatives, which is the normalisation of CMP98 (14) (p.19), with weights L^{−(d+1)}. There it reads Q(∂ζ) = L^{−1}D̄Q′ζ, and Q̃ = Q − L^{−1}D̄K. By #A.8, ⟨dA_N, dt⟩ = ⟨μ, Q̃t⟩ = ⟨μ, Qt⟩ with D̄*μ = 0 for every t vanishing on the data bonds of Λ₀, and QA_N = B (heading). So A_N minimises ‖da‖² on {#D.𝒞.2} 𝒞 := {a = B on the data bonds, Qa = B}, the problem being convex. Let ker {#D.Q.2} Q := {D = 0 on the data bonds, QD = 0}. Its gauges are ∂λ with λ ∈ N(Q′): λ is constant on the data graph of Λ₀, and D̄Q′λ = 0 on the connected graph of 𝔅_k, so Q′λ is one constant, which λ takes on Λ₀. A_N is least in ℓ² on A_N + ∂N(Q′) (heading).

    {#A.11.3} {#K0.b} (b) The fine data. Fine data bounded only in supremum give every admissible field an energy ≳ L^{d−1}θ_B² per block face: by closedness on the unit cubes that straddle the face, the face plaquettes' curvature dB is shared by the other five plaquettes of the cube. So the fine data are taken out explicitly. Let f be a face of Λ₀ within distance L/8 (*Setting.*), B_f be B on the bonds of f's plane in Λ₀ and 0 on its other bonds, s the depth from the plane, and P_s(x′, y′) the probability that the walk from (x′, s) first meets the plane at y′. The walk meets the plane with probability 1, its normal coordinate being recurrent. P_·(·, y′) is nonnegative and harmonic on the ball of radius s/2 about (x′, s). So Lawler–Limic Theorem 6.3.8 (p.131) gives, by (6.19)–(6.20) and, for the mixed second differences ∇_e∇_{e′}P, by (6.17) applied to the harmonic function ∇_{e′}P_·(·, y′) on the ball of radius s/4 about (x′, s), which is ≤ C(d)s^{−1}P_s(x′, y′) there by (6.19) at its points and the Harnack inequality (Theorem 6.3.9, with a constant of d for this pair of balls), Σ_{y′}abs(∇P_s(x′, y′)) ≤ C(d)/s and Σ_{y′}abs(∇²P_s(x′, y′)) ≤ C(d)/s² for s above a threshold of d, and ≤ C(d) below it. Put {#D.F_tan(s)} F_tan(s) := P_s(dB_f), harmonic at depth ≥ 1 with the values dB_f on the plane, and {#D.F_n·(s)} F_{n·}(s) := −Σ_{s′>s}∂*_tanF_tan(s′). Summation by parts moves one difference, and the two of ∂*_tanF_tan, onto P_s. So abs(F_tan(s)) ≤ C(d)θ_B/max(s, 1), abs(∂*_tanF_tan(s)) ≤ C(d)θ_B/max(s, 1)², and abs(F_{n·}(s)) ≤ C(d)θ_B/max(s, 1).

    {#A.11.4} {#D.F_f} F_f := (F_tan, F_{n·}) is closed: d_tanF_tan = 0, and ∂_nF_tan = d_tanF_{n·} by the telescoping sum of Δ_nF_tan = −Δ_tanF_tan = d_tan∂*_tanF_tan. It is co-closed at every bond off the plane. At the tangential ones F_{n·}(s) − F_{n·}(s − 1) = ∂*_tanF_tan(s), and at the normal ones ∂*_tanF_{n·} = −Σ_{s′}∂*_tan∂*_tanF_tan(s′) = 0. Let E_f be the axial field equal to B_f + Σ_{s′<s}F_{n·}(s′) on the tangential bonds at depth s and to 0 on the normal ones. Then dE_f = F_f, d*dE_f = 0 off the plane, E_f = B on f, and abs(E_f) ≤ C(d)θ_B(1 + log max(s, 1)). Let {χ_f} be a partition of unity on the free bonds within L/16 of Λ₀, homogeneous of degree 0 about each stratum (angular sectors). Here the *faces* are the facets, of side L, of the blocks of side L of Λ₀ that lie in ∂Λ₀, {#D.Y_f} Y_f := the block of which f is a facet, and the *strata* are the (d − 2)-dimensional faces of these facets, among them the strata of codimension ≥ 2 of ∂Λ₀ and the contacts of distinct local components (#A.10). Since B_f is B on all the bonds of f's plane in Λ₀, F_f and E_f depend on f only through its plane and the side of H₋(f). On a free bond χ_f is its value at the endpoint farther from Λ₀ (either, if the two are equally far).
    {#A.11.4-1} On the lattice, the closure of f is the set of the data bonds in the plane of the outer sites of Y_f next to f that have an endpoint among these sites, and on the data bonds χ_f := 1/n_b on the bonds b of the closure of f, n_b the number of faces whose closures contain b, so Σ_fχ_f = 1 on the edge bonds as well, and χ_f = 0 on the other data bonds; on the free bonds of f's interior half-space H₋(f), at the sites x whose foot on f's plane lies off f with dist(x, f's plane) ≤ c(d)dist(x, ∂f), and at the sites x with dist(x, f′) ≤ c(d)dist(x, S) for each other face f′ whose closure meets that of f, in S. abs(∇χ_f) ≤ C(d)/max(r, 1), r the distance to the strata. On the free sites such a partition is {#D.χ_f} χ_f := ψ_f/Σ_{f′}ψ_{f′} with {#D.ψ_f} ψ_f := ζ(dist(·, f)/dist(·, Λ₀))ζ₁(s_f/dist(·, Λ₀)), s_f the signed depth from f's plane, positive off H₋(f), ζ = 1 on [1, 1 + c(d)] and 0 on [1 + 2c(d), ∞), and ζ₁ = 0 on (−∞, 1/(4√d)] and 1 on [1/(2√d), ∞). Let p be the point of Λ₀ nearest to x and σ ∋ p a block of Λ₀. Then x − p = Σ_μλ_μn_μ, λ_μ ≥ 0, over the outward normals n_μ of the facets of σ through p, one per direction. Those with λ_μ > 0 are faces, since otherwise the block across, which contains p + εn_μ for small ε > 0, would contain points closer to x. So some λ_μ ≥ dist(x, Λ₀)/√d, that face has ψ = 1, and Σψ ≥ 1. The distances are homogeneous of degree 1 about each stratum.
    {#A.11.4-2} For c(d) small, ζ or ζ₁ vanishes where the conditions above require: on H₋(f), s_f ≤ 0; where the foot lies off f with s_f ≤ c(d)dist(x, ∂f), dist(x, f) = dist(x, ∂f), so either s_f ≤ dist(x, Λ₀)/(4√d) or the ratio is ≥ 1/(4√dc(d)); and where dist(x, f′) ≤ c(d)dist(x, S) for another face f′, dist(x, S) ≤ √2(dist(x, f) + dist(x, f′)), so the ratio is ≥ dist(x, f)/dist(x, f′) ≥ (1/√2 − c(d))/c(d). Here the closures of f and f′ are products of a point and intervals in single coordinates, meeting in S, and the distance to the intersection of two such products is ≤ √2 times the sum of the distances to them, coordinate by coordinate. Let D := dist(x, Λ₀). If r ≥ 3D/2 + 4 at x, then the ball B(x, 3D/2 + 4), of diameter < L for L ≥ 128, meets no stratum and meets at most one hyperplane of the block faces in each direction. So ∂Λ₀ ∩ B(x, 3D/2 + 4) consists of hyperplane sections of the ball, each inside one face, at most one per direction, and two of different directions within (1 + 2c(d))(D + 1) + 1 of x would meet within √2((1 + 2c(d))(D + 1) + 1) < 3D/2 + 4 of x in a stratum. Hence at both endpoints of a bond at x only the face of p is within the factor 1 + 2c(d) of dist(·, Λ₀), with s_f = dist(·, Λ₀), and every χ_f is constant on the bond. On the other bonds abs(∇ψ_f) ≤ C(d)/max(D, 1) ≤ C(d)/max(r, 1).
    {#A.11.4-3} There the arguments of ζ and ζ₁ are ratios to dist(·, Λ₀) ≥ 1/2 of 1-Lipschitz functions, bounded by 2 where ψ_f ≠ 0, and at most C(d) faces meet Q_{L/8}(x). That section is orthogonal to f's plane and within R′ of x, so the two would meet within √2(1 + 2c(d))R′ < 6√dR′ of x, in a stratum. In the overlaps of the sectors dist(·, Λ₀) is comparable to r, abs(F_f) ≤ C(d)θ_B/r, and abs(E_f − E_{f₀}) ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)θ_B. So abs(ℓ_E(T)) ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)³Σ_yS_y‖dT‖_{y⁺}, with S_y ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^{1/2}L^{d/2−1}θ_B per block y of side L, S_y² being the sum of θ_B²/min(max(r, 1), L)² over the free sites of the block within L/16 of Λ₀, near which lie C(d) strata of size L^{d−2}, the cap at L covering the terms with ∇χ_d, of size ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)θ_B/L, in the shell L/32 ≤ dist(·, Λ₀) ≤ L/16.     {#A.11.7} {#K0.c} (c) The coarse data and the gauge.

    {#A.11.8} *The two-layer problem 𝒫₁.* Let {#D.Ω₂} Ω₂ := ∪_{j≥2}B^j(Λ_j) (PRT2 (2.4)), and let 𝒞₁ ⊂ 𝒞 be cut out by the further constraints Q₁A = Q₁A_N on the scale-1 bonds with an endpoint in Ω₂, the crossing bonds from Λ₁ into Λ₂ included (constrained by no layer at the scale 1, which VAR leaves free: a bond of a plaquette of Λ_j that is not in Λ_j has both endpoints in Λ_{j−1}, VAR p.278 l.39–42, and REG p.81). With Q₁A = B on the other scale-1 bonds of Ω₁ and Q_j = Q^{(j−1)}Q₁ (PBG (3.15), p.393), they fix Q_jA at A_N's values on the bonds of the layers Λ_j, j ≥ 2, and on those read by VAR's coarse crossing constraints at Λ_j/Λ_{j+1}, j ≥ 1, which are constraints on Q_jA ((g)(1)); so these constraints hold on 𝒞₁ and are redundant there. A_N ∈ 𝒞₁, so A_N is least on 𝒞₁. 𝒫₁'s gauge group {λ: λ = 0 on Λ₀, Q′₁λ = 0 on Ω₁} lies in that of the full problem, so A_N is least on its orbit under it; in (c)–(f) N(Q′) denotes this group. 𝒫₁ has the single interface Λ₀/Ω₁; in (c)–(f) ℓ is its local unit, 1 on Λ₀ and L on Ω₁, and {#D.ℓ_ms} ℓ_ms := L^j on Λ_j is that of the full problem, so ℓ ≤ ℓ_ms. Let U be the union of the blocks Ω_c of these bonds c, and {#D.Ã′} Ã′ := 1_UA_N + Σ_c(B′(c) − Q(1_UA_N)(c))β_c over the other block bonds c, with the bumps β_c of #0.1.33.1, supported in the interior of Ω_c, of size 1/ℓ, with Qβ_c = δ_c. E is supported within L/16 of Λ₀ and Λ₁ is ≥ RM wide, so QE = 0 on the bonds with an endpoint in Ω₂, and a has the data Q₁A_N there. Then QÃ′ = B′ on the other block bonds, QÃ′ = Q₁A_N on these bonds, Ã′ = 0 on the data bonds, and per block off the 2L-neighbourhood of U, ‖dÃ′‖_y ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)ℓ^{d/2−1}θ_B and ‖Ã′‖_y ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)ℓ^{d/2}θ_B, in the units of θ; near U, Ã′ is bounded through ℳ of (f).

    {#A.11.9} VAR has no constraints on the bonds of the scale j from Λ_j into Λ_{j+1} (REG p.81, and VAR p.278 l.39–42, where a bond of a plaquette of Λ_j that is not in Λ_j has both endpoints in Λ_{j−1}; #0.1.3), and PRT2 Lemma 2.4's problem has none on the unit bonds from Λ^c into Λ, which are bonds of Λ (p.245; #0.1.31). Let 𝒳 be a choice of one such crossing bond into each layer site, at the scale j one scale-j crossing bond into each sub-block y′ ⊂ Λ_{j+1} joined to Λ_j. Every class of ker Q modulo ∂N(Q′) has representatives vanishing on 𝒳 (Q_j vanishing there at the scale j): a λ ∈ N(Q′) with the prescribed means Q′_jλ(y′) at the endpoints of 𝒳, its block means restored by bumps in the other sub-blocks, removes the 𝒳-values. The problem for a − Ã′ ∈ ker Q is gauge-invariant: its class minimises {#D.Φ(D)} Φ(D) := ‖dD‖² + 2Re(ℓ_E(D) + ⟨dÃ′, dD⟩) on ker Q modulo ∂N(Q′), and ⟨dD, dT⟩ = −ℓ_E(T) − ⟨dÃ′, dT⟩ for every T ∈ ker Q and every representative D. No gauge-fixing term is used. For a weight g > 0, the g-Landau representative of a class is the one with ‖gℓ^{−1}D‖ least on D + ∂N(Q′), ℓ on a bond being the larger of its endpoints' values.

    {#A.11.10} {#K0.d} (d) The gap in local units. The claim is ‖ℓ^{−1}D₁‖ ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)‖dD‖ for the 1-Landau representative D₁ of every class, for L ≥ 128 (#0.1.37). Let D ∈ ker Q vanish on 𝒳. Its values on the other crossing bonds are of two kinds.

    {#A.11.11} (α) Where the two endpoints in the finer layer are joined by a path of length ≤ C(d) of constrained bonds (data bonds of Λ₀; at the scale j, scale-j bonds of Λ_j), the value differs from that on the bond of 𝒳 by a sum of dD over C(d) plaquettes. At the scale j it is a sum of averages of dD over squares of side L^j, the lines of the four averages of a scale-j plaquette being paired by translation.

    {#A.11.12} (β) At a contact of codimension 2 between two distinct local components K₁, K₂ of Λ₀ (#0.1, *Bałaban's problem.*), a corner site x′ has crossing bonds b₁ ∈ 𝒳 to K₁ and b₂ to K₂, and the jump {#D.J(x′)} J(x′) := D(b₂) − D(b₁), which is D(b₂) since D(b₁) = 0, is gauge-invariant. It is bounded through the coarse crossing constraints. In the cross-section of the contact, the blocks of side L about it are Y₁ ⊂ K₁, y ⊂ Λ₁, Y₂ ⊂ K₂, and a fourth, and y shares a face with Y₁ and with Y₂, say Y₁ = y + Le₁ and Y₂ = y − Le₂. Their coarse crossing averages are QD(Y₁, y) = avg_{x∈Y₁}D([x, x − Le₁]) and QD(Y₂, y) = avg_{x₂∈Y₂}D([x₂, x₂ + Le₂]) (on the coarse crossing bonds Q′_{j+1} is a mean of scale-j means, PBG (3.15), (3.19), p.393), and both vanish. Pair {#D.x₂.2} x₂ := x − Le₁ − Le₂, so that both lines end at {#D.w.3} w := x − Le₁. The loop x → w → x₂ → x′ → x, closed through straight paths in K₂ and in K₁ and through b₂ and b₁, has D = 0 on its data bonds. So its integral is the difference of the two line integrals plus ±J(x′), and it equals the sum of dD over the cone Σ(x) from x′ over the loop, of area ≤ C(d)L². Averaging over x ∈ Y₁ gives J(x′) = ±avg_xΣ_{p∈Σ(x)}dD(p). A plaquette at distance ρ from x′ lies in Σ(x) for at most C(d)L^dmax(ρ, 1)^{2−d} of the x, so abs(J(x′)) ≤ C(d)Σ_{p∈Q_{CL}(x′)}abs(dD(p))max(ρ(p), 1)^{2−d} ≤ C(d)(1 + log L)^{1/2}‖dD‖_{Q_{CL}(x′)} for d = 4. At the scale j the same holds in (g)(2) for the differences of V. The field e. It is built from the blocks of side L of Λ₀. For a free site x within L/8 of Λ₀ let {#D.m(x)} m(x) := max(dist(x, Λ₀), 1).

    {#A.11.13} For a block Y of Λ₀ within C(d)m(x) of x let c_Y(x) be the point of Y nearest x, moved by m(x)/4 towards the centre of Y, and B_Y(x) the ball of radius m(x)/8 about it, which lies in Y for d ≤ 4, its centre being at distance ≥ m(x)/(4√d) from the faces of Y.
